title: Portfolio Operating Executive (REMOTE)
description:
We are seeking a Portfolio Operating Executive (REMOTE) for a full time and direct hire role for one of our amazing Private Equity partners. You will work remotely but will be required to travel to meet with clients at times. Must live in the Eastern or Central time zone with ready access to commercial air travel.


Overview:

You will work for a middle-market private equity firm that specializes in investing in founder-led and family-owned businesses across a range of stages, including control (majority ownership) and non-control investments in businesses. This role is working with one of their control funds portfolio companies, and these companies are typically small and successful companies that have enormous potential to scale. They typically have a $5-$40 million target revenue and $1-$4 million target EBITDA, and they span across sectors such as business services, consumer products, healthcare, niche manufacturing, and value-added distribution.


This role is a director level Operating Executive, and you will act as the quarterback for onboarding and integration of new portfolio company investments. You will work closely with deal teams, portfolio company management, and other members of the portfolio services group, ensuring smooth transitions, early value creation, and long-term scalability. You will coordinate across finance, HR, technology, and operations to ensure successful execution of their framework and drive alignment with founders and management teams. The role includes coordination, integration leadership, and interpersonal effectiveness more than hands-on technical execution.


Responsibilities:

  • Drive successful onboarding and integration, foster strong relationships, provide strategic business and operational leadership, develop and lead high-impact teams and enhance value creation opportunities.
  • Oversee onboarding across multiple portfolio companies within the control investments fund.
  • Lead post-merger integration efforts across finance, IT, HR, and commercial functions.
  • Develop and implement integration playbooks, synergy tracking, and reporting processes.
  • Support add-on integrations and platform investment onboarding.
  • Build trust and credibility with founders, boards, and portfolio company leadership.
  • Represent the PE firm on founder calls with strong professional manner and confidence.
  • Serve as a partner who inspires confidence in both sponsors and operators.
  • Maintain oversight of financial, HR, and systems-related initiatives in coordination with subject matter experts.
  • Support FP&A activities including cash flow forecasting, budgeting, and debt covenant tracking.
  • Identify, prioritize, and communicate operational risks and growth opportunities.
  • Collaborate with and oversee interim finance and operations resources.
  • Partner with portfolio leadership in selecting and onboarding permanent hires.
  • Provide structured leadership to cross-functional teams to ensure accountability and delivery.
  • Lead operational transformation projects aimed at EBITDA improvement and growth.
  • Implement structured program management (PMO) to ensure consistent execution.
  • Leverage technology and systems (ERP, CRM, BI tools) to modernize operations and reporting.


Responsibilities through stages of engagement:

  • Pre-LOI:
    • Partner with deal team on operational and financial capability assessments.
    • Identify integration considerations and organization design and talent needs.
  • Due Diligence:
    • Contribute to operational and financial diligence workstreams.
    • Assess infrastructure readiness and preliminary integration plans.
  • First 100 Days:
    • Deploy framework initiatives with founders and management teams.
    • Coordinate onboarding of critical systems (GL, CRM, HR/Payroll).
    • Align stakeholders on integration and growth priorities.
  • First Year:
    • Drive integration of add-ons and realization of synergies.
    • Execute value creation playbooks with measurable EBITDA impact.
    • Establish repeatable processes and dashboards to support long-term success.


Requirements:

  • 7-10 years of experience working with private equity portfolio companies, doing management consulting, or related operating roles.
  • Proven track record leading M&A integrations, synergy realization, and post-close execution.
  • Strong foundation in finance (FP&A, accounting, capital structures) with ability to engage confidently, even though its not required to operate as a CFO.
  • Demonstrated experience driving operational transformation and EBITDA improvement.
  • Background in program management (PMO) with experience designing and executing playbooks.
  • Broad business acumen across finance, HR, technology, and operations.
  • Tech-savvy, with exposure to ERP, CRM, and BI tools.
  • Hands-on and structured leader with the ability to coordinate cross-functional teams.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to prioritize dynamically across multiple companies.
  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills with a strong professional manner to speak with founders, boards, and executives.
  • Professional, resilient, and adept at navigating ambiguity.
  • Degree in Finance, Business, or related field. An MBA, CPA, or CFA is a plus.
  • Preferably living in the Eastern or Central time zone with easy access to commercial air travel.


All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, age, ancestry, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, disability, medical condition, genetic information, pregnancy, or military or veteran status. You must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship.

title: Associate Advisor
description:
About Allworth Financial

Allworth Financial (www.allworthfinancial.com) is an independent investment advisory firm providing full-context wealth planning solutions. The firm brings together investment, tax, retirement, estate, and other financial considerations to help clients evaluate decisions in the context of their whole financial lives.

Founded in Sacramento, California, in 1993, Allworth Financial is a high-growth, private equity-backed, multibranch registered investment adviser. Allworth is primarily a fee-based fiduciary advisory firm that emphasizes client well-being and education. The firm continues to expand through acquisitions and organic growth.

Allworth is a great place to work and build a career. The firm ranks among the top 15 on Barron’s Top 100 RIA Firms list, has a historical client retention rate of 97%, and is a National Business Research Institute (NBRI) Circle of Excellence Award winner. Learn more at AllworthFinancial.com.

SUMMARY:

The Associate Advisor plays a key role on our centralized planning team, partnering closely with our Financial Advisors to deliver an exceptional service and advice experience to Allworth’s on-plan asset management clients. This role is designed for individuals who are committed to becoming future lead advisors and who want to build deep technical planning expertise, strengthen client-facing skills, and gain hands-on exposure to the full Allworth operating model.

As an Associate Advisor, you will support the end-to-end planning process — from preparing and refining financial plans, to conducting research and case analysis, to participating in client meetings and follow-up. You will collaborate across departments, develop a strong understanding of our integrated service model, and play an important role in ensuring clients feel informed, cared for, and confident in their financial future.

This is an in-office position with a salary range of $70,000–$72,000 annually, commensurate with experience. The role includes structured professional development and support in pursuing the CFP® designation as part of your long-term career path within Allworth.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Shadows Financial Advisor future and existing client appointments to gain valuable training.
  • Creates and helps implement financial plans for existing clients.
  • Performs various tasks and research relating to casework for our clients.
  • Assists with future and existing client communication
  • Shadows various departments of Allworth Financial to obtain knowledge of how our business model functions.
  • Attends company events, including workshops and seminars.
  • Takes appropriate steps to obtain the CFP® designation.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • BS/BA in Business Finance, Economics, or related field
  • Has obtained their 65, 7/66 or ChFC
  • In pursuit of CFP® designation
  • Self-starter, with the ability to work independently
  • Strong communication, teamwork, and relationship-building skills
  • Demonstrates ability to learn related financial and office programs and systems

BENEFITS

We value our associates’ time and effort. Our commitment to your success is enhanced by our competitive base pay and an extensive benefits package, including:

  • Medical: Blue Shield (PPOs and HDHP with HSA) plans and Kaiser (HMO) plans for California associates
  • Dental insurance with MetLife
  • Vision insurance with VSP
  • Optional supplemental benefits
  • Healthcare savings accounts with company contribution
  • Flexible spending accounts
  • Flexible working arrangements
  • Generous 401K contributions
  • Exempt associates qualify for our flexible paid time off policy
  • Non-Exempt associates will receive 15 days of paid time off annually during the first three years of employment
  • 11 Paid Holidays
  • Option to participate in our Equity Purchase Program (Contract, intern, and part-time employees are not eligible)
  • Future growth opportunities within the company

In addition, we work to maintain the best possible environment for our associates, where people can learn and grow with the firm. We strive to provide a collaborative, creative environment where each person feels encouraged to contribute to our processes, decisions, planning and culture.

Benefits are available to full-time associates who work more than 30 hours a week.

Typical reporting relationships are described, but actual relationships may vary in some instances. This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, skills, or knowledge required of personnel classified in this job.

title: Professional Learning Specialist - Mathematics
description:
The Curriculum & Instruction (C&I) Department works to ensure outstanding instruction in every classroom. Sustainable implementation of high-quality curriculum is the most critical driver of that aim and supports the growth of teachers, administrators, counselors, and librarians at various stages throughout their careers. We aspire to ground our C&I work in a set of shared elements. We start with an understanding of how students learn; we organize around adult learning principles to support teachers and school leaders; we embed opportunities to modify curriculum materials for specific classroom contexts or student needs; and we organize everything around continuous improvement to get better over time.

Position Summary

The Professional Learning Specialist is responsible for providing professional learning for schools receiving mathematics implementation support through NYC Solves. The ideal candidate will be able to make sense of competing and rapidly changing priorities in teaching and learning at NYC Public Schools -- through collaboration with both New Visions staff and external stakeholders -- and leverage a shared set of resources and approaches to provide support that meets the needs of individual stakeholders in alignment with our collective goals and priorities. This is not a supervisory position.

The Professional Learning Development Specialist role involves the following major bodies of work:

  • Collaborate with the C&I math team to implement curriculum-based professional learning opportunities -- including school visits with classroom support (for example demo teaching, side by side coaching, coteaching, instructional planning, etc.), data dives that support teachers with HQIM implementation; and facilitating workshop sessions within or across schools
  • Utilize key data from NV staff, school staff, and district stakeholders to refine an understanding of Illustrative Mathematics curriculum in relation to school PL and coaching needs
  • Work in alignment with district and citywide leaders in NYC Public Schools to support key instructional goals and priorities through HQIM implementation
  • Stay informed of shifts in the field (including NY State Standards, Regents, and national standards) and ensure ongoing support for instructional leaders and teachers aligns with these shifts.

This role requires deep and consistent collaboration with members of the Curriculum team, as well as New Visions' school-facing staff. The person in this role must develop a deep understanding of the curriculum they are coaching, engage in ongoing team learning, and participate in other departmental and organizational activities. It also requires them to have a thoughtful and continuous exchange of ideas with stakeholders at all levels of the system.

Core Duties and Responsibilities

  • Understanding HQIM for Student Success: Collaborate with New Visions staff, teacher leaders, and other stakeholders to gain an understanding of how HQIM curriculum supports student mastery through the incorporation of instructional and language routines, embeds scaffolds and differentiations to support all learners, and promotes student success on the Regents exam (when applicable) and in future classes.
  • Professional Learning: Facilitate professional learning experiences in alignment with instructional goals and priorities of district and citywide leaders in NYC Public Schools for HQIM implementation. Engage in a shared coaching model to collaborate with school staff to set goals and develop instructional plans, provide school based coaching in support of curriculum implementation; and facilitate regular reflection on progress and challenges.
  • Evaluation and Improvement: Work with different forms of data relevant to school stakeholders, including surveys, interim assessments, classroom data, student work, and other relevant data to inform instructional decisions. Analyze data to identify trends and report on findings to various stakeholders. Use evaluation findings to make data-driven decisions to inform support.
  • Capacity Building and Collaboration: Build trust and strong relationships with teachers, school leaders, and district leaders to ensure effective communication and collaboration. Exhibit humility and empathy, recognizing the value of all contributions to the system.
  • Strategic Alignment & Ownership: Use shared goals, resources, and frameworks to ensure individual decisions align with our collective priorities. Proactively communicate timely updates regarding team priorities and tasks, and consistently model self-reflection and personal accountability in all our work.

Required Education and Experience

  • Masters-level degree
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in public education, preferably in urban schools and at the secondary level
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience supervising, coaching, or leading teachers at a school site
  • Prior simultaneous cross school experience is not required.
  • Prior school and district leadership is not required.

Required Skill Sets and Knowledge Base

  • Working knowledge of the role of high-quality instructional materials in systems change
  • Completion of IM Math Coaching workshop series (which may be completed after accepting this position)
  • Demonstrated ability to support teachers in modifying curriculum materials for students with a variety of learning needs that maintain integrity of the instructional model
  • Experience leading a team and collaborating with others, using data to drive organizational change
  • Demonstrated commitment to data-driven decision-making, systems thinking and continuous adult learning as drivers of improved student outcomes
  • Skills related to the design, implementation, and assessment of effective secondary curricula
  • Strong service and support orientation towards schools and school communities
  • Strong interpersonal skills to navigate the diverse cultural environments of a wide range of public high schools, and ability to work effectively with a wide range of school and district leaders and staff
  • Ability to work effectively as a member of a team
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to travel onsite to NYC public schools across the 5 boroughs, multiple days per week, typically in 6-hour daily increments
  • Ability to traverse a school environment, including accessing multiple floors, to attend meetings and facilitate learning activities
  • Ability to traverse an office environment to attend meetings and interact with colleagues
  • Ability to operate a computer and other relevant technology, such as phones, screens, printers, and tablets
  • Ability to carry up to 10 pounds (such as for a laptop and carrying case)

The ideal candidate must be able to complete all physical requirements of the job with or without a reasonable accommodation.

Job Status

  • Full-time, temporary position through June 2027, with possibility of part-time employment in the Fall
  • Offers are contingent on receiving fingerprint background check clearance by the NYCPS and completion of New Visions HR onboarding

Disclaimer:

The statements herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by the employee in this position. These statements are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of a person in this position.

Salary Information
While the majority of new hires’ starting salaries shall be expected to be placed in the first half of the range(s) to allow space to grow in the job, for those who already have significant relevant experience at that level of the job, placement at the higher end of the range(s) is possible.
Pay Range
$82,617—$132,187 USD

Who We Are

For over three decades, New Visions for Public Schools has played a central role in improving the quality of New York City public schools and removing barriers to the success of low-income students and students of color. We provide educators with the tools, resources, and supports to build and continuously improve strong and responsive systems—through investments in curriculum, technology, student planning tools, and innovative college and career preparatory programs.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

New Visions believes that our teams are most effective when they include representation from the diverse communities we serve, as their perspectives are critical to the work we do. Diversity, equity, and inclusion do not determine who gets hired—that is based on qualifications. They ensure that people who have traditionally had less access to opportunities are considered and, once chosen, feel supported and valued as part of our team.

New Visions provides a comprehensive and competitive compensation and benefits package in addition to the opportunity to make a significant impact on education reform and in the lives of urban youth.

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
Job Title: Senior Data Engineer

Location: Washinton DC

Summary

The Senior Data Engineer / Databricks Specialist will support a federal project by developing, designing , and optimizing high-performance Spark applications and enterprise data infrastructure in AWS Databricks. The role focuses on scalable ETL/ELT pipelines using Python, PySpark, SQL, and Delta Lake; Medallion Architecture; and secure, reliable data solutions for mission-critical environments.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and optimize scalable Spark applications in AWS Databricks using Python, PySpark, and SQL.
  • Design, build, and maintain ETL/ELT pipelines using Medallion Architecture (Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers), ensuring data integrity, completeness, and lineage.
  • Administer Databricks workspaces, clusters, scheduled jobs, access controls, Unity Catalog, and notebooks.

  • At least 3 years of dedicated, hands-on Databricks development experience.
  • Production experience with PySpark, Apache Spark, Spark SQL, and Delta Lake.

  • Strong hands-on experience with AWS S3, IAM, Lambda, Glue, and Aurora.

Preferred Qualifications

title: Sr Software Engineer
description:

The work you do with our team supports better health outcomes by connecting people to the pharmacy benefits, medications, and services they need to feel their best. Join us to start Caring.   • Design, develop, and deploy AI-powered solutions to address complex business challenges with emphasis on responsible use of AI

You'll be rewarded and recognized for your performance in an environment that will challenge you and give you clear directions on what it takes to succeed in your role as well as provide development for other roles you may be interested in.

Required Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience in full-stack web application development using JavaScript and Node.js
  • 5+ years of hands-on experience with building, deploying, and maintaining cloud applications. (Eg, AWS, GCP, Azure)
  • 3+ years of experience designing, building, and integrating RESTful APIs and microservices
  • 2+ years of experience with CI/CD tools, automated testing frameworks, and modern build pipelines

  • Experience with containerization and orchestration platforms (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes, AWS ECS/EKS)
  • Familiarity with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools such as Terraform, AWS CloudFormation, or AWS CDK
  • Experience working within an Agile/Scrum software development lifecycle
  • Pharmacy benefits management (PBM) or healthcare industry domain experience
  • Software engineering experience in full-stack web application development using React, Lambda, MySQL
  • Experience working on Mac OS based development tools and workflow
  • Experience with pharmacy, EHR, and healthcare system integrations is a plus

description:
The Executive Director – Debt Capital Markets Origination is responsible for leading Inland’s debt capital origination mandate within the Investments Department. This role will develop and maintain external lender relationships, source competitive financing alternatives, lead market execution for new acquisition financing, and support strategic growth initiatives across the company’s investment platforms. The position is designed to create dedicated coverage for new financing activity while partnering closely with the CIO, broader Investments Department, and applicable Portfolio Managers to ensure the financing strategy is aligned with investment objectives, transaction timelines, portfolio considerations, and company-wide capital formation priorities.
CORE RESPONSIBILITIES:

Lead debt capital markets origination for acquisition financing, development financing, structured debt, and other financing opportunities across Inland’s investment platform.
Develop, expand, and manage external lender relationships, including banks, life insurance companies, debt funds, agencies, CMBS lenders, private credit providers, and other capital sources.
Lead competitive lender marketing processes to improve pricing discovery, financing terms, execution certainty, and strategic optionality.
Partner with the Investments Department and Portfolio Managers to evaluate financing feasibility, capital structure alternatives, and transaction-level debt assumptions.
Prepare financing recommendations, lender comparisons, term sheet analyses, and transaction summaries for internal review, investment committee consideration, and executive decision-making.
Lead negotiations of term sheets, financing proposals, commitment letters, and key business terms in coordination with internal stakeholders, outside counsel, lenders, borrowers, sponsors, and transaction counterparties.
Coordinate with the Debt Transaction Manager to advance financing execution from lender selection through closing, including diligence coordination, documentation, approvals, and closing logistics.
Co-lead broader refinancing activities with the Director – Debt Portfolio & Treasury when transactions require market outreach, competitive bidding, or new lender execution beyond an incumbent lender.
Maintain current knowledge of debt capital markets conditions, lender appetite, credit spreads, leverage levels, underwriting standards, covenant structures, and asset-class-specific financing trends.
Support strategic growth initiatives by identifying financing products, capital sources, relationship opportunities, and execution strategies that enhance Inland’s investment and capital formation capabilities.
Promote a disciplined, accountable, and scalable debt origination process with clear ownership, consistent communication, institutional-quality execution, and strong cross-functional coordination.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY:
This position provides functional leadership, day-to-day direction, and transaction oversight to the Debt Transaction Manager and any future team members assigned to support debt origination activity. The role is responsible for establishing execution priorities, coordinating workloads, developing process discipline, and supporting team member development within the Debt Capital Markets Origination function.
QUALIFICATIONS:
Education:

Bachelor’s degree in finance, real estate, accounting, economics, business administration, or a related field required. Advanced degree, MBA, CFA, or other relevant financial industry certification preferred.

Experience:

Minimum of 10 years of relevant experience in commercial real estate finance, debt capital markets, lending, investment banking, mortgage banking, private credit, institutional real estate investment, or a related field. Demonstrated experience sourcing, structuring, negotiating, and closing commercial real estate debt transactions across multiple asset classes and lender types is required. Experience working with acquisition teams, investment committees, portfolio management, asset management, legal counsel, and external capital providers is strongly preferred.

Certifications/Licenses:

None required.

Skills:

Strong knowledge of commercial real estate debt markets, lender landscape, transaction structures, pricing conventions, credit standards, and documentation processes.
Demonstrated ability to build, maintain, and leverage lender relationships across banks, life insurance companies, debt funds, agencies, CMBS lenders, private credit providers, and other capital sources.
Excellent analytical skills, including the ability to evaluate financing alternatives, compare term sheets, assess risk-adjusted execution outcomes, and communicate recommendations clearly.
Strong negotiation skills and sound business judgment when evaluating transaction terms, lender proposals, execution risks, and strategic alternatives.
Executive presence and stakeholder influence, including the ability to prepare executive-level materials, present recommendations to senior leadership, and represent Inland professionally with external capital providers.
Strong transaction management capabilities, including attention to detail, accountability for deadlines, and ability to coordinate multiple internal and external parties.
Collaborative orientation with the ability to partner effectively across departments and align financing strategy with investment, portfolio, legal, and capital formation objectives.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, financial models, lender comparison tools, and transaction management processes.

WORKING CONDITIONS/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
Working Conditions:

Professional office environment.
Frequent interaction with internal and external business partners.
Travel is expected and may include lender meetings, industry events, and other business development activities, generally estimated at 10% or more.
Ability to work additional hours as necessary to support transaction deadlines.

title: Vice President, Project Development
description:
Overview
Tract Capital adopts a unique approach to digital infrastructure investment. Leveraging experience and strategic insights honed over three decades of creating successful companies in the space, we excel in nurturing and advancing leading-edge digital infrastructure enterprises. Our team of specialized experts are united by a singular purpose: to support the growth of digital infrastructure. Tract Capital goes beyond simple investment by acting as a strategic partner and catalyst for innovation within the sector. We ensure our engagements not only generate strong financial results but also develop essential digital infrastructure to meet growing demands. Tract Capital has introduced multiple digital infrastructure strategies including horizontal powered land, vertical development, and product development.

Position Overview

The position is a high-impact, execution-oriented role within Tract Capital's Project Development team, a subset of the Investments & Strategy team that holds end-to-end responsibility for Tract Capital's data center assets. The Vice President will be a core execution member of this team, driving active progress across large-scale data center development projects throughout their full lifecycle, from site acquisition or joint venture through master planning, entitlements, permitting, leasing, development, power, construction, equipment procurement, financing, and ultimately the disposition of those assets. Data center development is inherently multidisciplinary; the Vice President operates as a critical regional leader and coordinator across all of its key workstreams, ensuring each advances on schedule and in alignment with the broader project. The Vice President works closely alongside senior members of the organization, operates with direct visibility into firm-level investment decisions, and engages a broad network of internal functions and external project partners.

Job Responsibilities
The successful candidate will be responsible for the following key areas:

  • Lead full-lifecycle data center development workstreams, from site acquisition or joint venture through master planning, entitlements, permitting, leasing, development, power, construction, equipment procurement, financing, and asset disposition, tracking critical-path milestones, surfacing issues early, and driving resolution across internal and external stakeholders
  • Serve as a critical execution member of the permitting team across federal, state, and local jurisdictions; monitor permit timelines, coordinate with permitting consultants and internal stakeholders, and ensure open items are actively moving forward
  • Support power and energy infrastructure workstreams, including utility interconnection, behind-the-meter power solutions, and battery energy storage systems, coordinating with internal power teams, external consultants, and utility counterparties to monitor progress, flag risks, and keep deliverables aligned with the data center development schedule
  • Actively lead the structuring and execution of project-level financing, preparing diligence materials, excel models, tracking and responding to lender requests, and coordinating inputs across internal and external parties
  • Participate in the procurement of long-lead data center equipment in coordination with the procurement lead
  • Critically evaluate deliverables from engineers, consultants, legal counsel, investors, and contractors; identify gaps, escalate issues, and work across teams to hold parties accountable to scope, schedule, and cost
  • Prepare and maintain integrated project risk registers, development schedules, budgets, and executive-level project status reports
  • Assist in drafting, reviewing, and negotiating project agreements (including site control documents, construction contracts, power contracts, engineering and consultant contracts, equipment procurement agreements, and utility interconnection agreements) in coordination with internal legal and outside counsel
  • Support assessment of project-level legal and regulatory risk across jurisdictions, coordinating with outside counsel and internal legal on deal structuring and contract terms
  • Serve as a central coordination point across internal functions (investments, legal, capital markets, engineering, procurement, leasing, and construction) and the full roster of external project partners, ensuring alignment and preventing workstream drift
  • Support investment committee processes, including financial models, project narratives, and transaction diligence materials

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree (JD, MBA, or MSRE/MSRED) strongly preferred.
  • 4-6 years of direct, hands-on experience in data center, energy, infrastructure, or industrial development, with demonstrated exposure to complex, multi-stakeholder project environments. Attorneys with relevant experience at a top-tier firm or developer are encouraged to apply.
  • This position requires the ability and willingness to travel to project sites, major stakeholder meetings, and Tract Capital offices.

Core Skills & Competencies

  • Working knowledge of real estate development fundamentals, including real property ownership structures, land use frameworks, and entitlement processes applicable to large-scale infrastructure or commercial development
  • Working knowledge of project capital structures, including debt, equity, and construction financing dynamics applicable to large-scale infrastructure or real estate development
  • Familiarity with federal, state, and local permitting pathways for large-scale development projects; ability to engage substantively with permitting consultants, track regulatory timelines, and identify risks across multi-jurisdictional processes
  • Working knowledge of power and energy infrastructure as it relates to data center development — including utility interconnection, behind-the-meter power solutions, and battery energy storage systems — sufficient to engage constructively with power consultants, utility counterparties, and turnkey power providers, and monitor deliverables against project schedule
  • Ability to critically evaluate engineering and legal deliverables, identify gaps, and escalate or drive resolution — without waiting to be directed
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate across external consultants, contractors, and counsel, advancing workstreams toward defined milestones without serving as the primary functional owner of each discipline

Location: Morristown, NJ

Travel Requirement: This position requires the ability and willingness to travel to project sites, major stakeholder meetings, and Tract Capital offices.

Expected Salary Range: $250,000 - $300,000 Base Salary + Discretionary Bonus

Tract Capital Employment

Tract Capital employees enjoy competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits, including 100% employer-covered medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401K program, standard paid holidays, and unlimited PTO.

NOTE: This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employees may perform other related duties to meet the organization’s ongoing needs.

About Care Access

Care Access is working to make the future of health better for all. With hundreds of research locations, mobile clinics, and clinicians across the globe, we bring world-class research and health services directly to communities that often face barriers to care. We are dedicated to ensuring that every person has the opportunity to understand their health, access the care they need, and contribute to the medical breakthroughs of tomorrow.

With programs like Future of Medicine, which makes advanced health screenings and research opportunities accessible to communities worldwide, and Difference Makers, which supports local leaders to expand their community health and wellbeing efforts, we put people at the heart of medical progress. Through partnerships, technology, and perseverance, we are reimagining how clinical research and health services reach the world. Together, we are building a future of health that is better and more accessible for all.

To learn more about Care Access, visit .

How This Role Makes a Difference

As the Director of Engineering, you are someone who deeply cares about your team and the success of those around you. You are an experienced leader and manager with a strong background in SaaS-based product organizations, and you were once a developer yourself. You can hold your own in technical conversations without needing to write software daily. You take a servant-leadership approach to management, waking up every day to elevate your team and organization. You shine as a collaborator, are an impeccable communicator, and bring an energetic passion for learning and applying new technical paradigms.

In clinical trials, research site staff spend countless hours on manual, repetitive administrative tasks—chasing phone calls, answering basic questions, coordinating schedules, and running routine prescreening surveys.

You will lead the engineering organization building our AI Patient Engagement Agent—one of our newest and most transformative product initiatives. This team is engineering an intelligent, voice- and messaging-capable AI agent designed to handle standardized patient interactions, drive recruitment, manage appointments, and automate prescreening outreach at global scale.

The mission of this team is to eliminate operational friction and give hours back to clinical research staff so they can focus on high-value human care and medical decisions.

Please note that this position is hybrid role from the following location only: Boston, MA

This role requires one day per week in the Boston office.

How You'll Make An Impact

  • Configurable Conversational Workflows: Building dynamic, script-driven conversation engines that can be customized across diverse clinical trials and tailored to distinct patient needs while guiding users toward interaction goals.
  • Intelligent Logistics & Orchestration Engine: Engineering a resilient task engine that balances multi-factor variables—patient “safe-call” windows, local time zones, call-center operational hours, outcome tracking, and adaptive retry policies to maximize reach while maintaining strict best practices.
  • Delivery & Roadmap Execution: Own the execution of the AI Patient Engagement engineering roadmap. Partner with Product and Design to translate complex trial protocols into intuitive AI interaction workflows and deliver reliable, high-impact software.
  • Hands-on Architectural Guidance: Participate in architectural design reviews for real-time voice, messaging, workflow orchestration, and data pipeline engines. Ensure the team builds a resilient, highly available platform that scales without taking on technical debt.
  • Sprint & Capacity Management: Balance feature delivery with platform stability, managing team capacity, resource allocation, and technical debt to keep patient outreach timelines on track.
  • Agile Process Optimization: Refine agile ceremonies and continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) practices for your team. Eliminate operational roadblocks to foster a high-velocity shipping cadence.
  • Line Management & Mentorship: Directly manage, mentor, and grow Engineering Managers and Tech Leads. Conduct regular 1-on-1s, build career growth trajectories, and recruit top engineering talent to expand the team.
  • Team Health & Culture: Foster an inclusive, high-accountability environment where engineers are empowered, aligned, and motivated by the real-world healthcare impact of their work.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Serve as the technical point of contact across departments. Translate complex AI, telemetry, and platform concepts into clear operational updates for executive leadership and non-technical partners.

The Expertise Required

  • People Leadership: Proven experience as a “manager of managers,” directly leading, coaching, and developing Engineering Managers and Technical Leads.
  • Technical Breadth: Strong background in scalable cloud architecture, event-driven systems, API-first SaaS platforms, or workflow automation engines.
  • Execution Track Record: Demonstrated ability to own and ship complex, data-intensive, or automation-heavy products on time.
  • Operational Expertise: Deep proficiency in Agile/Scrum methodologies, sprint planning, and modern CI/CD practices.
  • Architectural Oversight: Active engagement in technical design reviews to guarantee platform durability, security, and scalability.
  • Communication Skills: Exceptional ability to articulate technical strategies, risks, and trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders and leadership.
    • Preferred Qualifications:
      • Experience or strong interest in conversational systems, telephony infrastructure (voice/SMS integrations), or AI/automation workflows.
      • Prior experience working within HealthTech, Biotech, Clinical Trials, or Life Sciences (or another highly regulated domain with strict data privacy requirements).

Certifications/Licenses, Education, and Experience

  • Minimum Education
    • BA or BS degree from college or university.
  • Minimum Experience
    • 7+ years of software engineering experience, with at least 3+ years successfully managing engineering teams.

How We Work Together

The expected pay range for this role is $180,000 - $230,000 USD per year for full time team members.

title: Palveluvastaavia, Pietarsaari (vakituinen 30 h/vko)
description:
Viihdytkö vauhdikkaassa myymäläarjessa ja otat luontevasti vetovastuun tilanteen sitä vaatiessa? Palveluvastaavana olet siellä, missä tapahtuu: asiakkaiden, työkavereiden ja myymälän sujuvan arjen keskellä.

Palveluvastaavana yhdistät käytännön myymälätyön, asiakaspalvelun ja työvuoron operatiivisen johtamisen. Työskentelet aktiivisesti myymäläarjessa, kuten kassalla ja muissa myymälätehtävissä, ja varmistat samalla, että työvuorossa työ sujuu suunnitellusti ja Tokmannin toimintamallien mukaisesti.

Tehtävässäsi vastaat

Vuoron operatiivisesta johtamisesta 💡

  • Vastaat työvuoron kokonaisuudesta silloin, kun myymäläpäällikkö tai apulaismyymäläpäällikkö ei ole paikalla.
  • Johdat vuoron tekemistä sekä jaat ja priorisoit työtehtäviä.
  • Huolehdit resurssien, taukojen ja työmäärän sujuvasta toteutumisesta.
  • Vastaat myymälän avaamiseen ja sulkemiseen liittyvistä tehtävistä.
  • Ratkaiset vuoron aikana eteen tulevia arjen tilanteita ja huolehdit myymälän turvallisuudesta ja toimintavalmiudesta.

Asiakaspalvelusta ja kassatyöstä ⭐

  • Työskentelet monipuolisesti myymälätehtävissä ja palvelet asiakkaita Tokmannin asiakaslupauksen mukaisesti.
  • Varmistat omalta osaltasi sujuvan ja asiakaslähtöisen palvelukokemuksen.
  • Ratkaiset asiakastilanteita ja käsittelet asiakasreklamaatioita työvuorosi aikana.
  • Toimit omalla esimerkilläsi mallina hyvästä palvelusta, myynnistä ja työotteesta.
  • Huolehdit kassatyöskentelyn sujuvuudesta ja asiakasvirran hallinnasta sekä osallistut tarvittaessa itse kassatyöhön.

Myymälän päivittäisestä toiminnasta 👏🏽

  • Koordinoit tavarakuormien purkua ja huolehdit työn sujuvasta etenemisestä.
  • Pidät myymälän palavereita Tokmannin toimintamallien mukaisesti.
  • Huolehdit tavaran vastaanoton ja hyllyttämisen sujuvuudesta työvuorosi aikana.
  • Varmistat myymäläkonseptin ja markkinointiohjeiden mukaisten esillepanojen ja hinnannäyttöjen toteutumisen.
  • Huolehdit myymälän siisteydestä, myymäläkuntoisuudesta, hyllysaatavuudesta ja päivittäisestä hävikin hallinnasta.
  • Hyödynnät Tokmannin järjestelmiä ja toimintamalleja osana päivittäistä työtäsi.

Tiimin ohjaamisesta ❤️

  • Toimit myyjien lähiesihenkilönä omassa työvuorossasi myymäläpäällikön (tai apulaismyymäläpäällikön) poissa ollessa.
  • Ohjaat, neuvot ja tuet myymälähenkilöstöä päivittäisessä työssä.
  • Annat palautetta arjen tilanteissa ja huolehdit yhteisten toimintatapojen noudattamisesta ja yhteistyöstä.
  • Osallistut uusien työntekijöiden perehdyttämiseen.
  • Edistät omalla esimerkilläsi avointa, kannustavaa ja vastuullista työilmapiiriä.

Yhteistyöstä myymälän johdon kanssa 🫱🏽‍🫲🏽

  • Teet tiivistä yhteistyötä myymäläpäällikön kanssa (ja apulaismyymäläpäällikön sekä palveluvastaavien, mikäli myymälässä on nämä roolit)
  • Huolehdit tarvittaessa työvuoron henkilöstöjärjestelyistä yhteistyössä myymälän johdon kanssa.
  • Huolehdit muista työvuoron sujuvuuden kannalta tarpeellisista myymälätehtävistä.

Haemme kahta palveluvastaavaa. Tehtävät ovat vakituisia ja työt alkavat heti sopimuksen mukaan. Viikkotyöaika on 30 h/vko.

Odotamme sinulta

  • Soveltuvaa kaupallista koulutusta tai aiempaa kokemusta vähittäiskaupasta.
  • Hyvää myymälä-, kassa- ja asiakaspalvelutyöskentelyn osaamista.
  • Hyviä valmiuksia erilaisten järjestelmien käyttöön sekä kykyä omaksua nopeasti uusia toimintamalleja.
  • Kykyä johtaa ja ohjata tiimin päivittäistä tekemistä sekä priorisoida tehtäviä muuttuvissa tilanteissa.
  • Hyviä yhteistyö-, vuorovaikutus-, päätöksenteko- ja ongelmanratkaisutaitoja.
  • Itsenäistä, vastuullista ja jämäkkää työotetta sekä rohkeutta tarttua tilanteisiin.
  • Palveluhenkisyyttä sekä kykyä toimia yhteisten ohjeiden ja toimintamallien mukaisesti ja käyttää hyvää pelisilmää erilaisissa asiakastilanteissa.
  • Mahdollisuutta työskennellä myymälän aukioloaikojen mukaisesti eri työvuoroissa.

Myymälätyö on liikkuvaa ja fyysistä. Työpäivään kuuluu muun muassa tuotepakkausten nostamista ja siirtämistä sekä työskentelyä erilaisissa työasennoissa.

Tarjoamme sinulle monipuolisen ja vastuullisen tehtävän, hyvän perehdytyksen sekä mahdollisuuden kehittää osaamistasi myymälätyössä ja tiimin ohjaamisessa. Saat ympärillesi osaavan työyhteisön ja tuen tehtävässä onnistumiseen.

Tarkkailethan sähköpostiasi hakemuksen jättämisen jälkeen ja muistathan kurkata myös roskapostikansion. Joskus rekrytointiviestimme saattavat vahingossa päätyä sinne.

title: PER DIEM - School-Based Therapist
description:
PER DIEM School-Based Therapist - San Leandro, CA Area

Transforming student mental health in schools.

About Effective School Solutions

Effective School Solutions (ESS) is a leading provider of school-based mental health services, serving 6,000+ K–12 students across 12 states.

We deliver the level of clinical care typically found in private practice, out-of-district placements, or higher levels of care directly within public schools- providing a full continuum of clinical programming, professional development, and district consultation.

Position Type: Per Diem

Hourly Rate: $55.00-$62.00/hour

This is a per diem position and is not eligible for benefits. Per diem therapist support ESS on an as-needed basis, including coverage for leave assignments (e.g., medical or maternity leave).

Therapist in this role have flexibility in their level of commitment. They may choose to pick up occasional shifts, work a few days per week on an ongoing basis, or take on a temporary full-time schedule when covering a longer-term leave assignment. Per diem clinicians can accept or decline assignments based on their availability.

This role does not follow a consistent full-time schedule; however, full-time hours may be required on a temporary basis when covering extended leave assignments.

Why This Role Matters

You’ll provide critical mental health support to students who may not otherwise have access to care—helping them succeed academically, build resilience, and thrive.

At ESS, clinicians are trusted partners in shaping supportive school environments.

Responsibilities

Direct Clinical Care & Family Support

  • Provide comprehensive, school-based mental health services, including individual, group, and family therapy, as well as intake, diagnostic, and clinical assessments
  • Partner with families and facilitate parent support programming
  • Conduct risk assessments and crisis intervention, ensuring student safety and coordinating referrals to appropriate levels of care when needed
  • Develop and implement individualized, evidence-based treatment plans that support students’ emotional, behavioral, and academic success

Supervision, Training & Collaboration

  • Oversee the day-to-day clinical operations of the assigned school-based program
  • Serve as the primary clinical point of contact for school partners, providing expert guidance, ensuring alignment on student support strategies, and fostering strong, collaborative relationships.
  • Facilitate weekly consultation sessions to ensure alignment on student goals and documentation standards
  • Collaborate with families, school staff, and interdisciplinary teams to deliver coordinated care, and provide consultation, coaching, and training on mental health and trauma-informed practices
  • Participate in team meetings, supervision, and ongoing professional development

Documentation, Compliance & Professional Expectations

  • Maintain timely, accurate clinical documentation in accordance with regulatory, ethical, and organizational standards
  • Uphold professional standards by maintaining active licensure, ethical practice, reliability, and a strong professional presence
  • Monitor program performance and ensure alignment with ESS clinical and operational standards
  • Support clinician performance through feedback, coaching, and evaluations

Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in Social Work, Counseling, or a related field
  • Active associate number or clinical license (e.g., AMFT, APCC, ACSW or LMFT, LPCC, LCSW) in the state of California
  • 2+ years of experience working with children and/or adolescents with behavioral and emotional needs
  • Experience providing training and coaching to educational professionals and parents/caregivers on student mental health issues.
  • Experience working with schools, families, and community-based services (school-based experience preferred)
  • Demonstrated ability to build and maintain trusting relationships with students, families, and school staff
  • Commitment to delivering high-quality, evidence-based care and advocating for best practices
  • Proven ability to positively influence, motivate, and elevate team members and stakeholders
  • Ability to make confident, sound decisions in ambiguous or evolving situations
  • Proficient in clinical documentation and use of electronic systems (e.g., EMR, Microsoft Office), with the ability to maintain accurate and timely records

Why Clinicians Choose ESS

✔ School-day schedule — No weekends; occasional evening hours as needed to support family engagement
✔ Light summers
✔ Small caseloads
✔ Ongoing clinical support, and free CEUs
✔ Competitive Pay
✔ Clinical leadership at the heart of our company

Make a meaningful impact on student mental health.
Join Effective School Solutions

This role translates business strategy into actionable improvement initiatives, influences decision-making at all levels of the organization, and establishes standards that enable long-term growth, efficiency, and customer value.

title: Program Supervisor
description:
*This is an interim position*

SUMMARY

Position Type: Full-time, non-exempt, hourly supervisor role.
Scope of Role:

Supervises a single program or unit within a program, typically supporting 4-8 individuals in residential settings or 10-15 individuals in periodic, vocational or day programs. Duties are split between the provision of direct support, professional or program activities and supervision.

Key Responsibilities:

Supervise Direct Support Professionals
Oversee the day-to-day operation of the program including delivery of supports, implementation of person-centered plans, health care, advocacy, customer engagement, regulatory compliance and when applicable, oversight of the physical environment.
Generally works 8 to 16 flexible hours per week in a supervisory capacity; and provides direct support for the remaining hours.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform each essential function listed below.
Services and Supports:

Direct Support: Works regularly scheduled shifts as a direct support professional (see DSP position description).
Records: Documents as required; reviews individual records, billing and other program documentation routinely for accuracy and completion on a daily basis; maintains
Program Planning: Assists the Program Director in development of individual program plans; trains and monitors implementation of plans each day across all shifts.
Team Meetings: Attends and assists with routine progress meetings.
Compliance: Assists the Program Director in maintaining licensing compliance for program services and supports; implements Sevita compliance plan; manages individual rights implementation.
Management of Individuals’ Assets: When assigned, assures safety of individual’s funds and property; monitors spending and reconciles individual’s financial accounts monthly.
Incidents: Completes or assists DSPs in documenting incident reports; submits initial incident reports to the Program Director.
Billing and Utilization: Compiles or accumulates census or attendance information; reviews data and attests to accuracy; submits accurate data to the Program Director or appropriate billing authority.

Health Care:

General Health Care: Monitors health of persons being served; documents; communicates with medical professionals as appropriate; implements preventive strategies to limit illness and serious incidents; reviews and monitors documentation across all shifts.
Appointments: When applicable, schedules or assists in scheduling health care appointments; may accompany individuals to appointments; may assist with communication; documents visits; oversees follow through of orders; communicates results as appropriate with families, guardians, case managers, day programs or others.
Medications: When applicable, accurately administers or supports self-administration of medication and documents delivery of medications and treatments; reviews all other medication documentation for accuracy and completeness, daily or weekly as required; reviews medication errors with employees; communicates medication changes and provides training across all shifts; maintains appropriate security of medications and supplies.
Medical Supplies and Equipment: Purchases and maintains medical supplies and equipment in consultation with Program Director; communicates with employees and may assist with training on proper use.
Dietary planning: Develops menus based on diets, preferences, and occasions, and with the exception of some in-home services, purchases or oversees purchasing of food and supplies in accordance with planned menus and individual choice or need; directs and monitors food service, consistent with individual plans.

Stakeholder Relations:

Communications: Maintains productive and professional relations with individuals, families, case managers and other stakeholders.
Customer Service: Implements Sevita Customer Service Standards; trains DSPs in delivery.

Personnel:

Recruitment and Hiring: As needed, assists with recruitment; interviews and hires direct support professionals in consultation with the Area Director and Talent Acquisitions teams.
Employee Scheduling: Populates and maintains schedule to assure that all shifts are covered, and overtime is minimized.
Training: Assists with onboarding and delivers orientation and ongoing training concerning the individuals served, program plans, policies, procedures and physical environment; Verifies training records are accessible in the home and are completed by all staff on the schedule.
Evaluation: Prepares and conducts annual evaluations for Direct Support Professionals, in consultation with the Program Director.
Discipline and Termination: Coaches employees as needed, correcting or directing employee behavior where required; may remove employees in the event of emergency; may recommend and participate in decisions regarding termination; consults with the Program Director on all matters of discipline.
Employee Safety: Responsible for employee safety and workers’ compensation within the program; implements and monitors compliance with safety standards.
Management: May assist with or lead monthly program meetings for direct support professionals; documents monthly meeting agenda and attendance.

Financial Management:

Purchasing: When applicable, purchases food and household supplies; purchases office supplies and minor equipment; reviews and attests company credit card statements and monthly invoices; directs employees as necessary; monitors and attests to cost effective, accurate and applicable spending.
Individuals’ Served Funds Management: Secures and safeguards individuals' served funds locally; uses forms for money/debit card transfers; updates financial ledgers weekly and maintains itemized receipts for purchases on behalf of individuals served
Billing and Utilization: Reviews census, attendance information or other required documentation to assure accurate billing; monitors utilization between authorization and provision of services and supports.
Staffing: Monitors staffing hours for budgetary compliance.

Census Management:

Census Capture: Captures daily census within systems; understands importance of accurate and timely service capture along with required documentation.
Census Performance: Develops basic understanding of census, including how census is measured and census performance for locations; Escalates potential service disruptions
Placements: Supports location preparations required for expected placements (e.g., room & furniture set-up, safety requirements, etc.).

Maintenance:

Vehicles: When applicable, test drives vehicle monthly; inspects vehicle lifts and seatbelts monthly; reports safety concerns immediately to supervisor or maintenance personnel; assures vehicle is washed and cleaned; trains staff in safe vehicle operation and safely transporting individuals; ensures routine maintenance is performed.
Living Environment: When applicable, schedules and monitors daily and seasonal housekeeping; oversees lawn and yard care. Maintains neat, clean and safe environment for individuals served.
Maintenance and Repair: When applicable, makes or arranges for minor repairs; reports to and schedules repairs by maintenance personnel as required; monitors environmental safety; monitors water temperature, refrigerator and freezer temperature, and safety alarms and extinguishers on a monthly basis; replaces furnace filters monthly.
Equipment: Monitors wheelchairs, lifts and other safety equipment; sees that repairs are made promptly and correctly in the event of faulty equipment.

Other:

Performs other duties and activities as required, including backfilling roles under your supervision.
MPA = Mobile Punch Authorized for timekeeping.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

Supervises the Direct Support Professionals.
Manages assigned personnel. Completes performance evaluations, orientation, and training. Makes decisions on employee hires, transfers, promotions, salary changes, discipline, terminations, and similar actions. Resolves employee problems within position responsibilities.

Minimum Knowledge and Skills required for the Job
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or abilities required to perform the job.

Education and Experience:

High School diploma or equivalent
One-year related work experience
Must be 18 years or older.
Working knowledge of computers

Certificates, Licenses, and Registrations:

Current driver's license, car registration and auto insurance if driving on the behalf of the Company or providing transportation to individuals receiving services.
Other licensure(s) or certification(s) where required by regulatory authority.

Work Environment:

Provides and oversees services or supports in residential, vocational, or in-home settings.
The Program Supervisor works at the program location and is generally expected to visit each shift and all employees at least one time per month, including supervising periodic or hourly services.

Physical Requirements:

Heavy work. Exerting up to 100 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 50 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 20 pounds of force constantly to move objects.

title: Design Consultant
description:

title: Senior Product Designer - ShareGate
description:
Company Description

Workleap is a Montreal-based tech company, founded in 2006. We're builders at heart, we make simple products that actually matter to the people who use them. We have two product lines: Workleap Agent, our newest solution built to make every manager more effective, and ShareGate, the world's leading solution for Microsoft 365 migration and governance. More than 15,000 companies worldwide trust us to do exactly that. We're intentional about who joins us. If you're the kind of person who gets excited by a hard problem and wants to help shape what comes next, there's a place for you here.

Your role

Almost every company now runs on Microsoft 365, and almost nobody has it fully under control. Work has to be moved into it and around it, through mergers, acquisitions and reorganizations that touch millions of files and can't afford to lose a single one. And once it's there it sprawls faster than anyone can track, with people sharing things they shouldn't and no clear view of what's actually going on. ShareGate is what IT professionals use to do both jobs. Taking something this complex and this consequential and making it feel simple and trustworthy is what we're here to do.

Your impact:

  • Own a whole product area end-to-end, from framing the problem with your team to shipping the solution customers actually use, and monitoring for learnings after.
  • Design AI-first flows where the product does the real work for customers while they stay fully in control.
  • Turn genuinely complicated situations into something a busy person can understand at a glance and feel confident acting on.
  • Put bold bets in front of real customers early, measure what happens, and let the result change the plan, including when it proves you wrong.
  • Bring AI into your own way of working so you can go from a question to something real and testable in days, and put it in front of customers while it's still rough.
  • Raise the bar for everyone around you through critique, through the standards you hold, and by making your thinking clear enough that the team can carry a decision without you in the room.

Your team

You'll join our design team at ShareGate and partner with a product lead and an engineering lead on every project you own, from first idea to launch. We're hiring across two sides of the product right now: one focused on moving companies into and around Microsoft 365, one focused on keeping it secure and organized once they're there. Both are big, high-stakes problems, and we'll work out together which one fits you best.

We're builders. We care a lot about craft and taste, we expect people to own their work rather than wait to be handed it, and we'd rather take a big swing on what's genuinely best for customers than ship the safe version. AI is part of how we work every day; it helps us move faster and try more ideas, not think less. Work gets shared early and often, feedback is direct, and decisions get made quickly and revisited just as quickly when we learn something new.

The people we design for run IT at their companies. They're experts who get the call when something breaks. Our job is to earn their trust and make complex, high-stakes workflows feel simple.

What you'll bring

  • 6+ years designing complex software for businesses, with shipped work you owned from the first question to the last detail;
  • A systems mind: you design the whole journey and think about what happens next, not one screen at a time;
  • The judgment to make design decisions that are hard to take back: what people see first, what they confirm, what they can reverse;
  • A weekly habit of talking to real customers, and the discipline to let what they actually do change your direction;
  • Design rationale you can defend out loud to designers, engineers, and executives alike: the problem, the options you turned down, the trade-off you made;
  • Real fluency using AI in your own workflow, with the judgment to know where it helps and where it gets in the way;
  • The drive to take your work the last mile yourself: refining and polishing in the real product and pushing those changes straight to production;
  • Comfort working without a clear brief: you name the assumption, pick a direction, and learn in the open;
  • Bonus: experience designing for IT, security, data or any audience where the user is an expert and a wrong move is expensive.

Most of this sounds like you? Apply.

What the job comes with

  • Base salary: $125 000 - $160 000. This range reflects our Canada-wide compensation scale. Final offers may be adjusted based on the candidate's region to align with local market conditions.
  • Annual bonus program.
  • LTIP program, share in Workleap's long-term growth.
  • RRSP + Family health insurance + telemedicine + annual wellness budget.

Assist with light cleaning, laundry, resident rooms, offices, and common areas as needed to support a safe and orderly environment.

Support community standards by maintaining professional appearance, participating in training, and delivering courteous service that promotes positive resident and family experiences.

Experience in a healthcare, hospitality, senior living, or service environment preferred.
CNA certification preferred; Personal Care Assistant (PCA) certificate may be accepted. CNA certification may be required in some states.
Must have and maintain CPR and First Aid certifications.
Must meet applicable state certification and licensure requirements.
General understanding of and concern for the needs of seniors.
Experience or aptitude working with Alzheimer’s disease and memory-impaired residents preferred.
Ability to work well with others and promote a team-oriented environment.
Must be at least 18 years of age; state-specific guidelines may apply.
Must pass required background screening, health screening, and drug-free workplace requirements.
Must have reliable transportation and, where required, a valid driver’s license, an acceptable motor vehicle record, and insurability by the community’s automobile insurance carrier.

You provide compassionate, respectful, and dependable support to residents each day.
You notice changes in resident needs and communicate concerns promptly and professionally.
You follow safety, infection control, residents’ rights, confidentiality, and documentation requirements carefully.
You work well with nurses, supervisors, coworkers, residents, and family members.

title: Assistent Begeleider Gehandicaptenzorg | Leusden
description:
Maak jij met jouw aandacht het verschil in iemands dag?

De dag begin je samen met een bewoner, helpen bij het aankleden, samen koffie- drinken of zorgen voor een gezellige sfeer tijdens het eten. Soms zit goede begeleiding juist in die kleine, vertrouwde momenten.

Als Assistent Begeleider bij Groot Schutterhoef in Leusden ondersteun je ouder wordende mensen met een verstandelijke beperking bij hun dagelijkse leven. Je helpt waar dat nodig is en stimuleert bewoners om zoveel mogelijk zelf te blijven doen.

Hoeveel uur je werkt, bespreken we samen. Ook flexibel werken behoort tot de mogelijkheden.

Jouw werkplek

Groot Schutterhoef is een groene, landelijke woonlocatie in Leusden. Er wonen 40 mensen met een verstandelijke beperking, verdeeld over vier woongroepen van ieder 10 bewoners.

In deze functie werk je met ouder wordende bewoners. Zij hebben begeleiding en ondersteuning nodig bij hun dagelijks leven en lichamelijke verzorging. De één kan nog veel zelf, terwijl de ander meer hulp nodig heeft bij bijvoorbeeld wassen, aankleden, eten of bewegen.

We kijken daarom steeds naar wat iemand nodig heeft én naar wat iemand nog zelf kan. Vertrouwde routines, persoonlijke aandacht en een rustige benadering zijn belangrijk.

Op het terrein is ook eigen dagbesteding. Activiteiten zoals muziek, snoezelen en buiten zijn kunnen onderdeel zijn van de dag. Zo draait jouw werk niet alleen om verzorgen, maar vooral om bijdragen aan een fijne en betekenisvolle dag.

Wat ga je doen?

Als Assistent Begeleider ben je veel in contact met bewoners. Samen met je collega's zorg je ervoor dat zij zich prettig en veilig voelen.

Je:

  • Ondersteunt bij dagelijkse verzorging en ADL;
  • Helpt bij eten, drinken en gezamenlijke momenten;
  • Stimuleert bewoners om te blijven doen wat zij zelf kunnen;
  • Zorgt voor rust, structuur en gezelligheid op de groep;
  • Ondersteunt bij activiteiten die passen bij de bewoners;
  • Helpt bij praktische werkzaamheden op de woongroep;
  • Merkt veranderingen bij bewoners op en bespreekt deze met je collega's.

De ene bewoner heeft vooral praktische hulp nodig, terwijl een ander behoefte heeft aan nabijheid, een praatje of samen iets ondernemen. Juist die afwisseling maakt het werk persoonlijk.

Waarom werken op Groot Schutterhoef?

Je werkt op een groene locatie waar wonen, zorg en dagbesteding dicht bij elkaar liggen. Hierdoor leer je bewoners goed kennen en kun je aansluiten bij wat voor hen belangrijk is.

Je werkt samen met een vast team van collega's en staat er dus niet alleen voor. En omdat we verschillende mogelijkheden hebben, kijken we ook naar wat bij jouw leven past. Wil je een vast aantal uren werken of juist flexibel inzetbaar zijn? Bespreek het met ons.

Wie ben jij?

Je hoeft niet degene te zijn die altijd vooroploopt. Veel belangrijker is dat je geduldig, betrouwbaar en betrokken bent. Je hebt aandacht voor bewoners, steekt graag de handen uit de mouwen en vindt het vanzelfsprekend om iemand te helpen bij de persoonlijke verzorging.

Daarnaast:

  • Heb je een afgeronde mbo-opleiding niveau 2 binnen Zorg & Welzijn, of aanpalend;
  • Heb je affiniteit met ouder wordende mensen met een verstandelijke beperking;
  • Ben je bereid om bewoners te ondersteunen bij ADL en verzorging;
  • Werk je graag samen met collega's;
  • Ben je bereid om onregelmatige diensten en weekenden te werken.

Ervaring binnen de gehandicaptenzorg of ouderenzorg is mooi meegenomen.

Wat bieden wij jou?

  • Een salaris van € 2.384,- tot € 3.276,- bruto per maand (FWG 25) op basis van 36 uur, afhankelijk van jouw ervaring en opleiding;
  • Uren in overleg: samen kijken we wat bij jou en de locatie past;
  • De mogelijkheid om flexibel te werken;
  • Extra toeslagen voor onregelmatige diensten;
  • Trainingen, opleidingen en mogelijkheden om jezelf verder te ontwikkelen;
  • Faciliteiten rondom vitaliteit, coaching en duurzame inzetbaarheid;
  • Een goede pensioenregeling en aantrekkelijke extra's.

Enthousiast?

Wil jij praktisch bezig zijn én met jouw aandacht iets betekenen voor ouder wordende bewoners? Solliciteer dan als Assistent Begeleider bij Groot Schutterhoef in Leusden.

Heb je nog vragen? Neem dan contact op met Cem Canan (Corporate Recruiter bij Philadelphia) op 06 - 27 25 40 36.

SEDE E MODALITÀ DI LAVORO

Cosa Offriamo

  • Ambiente di lavoro dinamico ed orientato alla crescita professionale;
  • Certification Program: il programma formativo di EIES Group pensato per supportare e valorizzare la crescita professionale in un’ottica di miglioramento continuo;

Chi siamo?

Il Gruppo EIES rappresenta l’alleanza strategica di quattro aziende italiane leader nel settore informatico, unite per offrire al mercato una copertura completa, integrata e sinergica.

Composto da Energent, I&M Consulting, Enway e Skienda, il Gruppo è una realtà che eroga consulenza, progettualità e servizi in ambito ICT, fornendo soluzioni ad alto valore aggiunto per i propri clienti. Con sedi a Roma, Napoli e Milano, operiamo in settori come Finance, Insurance, Telco, Energy e Pubblica Amministrazione, collaborando con aziende di primaria importanza ed i principali System Integrator.

Il gruppo è organizzato in practices tematiche afferenti a diverse aree di competenza: Infrastrutture & Security, Application Modernization & Cloud Transformation, Data Science e Artificial Intelligence e Consulting. title: Creative Localization Specialist
description:
Description

Keeper is hiring a detail-oriented Creative Localization Specialist to manage the localization of global creative assets across multiple languages and design platforms. This is a 100% remote position from select locations, with an opportunity to work a hybrid schedule for candidates based in the Chicago, IL metro area.

Keeper’s cybersecurity software is trusted by millions of people and thousands of organizations globally. Keeper is published in 23 languages and is sold in over 150 countries. Join one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity companies and help deliver high-quality creative experiences to a global audience.

About Keeper

Keeper Security is one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity software companies that protects thousands of organizations and millions of people in over 150 countries. Keeper is a pioneer of zero-knowledge and zero-trust security built for any IT environment. Its core offering, KeeperPAM®, is an AI-enabled, cloud-native platform that protects all users, devices and infrastructure from cyber attacks. Recognized for its innovation in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management (PAM), Keeper secures passwords and passkeys, infrastructure secrets, remote connections and endpoints with role-based enforcement policies, least privilege and just-in-time access. Learn why Keeper is trusted by leading organizations to defend against modern adversaries at.

About the Role

As a Creative Localization Specialist, you will adapt existing creative assets into multiple languages and formats while ensuring accuracy, consistency, and adherence to Keeper’s brand and design standards. Reporting to the Director of Localization, you will work closely with the design team and Head of Product Design to manage localization workflows, resolve design challenges, and deliver polished assets across print, digital, and motion formats.

  • Support the localization of digital, print, presentation, video, and other creative materials

  • Collaborate with the Director of Localization, translation team, designers, and other stakeholders to identify and resolve localization challenges
  • Maintain organized asset libraries, file naming conventions, version control, and final deliverables
  • Track project status and communicate updates, risks, and outstanding needs to relevant stakeholders
  • Support continuous improvements to localization processes, templates, and production workflows
  • Participate in special projects for the Localization, Design, and Product Design teams

Requirements

  • 2+ years of experience in creative production, localization, graphic design, or a related field
  • Proficiency in Adobe InDesign and Figma
  • Basic understanding of motion graphics tools, such as Adobe After Effects, Adobe Premiere, or similar platforms
  • Experience working with localization workflows and multilingual design best practices
  • Ability to work accurately with translated content across multiple languages
  • Strong understanding of layout, typography, spacing, formatting, and visual design principles
  • Excellent attention to detail and commitment to quality
  • Strong organizational and project management skills
  • Ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines, and file types simultaneously
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills
  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment
  • Ability to work effectively autonomously and as part of a cross-functional team
  • Bachelor’s degree in Graphic Design, Localization, Marketing, Communications, or a related field preferred

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with localization management platforms or computer-assisted translation tools
  • Familiarity with right-to-left language considerations
  • Knowledge of design-to-code handoff processes
  • Experience working in a SaaS, technology, cybersecurity, or global organization
  • Experience supporting video, motion graphics, or multimedia localization

Benefits

  • Medical, Dental & Vision (Inclusive of domestic partnerships)
  • Employer Paid Life Insurance & Employee/Spouse/Child Supplemental life

title: Clinical Coordinator - Endoscopy
description:
Clinical Coordinators allocate human resources to promote efficient, effective, safe and compassionate nursing care using the unit-based staffing matrix. They are responsible for maintaining safe, compassionate nursing care based on current standards and practice. They promote shared decision-making and professional autonomy by providing input into unit-level decisions and keeping the staff informed at the unit level. They problem solve to prevent a potential crisis, assess, evaluate, and manage unit operational issues and assist the nurse manager by sharing on-call responsibilities. The purpose of this position is to coordinate the completion of all required medicare and insurance documentation .

The Clinical Coordinator provides education and training based on the staff’s needs while making sure that clinical competencies of staff meet standards of practice. They facilitate an atmosphere of interactive management and the development of collegial relationships among nursing personnel and others. Clinical Coordinators serve as a link in continuity of care between nursing personnel and others healthcare disciplines and must have facilitate open communication to support the continuum of care for the patient. The Clinical Coordinator is responsible for (a) education and training of staff based on the specialty area, (b) staffing and scheduling using the matrix, (c) completion of payroll, (d) updating ANSOS on a regular basis, (e) completion of the unit performance improvement plan, (f) assisting in the completion of employee evaluations; and, (f) when needed, serving as a staff nurse. The Clinical Coordinator assures that care is delivered with respect for patient rights and appropriate nursing services.

The Clinical Coordinator is accountable for the unit environment in which clinical nursing is practiced. The Clinical Coordinator creates an environment that is open and respectful, and promotes the sharing of expertise to promote the benefits of health outcomes. The ability of the Clinical Coordinator to enhance the practice of the environment is critical to the recruitment and retention of registered nurses. Clinical Coordinators contribute to the unit processes, day-to-day operations, standards of care, and attainment of goals of the assigned unit. Clinical Coordinators collaborate with the Nurse Manager or Director in planning, innovation, and evaluation of unit activities.
