title: Senior Backend Engineer II - Patient Experience
description:
About Us

At Prenuvo, we are on a mission to flip the paradigm from reactive “sick-care” to proactive health care. Our award-winning whole body scan is fast (under 1 hour), safe (MRI has no ionizing radiation), and non-invasive (no contrast). Our unique integrated stack of optimized hardware, software, and increasingly AI, coupled with the patient-centric experience across our domestic and global clinics, have allowed us to lead the change against “we caught it too late again".

We're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer II to join our Patient Experience team and own the communications platform that keeps patients informed throughout their journey: booking confirmations, appointment reminders, intake nudges, results notifications, and follow-ups across email, SMS, and push. You'll also build on the patient-facing APIs behind our patient dashboard (web) and native mobile apps (iOS and Android).

Our in-house Python communications service converts event bus domain events into patient messaging via Iterable, AWS SES, SMS, and push. Key challenges involve ensuring reliable, exactly-once delivery, respecting consent and preferences, and gracefully handling vendor failures with detailed logging. We seek engineers who thrive on end-to-end system ownership, resilient event-driven architecture, and driving outcomes over tickets.

Our preference is for candidates based in Vancouver, who can accommodate a flexible hybrid arrangement during the initial onboarding period.

This role does not provide visa sponsorship. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Canada at the time of hire and must not require employer sponsorship for a work visa (current or future).

Help reshape the world through proactive healthcare while working with cutting-edge technology and high performing teams with deep expertise - join us to make a difference in people’s lives!

What You’ll Do

  • Own the communications platform: Own the patient communications platform end to end, from design through rollout, including service architecture, on-call standards, and technical roadmap.
  • Develop complex software solutions: Build and maintain scalable backend services using Python, FastAPI, and AWS event-driven services (EventBridge, SQS/SNS, Lambda, ECS) that power patient communications.
  • Deliver reliably: Guarantee reliable, exactly-once message delivery through retries and failures, using idempotency, deduplication, backoff, and dead-letter handling and replay, with a clear status for every message we attempt.
  • Build in consent: Build consent and preference handling into the send path, including channel and category opt-ins, STOP and unsubscribe propagation across systems, quiet hours, and clean separation of transactional and marketing messages.
  • Make sends safe: Build safe tooling for one-off and bulk patient sends (audience preview, test sends, rate limits, kill switches) with least-privilege access to patient data and vendor credentials, so that a production send is always a deliberate, reviewed action.
  • Evolve patient-facing APIs: Design and ship OpenAPI-first endpoints that follow our versioning and backward-compatibility standards for mobile clients we can't force-update, and help migrate consumers off legacy GraphQL.
  • Ensure system reliability: Lead improvements in reliability, observability, and incident response using Datadog. You are accountable for whether a message actually reached the patient, not just whether the code merged.
  • Raise engineering quality: Write comprehensive automated tests for the services you build, and improve the patterns, tooling, and processes that raise quality across teams.
  • Provide technical guidance: Lead design discussions, review technical implementations, and mentor engineers across levels.
  • Influence technical direction: Contribute to architectural decisions and the long-term evolution of the platform, partnering closely with Product, Design, Lifecycle Marketing, Clinical, and other engineering teams.
  • Use AI-assisted development: Use AI coding tools and agentic workflows thoughtfully as part of a structured build, review, and test workflow.

What You’ll Bring

  • 7+ years of backend engineering experience owning production services, ideally in Python (or a similar language such as Ruby, Go, Node.js)
  • Strong experience designing and building REST APIs, including contract design, versioning, and error handling, in a modern backend framework (e.g., FastAPI, Flask, Django, Express, Spring).
  • Hands-on experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, including event-driven systems (EventBridge, SQS/SNS, Lambda, ECS), and modern CI/CD practices.
  • Experience building and maintaining distributed systems and integrating with external APIs and webhooks, including idempotency, retries, rate limits, and partial failure.
  • Deep knowledge of relational databases, particularly PostgreSQL, plus experience with NoSQL (e.g., DynamoDB) and caching (e.g., Redis).
  • Experience implementing authentication and authorization (OAuth2, JWT, service-to-service security).
  • Experience writing comprehensive backend tests (e.g., Pytest) and ensuring strong test coverage.
  • Experience with monitoring and observability tools such as Datadog or similar platforms.
  • Ability to independently lead complex initiatives, make sound technical decisions, and balance short-term delivery with long-term maintainability, including on-call and incident response for what you own.
  • Ability to break down complex projects into components or milestones that other engineers can easily pick up.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity, able to balance speed with quality, and willing to take ownership from design through production.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate across engineering and business teams.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Iterable or a similar customer engagement platform (Braze, Customer.io, Klaviyo, Salesforce Marketing Cloud): event and user-profile APIs, journeys and workflows, message types and channels, and webhook processing.
  • SMS experience at scale: Twilio or similar providers, 10DLC and short codes, opt-in capture and STOP handling, and TCPA and carrier compliance.
  • Push notification experience: APNs and FCM (directly or through a platform), device token lifecycle, and deep linking into mobile apps.
  • Email delivery experience: AWS SES or similar, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, bounce and complaint handling, and suppression lists.
  • Notification orchestration: multi-channel routing, preference centers, frequency capping, and scheduled or reminder-based messaging.
  • GraphQL experience, Backend-for-Frontend patterns, or close partnership with native iOS/Android teams.
  • Familiarity with FHIR or other healthcare data models.
  • Familiarity with Terraform, Docker, and GitHub Actions.
  • Experience working in highly regulated industries, including handling sensitive health data.

Our Values

First: we are Pioneers

  • Transforming healthcare requires divergent thinking, bias for action, disciplined experimentation, and consistent grit and determination to maintain momentum. This journey is as challenging as it is rewarding.

Second: we are Platform-Builders

  • We’re always building foundations that allow us to achieve tomorrow more than we did today. We never lose sight of what’s ahead – in a mindset of ownership and duty to our mission.

Above all: we are Patients

  • We could all be the next person who walks through our very doors, seeking clarity or peace of mind. We are proud of our impact on our patients’ lives, and we won’t stop till everyone can benefit from our work.

What We Offer

  • An avenue to make a positive impact on people's lives and their health

title: Training Specialist
description:
About Crowned Grace International

Crowned Grace International (CGINTL) is a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Woman-

Owned, and ISO 9001:2015-certified federal contracting and professional services firm

headquartered in Lanham, Maryland. We serve the Department of Defense, federal civilian

agencies, and Fortune 1000 clients. Our mission is Accelerating Mission-Ready

Capabilities: we develop the capability of the organizations and people we serve and

modernize the systems and data around them for real and lasting change. At CGINTL,

everyone is a Leader.

Position Overview

CGINTL is seeking an accomplished Training Specialist to provide program, portfolio, real-property, project-analysis, risk, facilitation, and acquisition-support analysis to the BPAM PMO. You will help the PMO report consistently, keep facility data current, and give leadership clear visibility into construction, sustainment, and operational performance across the Border Patrol and Air and Marine portfolio.

This position supports U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) through the Program, Project and Mission Support Services (PPMSS) effort for the Border Patrol and Air & Marine (BPAM) Program Management Office (PMO). The BPAM PMO plans, builds, sustains, and operates the facilities that U.S. Border Patrol (USBP) and Air and Marine Operations (AMO) rely on to carry out their mission.

Training Execution

  • Oversee all training execution for the PMO and monitor compliance with CBP mandatory trainings.
  • Develop trainings as requested by the Government.
  • Guide the certification process for PMO employees, including DHS FAC-COR and FAC-PM.
  • Assist in creating individual development plans and manage the Training SharePoint page.
  • Assist with training-course research and logistics, including registration, travel-approval submissions, and related communications.

Facilitation and Process Improvement

  • Serve as facilitator for meetings and ad-hoc projects: set agendas, manage to the agenda, track action items, distribute minutes, and keep stakeholders current on next steps.
  • Coordinate facilitation planning for the PMO: gather information from sponsors and stakeholders, research appropriate facilitation methods, review reference documentation, facilitate, and document a Parking Lot and process-improvement write-up.
  • Assess PMO work to capture lessons learned and recommend process improvements, and help develop lessons-learned capture, review, and incorporation procedures across the PMO.
  • Plan, facilitate, and execute lessons-learned meetings on behalf of the Government and document findings for Government review.

Funding Management and Budget

  • Manage, track, and report funding and budget for assigned training and facilitation initiatives.
  • Submit Purchase Requisition Requests (PRRs) as directed, track financial actions in SAP, and track related costs in TRIRIGA or successor at least monthly.
  • Report funding and budget status to the Government monthly.

Coordination

  • Work closely with Mission Support Assistants and Mission Support Specialists on training-related documentation, scheduling, and travel.0

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree. Additional relevant experience may offset education requirements on a case-by-case basis with Government client and COR approval.
  • Three (3) or more years of relevant experience.
  • Strong writing, organization, and stakeholder-coordination skills.
  • Ability to design and facilitate sessions that end in documented, actionable outcomes.
  • Attention to detail in tracking compliance, certifications, and training funds.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience coordinating federal training, certification programs, or workforce development.
  • Experience with DHS FAC-COR and FAC-PM certification processes.
  • Facilitation experience for working sessions, lessons-learned meetings, and process-improvement events.
  • SharePoint content-management
  • Experience with federal travel systems and training-registration logistics.

Our Core Values

Our Leaders live out Integrity & Trust, Credibility, Accountability, Continuous

Improvement, Action Orientation, Caring for the Team, the Client, and the Business, and

Marketplace Ministry. We look for people who can answer two questions: What can I

contribute that will significantly affect the performance and results of CGINTL and the

organization I serve within? And what can I do to contribute to the bottom line?

Equal Opportunity Employer

Crowned Grace International is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

A successful background check and drug screen is required.

The successful candidate must be U.S. citizen and favorably pass a background check.

title: Coördinerend ambulant begeleider
description:
Ben jij die professional met lef, een open houding en klaar om het verschil te maken? Weet jij wat nodig is om kwetsbare burgers zo goed mogelijk te ondersteunen in hun deelname aan de samenleving? Word Coördinerend Begeleider Ambulant en werk aan een samenleving waarin iedereen meetelt!

Jouw rol

Je werkt ambulant binnen de langdurige zorg (Wlz) én het sociaal domein (Wmo). We werken vanuit een integrale aanpak waarbij we niet naar beperkingen kijken, maar naar mogelijkheden. Daarbij zetten we ons dienstverleningsconcept Mijn Netwerk in, waarin maatwerk, eigen regie en zelfredzaamheid vooropstaan.

Dit betekent dat je:

  • Individuele begeleiding biedt, maar ook gebruikt maakt van digitale ondersteuning via DigiContact en ondersteunt bij groepsmomenten, zoals op onze ontmoetingsplekken en tijdens cursussen.
  • Samenwerkt met gemeenten, ketenpartners en de sociale basis om ondersteuning optimaal te organiseren.
  • Durft te ondersteunen én los te laten, met oog voor wat écht nodig is (en niet alleen waar iemand ‘recht op heeft’).
  • Om kunt gaan met tegenstrijdige belangen binnen een dynamisch werkveld.

Jouw werkplek

Je wordt onderdeel van het ambulante team en bent werkzaam in Parkstad, Sittard-Geleen en/of Maastricht-Heuvelland. Je werkplek is veelzijdig: soms werk je met je kernteam Ambulant van Philadelphia, dan weer met collega’s van zorg wonen en regelmatig in groter verband binnen het sociaal domein, samen met collega’s van andere zorgaanbieders. Daarbij werk je dicht bij de leefwereld van de cliënt. Je ondersteunt cliënten met een licht verstandelijke beperking (LVB), vaak in combinatie met bijvoorbeeld autisme, verslaving of psychiatrische problematiek.

Je komt terecht in een betrokken en divers team met collega’s die extra ervaring meebrengen vanuit onder andere de GGZ en forensische zorg. Binnen het team krijg je volop ruimte om je te ontwikkelen. Zo bieden we alle collega’s scholing aan in methodisch begeleiden, met specifieke aandacht voor het werken met mensen met autisme (ASS) en het herkennen van psychiatrische ziektebeelden in combinatie met LVB. Op die manier zorgen we samen voor passende en professionele ondersteuning.

Over jou

Mensen omschrijven jou als een positief en open persoon die moeiteloos gelijkwaardigheid uitstraalt. Je weet humor in te zetten (want soms is relativeren dé sleutel) en je bent flexibel in denken en doen:

  • HBO werk- en denkniveau (Zorg & Welzijn).
  • Ervaring binnen de gehandicaptenzorg en/of ggz is mooi meegenomen.
  • Kennis van de sociale kaart van Zuid-Limburg is een pre.
  • Je hebt sterke schouders en schoenen waar je stevig in staat.
  • Je laat je niet snel uit het veld slaan: rust en overzicht houden is jouw tweede natuur.
  • Je vindt het niet erg om af en toe ’s avonds of in het weekend te werken.
  • Je beschikt over een rijbewijs en auto (je werkgebied is immers Limburgs uitgestrekt).

Dit krijg je van ons

Bij Philadelphia haal jij het beste uit jezelf, voor de ander. Om dit te kunnen doen moet je zelf ook goed in je vel zitten. Want dit werk vraagt veel van je. En kun je alleen maar goed doen, als je zelf ook lekker in je vel zit.
Wij bieden jou:

  • Een topteam van fijne en ervaren collega’s die samen de schouders eronder zetten.
  • Salaris tussen € 3.113,- en € 4.347,- (FWG 45, CAO Gehandicaptenzorg) bij een fulltime dienstverband (36 uur) + goede reiskosten regeling.
  • Betrokken leidinggevenden die meedenken en niet voorschrijven.
  • Invloed op je eigen werkrooster, samen met je team.
  • Ruimte om te groeien, zoals jij dat wilt: met jouw talent en ambitie, maar ook met ons Leerhuis en de vele opleidingsmogelijkheden;
  • Een betekenisvolle baan, waarin geen dag hetzelfde is.
  • Een laptop en telefoon, zodat werken thuis of ergens op een terras nóg leuker wordt.
  • Jaarcontract met intentie tot onbepaalde tijd.

Solliciteren

Vertel ons waarom jij denkt dat je bij ons past! Reageer uiterlijk 19 oktober 2026. We bekijken sollicitaties doorlopend, dus wacht niet te lang met reageren. Heb je eerst nog vragen? Neem dan gerust contact op met Marja Welman (Corporate Recruiter Zuid/West 0629062281).

Wil je sfeer proeven? Je bent van harte welkom. Een meeloopmoment en referentiecheck is onderdeel van de procedure.

Overweeg je een ‘second career’ in de zorg? Wij verwelkomen zij-instromers met de juiste competenties!

Tot slot! Bij ons ben je welkom zoals je bent, waar je vandaan komt, waar je in gelooft of van wie je houdt, maakt ons niets uit. We zijn vooral benieuwd naar jouw talent en hoe jij het verschil maakt. Wij kijken uit naar je sollicitatie!

title: Director of Commissioning
description:
5C DATA CENTERS

Join the Future of Digital Infrastructure

Are you a passionate Director of Commissioning looking to make a meaningful impact? We're building the next generation of digital infrastructure powering hyperscalers, AI innovation, and high-performance computing across North America.

JOB TITLE

Director of Commissioning

DEPARTMENT

DC Construction

LOCATION

USA

WORK ARRANGEMENT

Remote

TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS

25-50%

SALARY RANGE

$210,000-250,000 USD

Role Summary

The Director of Commissioning will lead 5C's field commissioning function, reporting directly to the VP of Commissioning & Quality Assurance. Initially the primary dedicated commissioning resource, is a hands-on leader who establishes portfolio standards, commissioning strategies and readiness requirements; provides independent assurance of testing and system performance; and coaches delivery teams and commissioning providers.

The role will help define portfolio-wide commissioning governance from design and pre-construction through construction, energization, functional performance testing, integrated systems testing and handover. As the portfolio scales, the Director develops and implements approved coverage plans using direct hires, third-party commissioning providers and specialist resources while retaining functional accountability

How We Work at 5C

Our core values guide how we collaborate, make decisions, support one another, and serve our customers. We're looking for people who embrace them and help us build something great.

What You Will Do

Commissioning Strategy & Governance

  • Establish portfolio commissioning standards, roles, responsibilities, script requirements, acceptance criteria, and escalation paths.
  • Personally oversee priority commissioning activities while developing reusable procedures, templates, tools, and a risk-based roadmap.

Scalable Staffing & Third-Party Resource Management

  • Develop resource triggers based on concurrent sites, commissioning complexity, test duration, geographic spread and specialist requirements.
  • Recruit approved hires and manage third-party commissioning providers and specialists with clear competency, authority, deliverables, and performance expectations.

Design & Pre-construction Integration

  • Partner with Engineering and Planning & Pre-construction to review commissioning implications of design, sequences of operation, controls architecture, maintainability, and testability.
  • Embed commissioning requirements, witness points, test boundaries, specialist needs, schedule logic and documentation requirements into design reviews, procurement packages, and project plans.

Contractor & Commissioning Vendor Selection

  • Evaluate commissioning providers and contractor commissioning capability, relevant mission-critical experience, technical depth, staffing and proposed methodology.
  • Review commissioning plans, staffing, test procedures, equipment startup responsibilities, and readiness criteria; require deficiencies are corrected before affected testing proceeds.

Construction & Startup Readiness

  • Establish system turnover and commissioning-readiness criteria based on needs of the customer (Operations), including installation completion, quality records, controls readiness, labeling, documentation, and safe access.
  • Coordinate with Build Quality and Construction to prevent incomplete installation of systems from entering functional testing.

Functional Performance & Integrated Systems Testing

  • Own the portfolio methodology for functional performance testing and integrated systems testing, including failure scenarios, sequence verification, redundancy, controls, and recovery behavior.
  • Witness or direct critical tests, challenge assumptions and ensure objective evidence supports acceptance.

Deficiency Management & Corrective Action

  • Establish risk-based deficiency classification, ownership, due dates, escalation, and closure verification.
  • Identify systemic or repeat failures and drive root-cause analysis and corrective action across projects.

Energization, Live-Site & Operations Interfaces

  • Partner with Engineering, Pre-Construction, Operations and Safety to define testing boundaries, temporary configurations, and operational constraints.
  • Ensure operational personnel are engaged in testing, training, documentation review, and phased turnover.

Documentation, Data & Knowledge Management

  • Establish the commissioning record as a reliable source of acceptance evidence, including test scripts, results, trends, deficiencies, and final records.
  • Use digital platforms and analytics to identify recurring failure modes, schedule risk, and portfolio-wide improvement opportunities.

Performance, Risk & Executive Reporting

title: Research Intern (Academic Credit) - Biomedical Sciences - Riera Lab
description:
Description

Overview of Department & Mentor
Dr. Celine Riera is an Associate Professor in the Center for Neural Science and Medicine within the Department of Biomedical Sciences at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center. Her research program is focused on understanding the neuronal and neuroendocrine mechanisms that regulate energy homeostasis, thermoregulation, and metabolic health, particularly in the context of aging and obesity.

The Riera laboratory integrates systems neuroscience, metabolism, and physiology to investigate how specific hypothalamic circuits and peripheral tissues, such as adipose tissue, interact to control whole-body energy balance. Ongoing projects include studying the role of sympathetic innervation of adipose tissue, neurotrophic signaling (e.g., NGF), and hypothalamic neuronal populations (including AVP and CCK-expressing neurons) in regulating metabolism and age-related physiological decline.

The lab employs a highly interdisciplinary approach combining in vivo mouse models, viral and genetic manipulations, metabolic phenotyping, imaging, transcriptomics (including single-nucleus RNA sequencing and spatial approaches), and human tissue analyses. Dr. Riera serves as the primary mentor and is actively involved in trainee development, providing guidance in experimental design, scientific communication, and career development within academia and biomedical research.

Role Summary & Objectives
The intern will serve as a trainee within an active biomedical research laboratory, contributing to ongoing projects while gaining exposure to experimental science. The primary goal of this role is to provide a rigorous and supportive educational experience that introduces the intern to fundamental concepts in neuroscience, metabolism, and translational research.
Goals and Objectives:
-Develop a foundational understanding of how neural circuits regulate physiological processes such as energy balance and thermoregulation

-Gain hands-on experience with experimental techniques used in modern biomedical research
-Learn how to interpret scientific data and understand the broader research questions being addressed
-Build critical thinking and problem-solving skills through active participation in research discussions
Skills and Techniques the Intern Will Learn:
-Basic laboratory skills (pipetting, sample preparation, record keeping)
-Immunohistochemistry and microscopy techniques
-Exposure to molecular biology methods (e.g., RNA/protein analysis)
-Introduction to data analysis and visualization
-Scientific communication, including presenting data and discussing literature
This role is designed to foster intellectual growth, scientific curiosity, and professional development, while also providing meaningful exposure to collaborative, team-based research in an academic medical center environment.

Role Activities & Timeline
The intern will receive hands-on training in a range of experimental techniques commonly used in neuroscience and metabolic research. Training will include mouse metabolic phenotyping, behavioral assays, and genotyping, providing exposure to in vivo approaches used to study physiological regulation. The intern will also be trained in tissue collection and processing, including RNA extraction and cryosectioning of brain tissue.
In addition, the intern will learn histological and imaging techniques such as immunohistochemistry, microscopy, and quantitative image analysis. Emphasis will be placed on proper experimental technique, data integrity, and reproducibility.
All activities will be conducted on-site at Cedars-Sinai under direct supervision. The intern will receive close mentorship from Dr. Riera and experienced laboratory members to ensure appropriate training, adherence to institutional guidelines, and a safe and supportive learning environment.

Qualifications

Required Education & Experience

  • Must be 18 years of age or older.
  • Must have a HS Diploma or GED.
  • Must reside in the greater Los Angeles area or surrounding cities while conducting all activities related to the intern appointment.
  • INTERNS: Those participating for academic credit must receive academic credit for the duration of the internship.

7-10+ years’ experience in a Security Operations Centre (MDR or MSSP) or customer-facing security role, including leading escalations or complex case management.
Advanced knowledge of adversary behaviour and the MITRE ATT&CK framework: you can map observed activity to techniques, explain the attack chain to a customer in plain language, and judge severity and likely next steps.
Advanced knowledge of Windows internals and endpoint telemetry: process trees and parent/child relationships, services, scheduled tasks, registry, persistence mechanisms, credential access, lateral movement, and Windows event logs. Working knowledge of Linux and macOS endpoint behaviour.
Hands-on investigation experience with EDR platforms (such as CrowdStrike, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, SentinelOne, or equivalent), including interpreting detections, scoping activity across hosts, and knowing which response actions are safe to take and when.
Hands-on experience with SIEM and log platforms (such as Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, or equivalent), including writing and tuning queries (SPL, KQL, or similar) and regular expressions to validate a detection and scope an incident.
Working knowledge of networking and network telemetry: TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/S and TLS, plus proxy, firewall, and NDR or packet capture data, well enough to separate malicious traffic from benign.
Working knowledge of cloud and identity security: Microsoft 365 and Entra ID, Active Directory, and AWS, Azure, or GCP audit logs. This includes authentication flows (SSO, MFA, Kerberos, OAuth) and common abuse patterns such as token theft, MFA fatigue, and business email compromise.
Experience with email and phishing analysis: message headers, SPF/DKIM/DMARC results, and URL and attachment triage.
Understanding of how detections are built and tuned, including the trade-off between false positives and false negatives. You can explain why a detection misfired and what would make it more accurate.
Experience troubleshooting complex issues in security tooling and services, such as agent health, log ingestion gaps, integration or API failures, and tracing them to root cause. You can read JSON and API responses.
Working knowledge of AI and LLM concepts in cybersecurity, with the ability to translate a process into clear decision logic (inputs, conditions, outputs, and failure cases) that another team can automate, and to build or use tooling that improves efficiency and supports security investigations.
Experience applying responsible and ethical AI practices in security, including refining prompts and interpreting results to reduce bias and support objective conclusions, contributing to model training and validation, assessing when AI-generated conclusions are safe or need manual review, and identifying and communicating emerging AI risks (e.g., drift, adversarial inputs, inconsistent logic) while staying current on AI-powered threats and defensive capabilities.
Experience auditing, coaching, or mentoring others, formally or informally.
Experience building training, knowledge content, or documented procedures that other people use.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to lead sensitive conversations and drive escalated issues to resolution.
Work scheduled shifts in a 24x7 operation, which can include nights, weekends, and holidays.

Industry certifications (GCIH, GCFA, GX-FA, GCFR, GPEN, GEIR, etc.) or equivalent.
Ability to read and write scripts for triage and analysis (PowerShell or Python, for example).
Experience with digital forensics, malware triage, or sandbox analysis.
Experience applying threat intelligence to investigations or detection improvement.
Exposure to case automation, SOAR, or playbook design work.
Experience maintaining a knowledge base or playbooks rooted in adult learning (andragogical) principles.
Familiarity with MDR/XDR tooling.

title: Director, Land Development
description:
Overview
Fleet Data Centers designs, builds and operates mega-scale data center campuses. Fleet provides its customers flexibility and predictability to meet their upside demand forecasts, addressing a key need in the market as traditional leased models are struggling to keep pace with the demand for new Cloud and AI infrastructure. Fleet is led by a team of industry veterans that have already made a lasting imprint on the evolution of global digital infrastructure and are committed and uniquely capable of upleveling data center development scale and operations in the face of rising demand. Fleet is well positioned to bring in-house design, engineering and operational capabilities to collaborate with customers on tailored solutions for campuses of 500MW+. This unique model enables Fleet to provide the world’s largest and most sophisticated customers a seamless extension of their own data center fleets with constant access to design innovation.

Position Overview

The Director of Land Development supports the pre-development phase of Tract Capital's data center and energy projects and carries those projects forward through the balance of their lifecycle. The role sits within Tract Capital's Project Development team, a subset of the Investments & Strategy team that holds responsibility for the development of Tract Capital's data center and energy assets. The Director of Land Development leads site diligence, campus master planning, entitlements, and permitting, from initial site control or joint venture through stabilization, then stays with the project through lease, vertical construction, stabilization, and the ultimate disposition of the asset. The Director of Land Development works closely alongside senior members of the organization, and represents Tract Capital and its operating strategies before the jurisdictions, agencies, utilities, and communities that decide whether a campus gets built.

Job Responsibilities

In addition to other duties assigned, the Director of Land Development will hold the following primary responsibilities:

  • Lead site inquiry and evaluation of prospective sites in assigned markets, identifying the risks and opportunities that determine whether a site advances to site control or joint venture formation, and carrying multiple projects across diverse jurisdictions at once
  • Own the pre-development workstream plan for assigned projects: define the diligence scope at site control or joint venture formation, sequence the studies that gate a development decision, and hold the schedule that carries a site from control to vertical construction
  • Run land and site diligence, including title and survey, geotechnical, environmental, wetlands, cultural resources, traffic, and water and wastewater, and convert the findings into buildable area, phasing, and cost consequences that leadership can act on
  • Drive entitlements and permitting across local, state, and federal jurisdictions: map the approval path for each site, prepare applications alongside counsel and consultants, and carry hearings through to recorded approvals and issued permits
  • Direct master planning with internal and external stakeholders so each campus plan reconciles critical load, building form factor, substation and switchyard siting, water strategy, and site constraints, and revise that plan as customer requirements, power availability, and investment strategy move
  • Support the internal power teams on the entitlements, permits, and land use matters that power infrastructure requires, including substation and switchyard siting approvals, transmission and distribution easements and rights-of-way, conditional use approvals for generation and battery energy storage, and the property rights needed to bring interconnection and behind-the-meter solutions onto the site
  • Support the creation and management of a bottom-up pre-development budget, tracking commitments and spend against it and helping forecast the capital draw by phase so leadership can plan funding
  • Assemble and manage the consultant bench: write scopes of work, support solicitations, bid-leveling, recommend awards to management, negotiate agreements with internal legal, and hold each firm to its deliverable dates
  • Interrogate engineering and consultant deliverables before they circulate, testing them against the approval path, the site constraints, and the development schedule, and returning work that does not hold up
  • Represent Tract Capital and its operating strategies before local government, including planning and zoning commissions and public works staff, and attend city council and county commission meetings as required
  • Work the rest of the local apparatus that moves an approval, including assessors, clerks, utilities, and state and local economic development offices, and build the relationships that drive approvals
  • Support leasing and capital markets on assigned sites, translating site and schedule reality into delivery dates and costs that can be committed to customers, lenders, and investment partners
  • Advance the horizontal scope that makes a campus buildable, including water, wastewater, fiber, and road infrastructure to the site and coordinating earthworks packages specific to data center campus use
  • Represent Tract Capital and its operating strategies in the community, building and maintaining relationships with adjacent landowners and community groups, and reflecting the company's approach to land stewardship and local economic benefit in every public interaction
  • Uphold company Environment, Health & Safety standards across consultant and contractor activity on assigned sites
  • Hand projects to construction without losing the record, transferring permit conditions, commitments made to jurisdictions and utilities, and design assumptions, then stay with assigned projects through vertical construction, stabilization, and disposition
  • Contribute to scalable tools and processes that improve project delivery and communication, from schedule and budget standards to trackers and reporting templates, so each new site starts from the last one's lessons

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering, real estate development, architecture, planning, or an equivalent discipline. Current or past Professional Engineer licensure greatly preferred.

  • Minimum four years' experience in large-scale land development, civil engineering, site planning, construction, or data center and energy development, including direct ownership of at least one entitlement path from application through approval. Data center, utility, or telecom engineering experience greatly preferred. Candidates who have taken a greenfield site through to a construction start, will stand out.

Core Skills & Competencies

  • Working knowledge of real estate development fundamentals, including ownership and site control structures, land use frameworks, rezoning mechanics, and the entitlement processes that apply to large-scale industrial and infrastructure projects
  • Practical command of the diligence stack, including what each study can and cannot resolve and how long each one takes in a given jurisdiction
  • Ability to read a civil site plan and a utility one-line and press the engineer who drew it, sufficient to test buildable area, phasing, and infrastructure assumptions rather than accept them
  • Working knowledge of power and energy infrastructure as it relates to data center development — including utility interconnection, behind-the-meter power solutions, and battery energy storage systems — sufficient to track queue position, study milestones, and energization dates against the campus schedule
  • Command of pre-development budgeting and capital forecasting, with enough modeling literacy to see how a schedule slip or a scope change lands in project returns
  • Demonstrated negotiating experience with consultants, contractors, utilities, and public agencies, covering scope, fee structure, and the commitments made to secure an approval
  • Ability to carry several sites in different jurisdictions at once without dropping conditions, deadlines, or commitments, and to reprioritize as sites advance or stall
  • Judgment to escalate, surfacing a schedule or cost problem while it can still be fixed — without waiting to be directed
  • Direct writing, covering internal reports and dashboards as well as external land use applications, producing packages a senior audience can act on without a walkthrough
  • Strong verbal communication, including internal presentations and public speaking at local government meetings
  • Ability to manage projects and teams to a predictable conclusion, and to problem solve by leveraging independent analysis, local relationships, corporate resources, and executive support
  • Curiosity and the ability to network in structured and unstructured settings, surfacing opportunities and challenges early
  • Fluency in Excel for budgets and schedules and PowerPoint for leadership reporting, with comfort in drawing markup and project tracking tools

Location: New York, NY, Morristown, NJ, or remote

Travel Requirement: 50% This position requires regular travel to project sites, jurisdictional hearings, utility and consultant meetings, and Tract Capital offices, with meaningful time in the field during active entitlement periods.

Expected Salary Range: $180,000 - $195,000 Base Salary + Discretionary Bonus

Fleet Data Centers employees enjoy competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits, including 100% employer-covered medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401K program, standard paid holidays, and unlimited PTO.

If you need assistance applying for any of our open positions, please contact us at info@fleetdatacenters.com.

title: Organisational Design Consultant
description:
The Organisational Design Consultant answers the question the other two workstreams cannot: who, specifically, inside the client organisation will own, write, review, approve, and maintain this content once the consultants leave — and does that capacity exist today or does it need to be created?

Enabling a Genesys AI feature does not by itself create value, and that processes, legacy tools, and operating practices will need to change alongside it. This role designs that change at the organisational level. It is a part-time engagement concentrated in two to three months of the overall project, and it should be sequenced to begin once the current-state content and requirements picture is sufficiently developed to design against.

Responsibilities:

  • Document the current-state organisation. Map the organisational units, roles, reporting lines, and capacity currently involved in knowledge creation and maintenance across the in-scope business lines — tax, individual enquiries, and business enquiries. Identify who performs content work today, formally or informally, and how much of their time it consumes.
  • Conduct the organisational design analysis. Assess the gap between the current-state organisation and what the target knowledge management operating model requires. Identify capability gaps, capacity shortfalls, unclear or contested ownership, single points of failure, and the places where content work is currently being absorbed informally by people whose job description does not mention it.
  • Build the Organisational RACI Matrix. This is the central deliverable. Define, at named-role level, who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed for every stage of the content lifecycle — authoring, subject matter review, legal or policy review, official-languages review, accessibility review, publication, periodic review, and retirement. The matrix must be specific enough that the client can act on it: which positions need to be created, which need to be reassigned, and which existing roles need their scope formally amended.
  • Define the target knowledge management operating model. Specify the structure needed to sustain the capability — whether a central knowledge team, a federated model with embedded content owners in each business line, or a hybrid — with the rationale, the trade-offs, and the resourcing implication of each option.
  • Produce role profiles and resourcing requirements, including the AI-era roles. Draft position descriptions for the new or amended roles the model requires — knowledge manager, taxonomy steward, content owner, content author — and for the roles the Genesys AI roadmap creates that do not exist in the organisation today: who tunes and retrains the virtual agents, who reviews AI-surfaced answers for accuracy, who owns the feedback loop from AI failure back to content correction. Include competencies, effort estimates, and classification guidance the client needs to resource them through their own staffing processes.
  • Design the transition and change approach. Set out the sequence for moving from current to target state, the change-management, training, and communication requirements, and the risks — including the realistic constraints of staffing in a federal environment, where creating or reclassifying a position is not a quick exercise.
  • Align with the governance workstream. Work directly with the Senior Business Consultant so that the Governance Playbook and the RACI Matrix describe the same organisation. Governance that names no owner, and an org model with no governance, both fail.
  • 8+ years in organisational design, operating model design, workforce planning, or organisational effectiveness consulting.
  • Demonstrated experience producing an organisational design deliverable set that a client implemented — RACI matrices, target operating models, role profiles, and transition plans.
  • Experience designing operating models for a function that spans multiple business units, where ownership is shared or contested.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement capability at director and executive level, with the credibility to tell a client that a capability they want is not resourced and will not survive without structural change.
  • Ability to work effectively in a part-time, concentrated engagement alongside a wider consulting team.
  • Eligible to obtain and hold a Government of Canada security clearance.

Nice to have:

  • Prior experience designing the operating model for a knowledge management, content, or digital service function specifically.
  • Contact centre or shared services operating model experience, particularly where AI or automation changed the shape of agent work and the roles required to support it.
  • Formal change management credential (Prosci, CCMP) or an organisational development qualification.
  • Bilingual English/French.

We offer:

  • Culture of Relentless Performance: join an unstoppable technology development team with a 99% project success rate and more than 30% year-over-year revenue growth.
  • Competitive Pay and Benefits: enjoy a comprehensive compensation and benefits package, including health insurance, language courses, and a relocation program.
  • Growth Mindset: reap the benefits of a range of professional development opportunities, including certification programs, mentorship and talent investment programs, internal mobility and internship opportunities.
  • Global Impact: collaborate on impactful projects for top global clients and shape the future of industries.
  • Welcoming Multicultural Environment: be a part of a dynamic, global team and thrive in an inclusive and supportive work environment with open communication and regular team-building company social events.
  • Social Sustainability Values: join our sustainable business practices focused on five pillars, including IT education, community empowerment, fair operating practices, environmental sustainability, and gender equality.

title: VP of Engineering
description:
About Ornn
Ornn is building the financial infrastructure for AI compute. Our price indices are live on Bloomberg Terminal. We structure and trade compute hedging instruments. And we're now building a platform that brings exchange-grade mechanics like order management, matching, scheduling, and settlement to how compute capacity gets reserved and allocated. We're a lean team in New York, backed by leading venture and strategic investors.

About the Role
This role will lead engineering at Ornn and own the systems the whole business runs on. Our platform handles real capacity commitments backed by real contracts, and our indices are used to price and hedge them, so the bar is closer to a trading system than a typical SaaS product. A bug here is a financial event, not just an incident ticket.

Day to day, the role splits between setting technical direction across Ornn Data, Ornn Exchange and Ornn Compute, building and leading the engineering team, and staying close enough to the code to make good calls on architecture, reliability and tradeoffs. The position works directly with the founders, and with product, GTM and markets, because what we build has to match what we sell and what our counterparties rely on.

What You'll Do
  • Own the technical strategy and architecture across our data, exchange and compute platforms, and make the calls on what we build, buy and defer.
  • Build the engineering team: hire senior engineers, set the bar, and grow a small group into a high-performing org without losing speed.
  • Make reliability and correctness a feature. Set the standards for testing, code review, observability, incident response and security.
  • Run engineering execution: planning, priorities and delivery, so the team ships on the timelines our customers and partners depend on.
  • Partner with the founders, product and markets teams to turn new financial products and customer needs into a clear technical roadmap.


What We're Looking For

Requirements
  • 5+ years building production software, including 2+ years leading engineering teams.
  • A track record of scaling an engineering team and platform at an early-stage, high-growth company.
  • Deep experience with systems where correctness and uptime matter, such as trading, payments, exchanges or core infrastructure.
  • Strong technical depth in backend and distributed systems.
  • Excellent judgment on architecture and tradeoffs, and the ability to explain them clearly to engineers and non-engineers alike.
  • An operator mentality and high agency. You are comfortable in a lean team where the leader still builds.


Nice-to-Haves
  • Experience at a trading firm, exchange, market data provider, fintech or crypto company.
  • Familiarity with GPU compute, cloud infrastructure or datacenter operations.
  • Rust experience, especially for performance-critical systems.
  • Experience with security and compliance programs such as SOC 2, or with regulated financial products.


Why This Role Matters
Everything Ornn offers rests on the platform working. Our indices, the hedging products built on them and the marketplace that allocates real capacity all assume a reliable, correct system underneath. This role will decide how that system gets built and who builds it, and the decisions made in the next year will shape what Ornn can become.

Compensation and Benefits
Benefits include competitive salary, meaningful equity, health coverage, free meals, and additional benefits. This is a leadership role with significant strategic impact and equity upside.

Equal Opportunity Statement
Ornn is committed to building a diverse team. We evaluate candidates based on their ability to do the work, not on pedigree or background. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences.

title: Gastroenterologian erikoislääkäriksi Terveystaloon
description:
Me Terveystalossa teemme työksemme tärkeintä, terveyttä. Työllämme on suuri merkitys, ei vain asiakkaillemme, vaan koko yhteiskunnalle. Meitä tärkeimmän tekijöitä on Terveystalossa jo yli 14 000 lähes 400 toimipaikassa eri puolilla Suomea. Siellä, missä ihmiset elävät arkeaan ja missä kotimaista työtämme tarvitaan.

Etsimme nyt gastroenterologian erikoislääkäreitä Lahteen, Turkuun, Kouvolaan sekä Hyvinkäälle. Tutustu yksiköihin ja jätä yhteystietosi, niin suunnitellaan sinulla sopiva kokonaisuus!

  • Lahden Terveystalo muuttaa uusiin, moderneihin tiloihin kauppakeskus Trioon loppuvuodesta 2026. Käytössä on Olympuksen laitteet: kolme gastroskooppia ja kaksi kolonoskooppia. Tähystyksiä on mahdollista tehdä maanantaisin sekä tiistaisin ja keskiviikkoisin aamuisin.
  • Turun Terveystalossa on ison talon palvelut ja laajat aukioloajat. Kuusi kolonoskooppia ja kolme gastroskooppia. Tarve erityisesti vastaanottoja tekevälle gastroenterologille.
  • Kouvolan Terveystalossa on joustava mahdollisuus vastaanottoihin ja tähystyksiin. Käytössä on Olympuksen laitteet, yksi gastroskooppi ja yksi kolonoskooppi.
  • Hyvinkään Terveystalossa voit tehdä tähystysten lisäksi ligneerauksia sekä patin, luomien ym. poistoja. Pyrimme järjestämään hoitajaresurssin omien aikataulujesi mukaan.

Tarjoamme gastroenterologeillemme hyvin toimivat ja nykyaikaiset endoskopiayksiköt yli 25 lääkäriasemalla. Viime vuosina olemme kehittäneet erityisesti konsultaatiomahdollisuuksia, kattavia laboratoriotoimintoja ja hoitopolkuja mm. ravitsemusterapeuttien kanssa. Diagnosoinnissa käytössäsi on myös kokeneet patologit, jotka ovat tottuneet gastroenterologisten näytteiden analytiikkaan. Yhteistyö gastrokirurgien kanssa on myös jokapäiväistä.

Gastroenterologian erikoisalasta vastaa vatsaelinsairauksien vastuulääkäri Markku Nissinen. Lääketieteellisen tuen lisäksi työtäsi helpottaa ja tukee oma nimetty lääkäri- ja asiantuntijavastaavasi, joka tukee sinua arkesi suunnittelussa, huolehtii perehdytyksestäsi Terveystaloon, järjestelmiimme ja toimipisteeseen. Hän varmistaa, että arkesi on sujuvaa ja voit keskittyä ydinosaamiseesi.

Lue lisää gastroenterologin ja gastrokirurgin työstä Terveystalossa: Hyvät resurssit toiminnan kehittämiseen näkyvät potilaalle sujuvana hoitopolkuna.

Kiinnostuitko tehtävästä?

Jätä yhteystietosi hakulomakkeen kautta tai ole yhteydessä suoraan minuun, niin suunnitellaan yhdessä sinulle sopiva kokonaisuus.

Tuukka Ronkainen, vastaava ura-asiantuntija, p. 044 4942 147, tuukka.ronkainen@terveystalo.com

You will join a highly collaborative Cedar Legal & Compliance team and serve as a go-to legal partner to Cedar’s growth, client management, sales, strategic partnerships, and vendor contracting teams, owning a portfolio of complex deals from structuring to signature. You will also help shape the playbooks, templates, and AI-enabled workflows the rest of the team relies on. Growth opportunities in the role based on your skills, experience, and interests may include product counseling, privacy, compliance, marketing, and general corporate matters, with guidance from experienced colleagues.

At Cedar, we offer customizable, enterprise solutions to leading health systems aimed at improving the healthcare financial experience for Americans, so our commercial agreements are large, complex and highly negotiated. This is a unique opportunity for you to work on high-stakes deals while helping curate the tech- and AI-forward tools and practices that help our team scale. You will have real latitude to improve our contracting process, grow your skills, get regular coaching and feedback, put new tools into practice, and see the direct impact of your work on deal velocity and our business.

Responsibilities

  • Commercial Transactions: Structure, draft, and negotiate complex sales, vendor, and strategic partnership agreements, including Master Services Agreements (MSAs), HIPAA Business Associate Agreements (BAAs), license agreements, and consulting agreements. Own a portfolio of assigned matters from intake through execution, manage competing deadlines, and partner with product, privacy, and compliance legal colleagues for specialist support.
  • Business Counseling: Serve as a trusted and pragmatic legal advisor to sales, finance, procurement, and business development teams on deal structures and commercial terms, including AI, technology licensing, data rights, and go-to-market activities.
  • Technology, Ops, & AI Enablement: Partner with legal colleagues to identify and implement ongoing improvements of Cedar’s standard contract templates (MSA, BAA, NDA, Order Form, and Service Descriptions.), deal intelligence and playbooks, and legal processes to ensure they remain streamlined and "plain English." Collaborate with Legal & Compliance Operations to maintain and improve contract templates, playbooks, CLM tools, and technology-enabled contracting workflows. Use approved technology and AI tools to improve drafting, contract review, and access to contract information, with appropriate attention to confidentiality, accuracy, and team guidance. Measure and share results, such as cycle time and business self-service.
  • Team: Contribute as a team player to help further the status of the Legal & Compliance team as an effective, respected, and valued resource within the company. Collaborate with the Legal Product, Regulatory, and Compliance team to understand relevant product and regulatory developments and incorporate agreed updates into Cedar’s agreements, templates, and guidance.
  • Knowledge Sharing: Share practical learnings, business direction, and market insights with teammates. Seek and incorporate feedback, and support the onboarding and development of colleagues as appropriate.
  • Outside Counsel Collaboration: Collaborate with specialized outside counsel and supplemental legal resources on assigned technology transactions and other matters, with attention to quality and budget.
  • Periodic travel to New York and other locations for company and team meetings.

Required Skills & Experience

  • JD Degree from an accredited law school and license in good standing to practice law in at least one state bar.
  • 4-6 years of relevant legal experience at a leading law firm and/or in-house (a combination is a plus), including substantial experience drafting and negotiating technology transactions and enterprise SaaS agreements. Experience with AI, healthcare technology, and HIPAA is a strong plus, but not required.
  • Legal Operations & AI Fluency: Hands-on experience improving how legal work gets done, from systems to tools, such as building playbooks or clause libraries, configuring workflows, or using AI tools for drafting and contract review, along with the judgment on how to use these tools inside and outside of the legal team.
  • Adaptability and Growth Mindset: Thrives amidst shifting priorities and ambiguity, bringing clarity and direction where information or processes are still evolving. Eager to ask questions, incorporate feedback, learn new areas, and experiment with practical and AI-enabled improvements to legal workflows. Previous experience in technology or high-growth companies is preferred.
  • Negotiation and Communication Skills: Demonstrated ability to lead assigned commercial negotiations with sophisticated organizations and their legal teams, partnering with senior counsel on novel, unusually complex, or material risks. Ability to explain complex terms and tradeoffs clearly to business stakeholders, develop pragmatic solutions, negotiate convincingly, and manage multiple matters with competing deadlines.
  • Drafting Excellence: Strong contract drafting skills. Demonstrated ability to draft in plain English and write clear legal guidance that business partners can understand and apply. Experience identifying and contributing improvements to contract templates and playbooks.
  • Business and Legal Judgment: Sound judgment in spotting product and commercial risks, weighing business objectives, and recommending pragmatic solutions. Comfort making risk calls independently within established guidelines, and knows when to escalate, seek input, or consult a colleague.
  • Collaborative Mindset: A self-starter who takes ownership of assigned matters, follows through reliably, and builds effective relationships with Sales, Finance, Product, and other business partners. Works collaboratively within Legal & Compliance and seeks and shares expertise as needed.

Compensation Range and Benefits

  • Salary/Hourly Rate Range*: $195,500 - $230,000
  • This role is equity eligible
  • This role offers a competitive benefits and wellness package

*Subject to location, experience, and education

#LI-REMOTE

What do we offer to the ideal candidate?

  • Unless stated otherwise, most roles have flexibility to work from home or in the office, depending on what works best for you
  • For exempt employees: Unlimited PTO for vacation, sick and mental health days–we encourage everyone to take at least 20 days of vacation per year to ensure dedicated time to spend with loved ones, explore, rest and recharge

About us

Cedar was co-founded by Florian Otto and Arel Lidow in 2016 after a negative medical billing experience inspired them to help improve our healthcare system. title: Certified Financial Planner (Part-time)
description:
About LearnLux

LearnLux is the leading provider of workplace financial wellbeing, blending fiduciary digital planning with access to one-on-one guidance from Certified Financial Planner™️ professionals. Our award-winning program helps employees navigate critical financial decisions from budgeting and benefits elections to equity compensation, home buying, and retirement so they can feel confident about their money and focused at work. If you’re energized by solving new problems, taking accountability, and pushing yourself to do your best work every day, you’ll find this a rewarding environment.

We’re a venture-backed company that has raised over $35M to date and is supported by experienced investors and long-term partners. We’re a growth-focused business building for scale, and we’re excited by the opportunities and challenges that come with that journey.

LearnLux is looking for a part time Certified Financial Planner® to join our fast growing team. Your extensive financial experience and client-first approach will help employees prepare for and accomplish their personal and financial goals.

This role is 100% remote within the US and reports to the Director of Financial Planning.

What you’ll do

  • Must be available to work various shifts from 8 AM - 11 PM ET Monday through Friday with a typical expectation, but not guarantee, of 5-15 hours per week
  • Meet and engage with clients remotely over video, chat and email to give guidance on topics like budgeting, student loans, retirement readiness, equity compensation, debt management and more

  • Can demonstrate ability to take initiative and execute
  • Experience in multiple areas of personal Finance: Retirement, Equity Compensation, investments, budgeting, debt management, Student Loans, cash flow planning, digital currencies, estate planning, insurance and more

It would be great if you also

  • CPA, Enrolled Agent, or similar
  • Certification in Credit Counseling
  • Additional Certifications
  • Startup and/or Fintech experience
  • Bi-lingual (Spanish)
  • Experience creating presentations and presenting to large audiences virtually or in-person
  • Availability to work occasional evenings and Saturday
  • Ability to occasionally travel to on-site events

LearnLux is a fit for you if you

  • Thrive in fast-moving environments and enjoy building in moments of change. We operate with urgency, and roles, priorities, and approaches evolve as we grow.

  • Take initiative and don’t wait to be asked. You see problems as opportunities and are comfortable stepping in to move work forward.
  • Are energized by ambiguity and willing to make decisions with imperfect information. We learn quickly by doing, and pace is a competitive advantage for us.
  • Enjoy being hands-on and owning work end to end. While strategic thinking matters, execution, follow-through, and accountability are what drive impact here.
  • Are motivated by high standards and continuous improvement. As we hit new milestones, we intentionally raise the bar on quality, ownership, and outcomes.
  • Value clear, frequent communication and collaboration. As a remote team, staying aligned through proactive communication is core to how we operate.

Closing

LearnLux strives to be an inclusive workplace and values learning from and engaging across different perspectives. Women, people of color, LGBTQIA+ individuals, and members of other minority or marginalized groups are strongly encouraged to apply.

LearnLux is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against candidates on the basis of race, ethnicity, color, national origin, age, religion, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, disability, or veteran status.

We are committed to fostering an environment that embraces diversity and inclusion and are seeking candidates from a variety of backgrounds, experiences, abilities, and perspectives to join our team. title: QA Engineer - Contract
description:

  • Create, maintain, and execute test cases defined in the Test Management Platform (TestRail).
  • Define pre-conditions and create test data needed for test case execution.
  • Isolate the signal from the noise through methodical troubleshooting and root cause analysis.
  • Think out-of-the-box and find creative ways to solve a variety of testing challenges.
  • Log high-quality bugs tickets into JIRA.
  • Identify and validate across browsers, operating systems, and devices.

  • Proactively provide feedback on product usability and recommendations to improve overall quality.
  • Assist in supporting the customer by assisting helpdesk support with investigations and ticket triage.

What you need to succeed:

  • 4+ years of software QA experience testing web and/or mobile applications
  • Strong experience creating, maintaining, and executing test cases, including functional, regression, exploratory, and end-to-end testing
  • Experience with SQL, preferably PostgreSQL, including writing queries to validate data, troubleshoot issues, and support application testing
  • Experience identifying, documenting, tracking, and retesting defects, with clear reproduction steps and supporting evidence
  • Experience with TestRail and JIRA, or comparable test management and issue-tracking tools
  • Experience with web and mobile test automation, preferably Playwright/JavaScript and Appium/AltTester

  • Ability to troubleshoot test failures and differentiate between application, automation, environment, and test-data issues
  • Strong attention to detail, problem-solving skills, and ability to clearly communicate defects, test results, risks, and release readiness
  • Ability to collaborate with Product, Design, Development, and QA to clarify requirements, identify edge cases, and ensure adequate test coverage

title: Product Design Intern
description:
About us:

Kiva is a global nonprofit, founded in 2005, with a mission to expand financial access and help underserved communities thrive. Kiva unlocks capital for borrowers through crowdfunded loans supported by individuals around the world. Lenders on Kiva can start with as little as $25 to support causes that matter most to them, whether that’s gender equity and support for women, refugees, climate change, small businesses, agriculture, and more. Since our founding, over two million people have invested over $2 billion in real dreams and real opportunity, spanning more than 100 countries and over 5 million borrowers.

As we work toward our mission, Kiva invests in building and retaining a global team of talent to add to our values-driven and digital-first culture. Our organization is supported by over 700 volunteers and 130+ full-time employees dispersed around the world, as well as within team hubs located in San Francisco, Nairobi, Bogota, and Bangkok. Kiva’s team is growing as we pursue exciting new opportunities to scale our impact and create a financially inclusive world.

Kiva's values:

Impact first - This is why we exist. This is the drumbeat we march to. Every day.

Extreme ownership - Own it; you, your relationships, your impact. Insist that others support you and hold you accountable.

Be curious and bold - Never stop learning. Question assumptions. Take Risks and dream big.

Inclusion. Equity. Diversity. - Without reservation and without caveat. In our hiring, in our workplace and in our impact in the world.

Honor and integrity - Do the most right thing in the most right way. Cherish diversity and respect each other.

Love and kindness always - Say what you mean. Mean what you say. And don't say it mean. Clarity. Courage. Kindness.

Internship Program

Since its founding, volunteerism has been an integral part of Kiva's foundation and success. As a Kiva Intern, you will contribute your passion, drive, ideas, and expertise to expanding our reach and impact while taking on immediate and significant responsibilities within your team. In addition to learning on the job, you'll partake in a variety of educational, social, and professional development workshops and events that will accelerate your professional growth while learning about Kiva and the non-profit, technology, and microfinance sectors.

Through this volunteer internship, we’re hoping to provide a high-caliber learning experience. With the completion of our internship program, you will take away many in-demand job skills. Additionally, all Kiva interns will gain exposure to foundational microfinance concepts and ongoing professional development tailored to your career goals. This position will also put you in contact with a wide array of employees around the world, giving you a jump start on networking opportunities.

This Kiva internship is a 6-month, part-time (24- 32 hours per week), United States-based, remote volunteer position.

Placement Process

Kiva places interns within most departments of the organization. During recruitment, we evaluate your application and interests to match you to a specific team that will leverage your talents while providing you with an opportunity to develop and grow.

Although Kiva Interns range in age and experience, a common theme among our participants is a "can do" attitude as well as a desire and willingness to dive in and get their hands dirty.

Role overview:

Joining Kiva's Design Team, you'll be reporting to our Principal Product Designer. Our Product Design team has worked on experiences for some of the biggest brands in the world, including Apple, Google, HBO, and Mastercard. Your work at Kiva will enable people across the world to do good and help each other. This role requires a high level of collaboration with our Product Management and Engineering teams. We're looking for curious, thoughtful, collaborative people who want to live their values.

We're looking for a Product Design Intern with a focus on UX design, strong UX writing, and a knack for systems thinking. Each day will be super collaborative: you'll work with an international team of Kivans, designing features for millions of users, running studies with our Principal Researcher, and contributing to Kiva's design system.

At this time, we can only consider applicants with authorization to work in the United States on a permanent, full-time basis; unfortunately, we cannot provide visa sponsorship.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Partner with our Principal Researcher on at least one research project, helping conduct user interviews, usability tests, and surveys, and turning what you learn into insights that shape product decisions
  • Join a cross-functional team of engineers and a product manager to design and ship at least one feature tested live on Kiva.org, from early flows and wireframes through launch
  • Build interactive prototypes in Figma to explore ideas, test with users, and communicate designs to your team
  • Contribute to Kiva's design system by defining and shipping at least one new component or primitive alongside the system's design and engineering leads
  • Share your work in weekly design critiques with the team, giving and receiving feedback and explaining your decisions to designers and non-designers alike

Preferred qualifications:

  • At least 21 years of age or older by January 12, 2027
  • Able to commit to the full 6-month term
  • Strong UX writing skills: you can write clear, concise, brand-aligned copy
  • Systems thinking: you can spot patterns and design reusable components
  • Visual and interaction design: you can create polished, intuitive interfaces with a strong eye for detail
  • Comfortable working on macOS
  • Proficiency with standard design tools such as Figma and Adobe Creative Cloud
  • AI design tools: you can use tools like Figma Make, Claude, and ChatGPT to explore and prototype ideas
  • Able to keep track of projects from handoff to completion
  • Proactive, able to meet deadlines, and able to explain design decisions to non-designers
  • Exceptional communicator with a knack for articulating design rationale
  • Thrives in an iterative process that involves listening, adapting, moving fast, talking with users, incorporating feedback, and constantly collaborating

What we offer:

  • Professional development and skills workshops
  • Access to Kiva’s network of Kiva Fellowship and Internship Alumni
  • Optional participation in Kiva’s Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) and social activities such as happy hours and coffee chats
  • References are gladly given for successful participants

Kiva's Internship is a part-time volunteer position, however, to help offset some expenses, Kiva will provide a modest stipend of $800 a month (before taxes) to its volunteers. Please note that the stipend is considered taxable income, and we expect interns to do their own research as to how this may affect their personal/tax implications.

The weekly time commitment for a Kiva Internship is 24 - 32 hours per week, from January 12, 2027 - June 30, 2027. Please make sure you have the availability to commit for the entire internship period before submitting an application.

A diverse and inclusive workplace where we learn from each other is an integral part of Kiva's culture. We actively welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer and a great place to work. Join us and help us achieve our mission!

We will only accept applications directly from candidates. Kiva will not be responsible for any recruiting agency fees, absent a formal agreement.

title: Administratief medewerker CJG Cursusbureau
description:

Administratief medewerker

24 uur per week (in ieder geval woensdagen, andere dagen in overleg)

Als administratief medewerker van het CJG Cursusbureau maak je deel uit van een leuk en enthousiast team en ben je medeverantwoordelijk voor de administratieve werkzaamheden rondom alle CJG cursussen. Hecht GGD Hollands Midden volgt de cao Samenwerkende Gemeentelijke Organisaties (SGO) en heeft een aantrekkelijk pakket aan (secundaire) arbeidsvoorwaarden:

title: Obsolescence Specialist
description:
Company Overview

Metrea delivers effects-as-a-service to national security partners across five domains and more than a dozen mission areas. These include airborne ISR, electronic warfare, secure communications, aerial refueling, special air missions, aerial firefighting, and advanced simulation. We own the whole stack: designing, building, and operating turnkey capabilities that give our partners decisive, asymmetric advantage against rapidly evolving threats.

Our operating model is built around three interlocking pillars. The Support Groups provide a global shared-service – spanning people, finance, platform, operations, legal, and engagement. This frees up our Core Groups, who develop and own mission capabilities end-to-end, to focus entirely on delivery. The Market Groups apply a regional lens, ensuring that our agile and adaptable capabilities remain aligned to the wicked problems that matter most to our partners across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific.

At the heart of our model is a simple but powerful idea: be a true partner with skin in the game. Our partners need effects, not just equipment. By owning the full stack – from the lab to the field – we are able to drive a continuous cycle of innovation that keeps our partners ahead. It's a fast-moving, intellectually demanding environment where talented people are given real responsibility, work on problems that matter, and contribute to an enterprise that is growing quickly and deliberately.

Headquartered in Washington, DC, with facilities across the United States, the United Kingdom, as well as Continental Europe and Asia-Pacific.

Group Overview

Air Mobility Group (AIRMOB) is responsible for developing and delivering Metrea’s aerial refueling (AAR) capabilities, ensuring the readiness and operational effectiveness of the tanker fleet. AIRMOB oversees fleet management, maintenance, and airworthiness, working to sustain and enhance refueling operations. It manages the integration of new processes and technologies, ensuring that tanker aircraft remain mission-ready through effective logistics, maintenance oversight, and regulatory compliance. By coordinating across various teams, AIRMOB ensures the fleet meets both current and future operational needs, supporting a range of specialized air mobility missions.

Position Summary

In this role, you will own the obsolescence and diminishing manufacturing sources problem for AIRMOB’s KC-135R and C-135FR fleet, aircraft that have decades of service still ahead of them despite being out of original production. You will identify component and repair-source risks before they ground a tail, build the mitigation pathway, whether that is alternate sourcing, PMA evaluation, owner-produced parts, repair development, or engineered substitution, and coordinate the cross-functional execution that keeps our aerial refuelling capability sustainable. You will be successful if our maintainers and crews never lose a mission to a part they should have known was going away.

What You'll Do

  • Lead AIRMOB’s DMSMS program by identifying obsolescence and material availability risks across the KC-135R and C-135FR fleets and tracking them in AMOS before they impact the line
  • Develop and execute mitigation strategies including alternate part sourcing, PMA evaluation, owner-produced parts under 14 CFR 21.9, surplus and used serviceable material qualification, repair source development, and engineered substitutions
  • Partner with Quality & Airworthiness (CASS and Reliability) and Maintenance Programs to translate reliability and removal data into early warning signals for at-risk components
  • Serve as the primary interface among Global Supply Chain, Engineering, Maintenance Operations, the Technical Library, and AIRMOB leadership on obsolescence resolution
  • Build and maintain the obsolescence tracking dashboard in AMOS, documenting status, mitigation owner, and resolution path for every flagged item
  • Develop cost-benefit analyses for redesign versus repair versus alternate-source decisions and report obsolescence cost exposure to capability area leadership
