title: Software Engineer II, Fintech
description:
About Us

Twitch is the world’s biggest live streaming service, with global communities built around gaming, entertainment, music, sports, cooking, and more. It is where thousands of communities come together for whatever, every day.

We’re about community, inside and out. You’ll find coworkers who are eager to team up, collaborate, and smash (or elegantly solve) problems together. We’re on a quest to empower live communities, so if this sounds good to you, see what we’re up to on LinkedIn and X, and discover the projects we’re solving on our Blog. Be sure to explore our Interviewing Guide to learn how to ace our interview process.

About the Role

Twitch's Enterprise Platform & Technology (EPT) organization is looking for a Software Development Engineer II to build the systems where SAP meets AWS — extending our enterprise ERP with cloud-native services and agentic AI to power Finance and enterprise functions across Twitch and Amazon. This is a hands-on engineering role where you'll work on SAP-side development (ABAP, CDS, RAP, OData) and AWS-native engineering (Lambda, Step Functions, MCP servers, Bedrock, CDK) — owning integrations end-to-end.

You'll work at the intersection of SAP enterprise systems and modern cloud engineering — building AWS-hosted APIs and pipelines that talk to SAP, standing up agentic AI tooling (MCP servers, Bedrock agents, Claude-powered workflows) that automates Finance operations, and shipping production AWS services alongside SAP customizations. The business problems are well understood; how you solve them with SAP + AWS + AI is up to you. We're looking for an SAP developer whose toolkit has grown past the ERP — someone who writes ABAP inside SAP GUI and is just as ready to pick up Python or TypeScript to ship the cloud half of their own integration, and who raises the bar on automation along the way.

You Will

Build in SAP

  • Design, build, and maintain integrations between SAP (S/4HANA, BTP) and downstream systems — owning the full lifecycle from design through operations
  • Write ABAP, SAP HANA SQL, and CDS views to implement business logic, reports, and data transformations within the SAP ecosystem
  • Design, build, and maintain SAP APIs — OData services (SEGW / RAP), RESTful APIs, SOAP web services, and RFC-based interfaces — for consumption by external systems, Fiori apps, and AWS-hosted middleware

Extend it with AWS and agentic AI

  • Build and operate AWS-native services (Lambda, Step Functions, API Gateway, S3, DynamoDB, ECS/Fargate, Amazon ECR) that extend SAP capabilities beyond the traditional ERP boundary
  • Deploy and manage the AWS infrastructure behind your integrations using CDK (TypeScript/Python) — including CI/CD pipelines, IAM roles, VPC/VPCE connectivity to SAP, and multi-environment topology (beta/gamma/prod)
  • Design, build, and ship agentic AI systems on top of your SAP APIs — MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, Bedrock-based agents, and Claude-powered workflows — that automate Finance operations like reconciliations, reporting, variance analysis, and payout workflows
  • Build data pipelines that move financial data between SAP, Redshift, and enterprise applications

Cross-cutting

  • Collaborate with Finance, Accounting, and Tax stakeholders to translate business requirements into technical solutions delivered across SAP and AWS
  • Own production systems end-to-end — deployment, monitoring, incident response, and iterative improvement
  • Improve engineering practices on the team through code reviews, documentation, and mentoring

You Have

SAP

  • 4+ years of hands-on SAP development experience (ABAP, HANA SQL, CDS views, BTP, or SAP integration technologies like BAPIs, RFC)
  • Experience building integrations using File-Based and API-Based (REST, OData, SOAP) patterns
  • Experience with the S/4HANA top-down development approach — CDS views (with associations, annotations, parameters) and AMDP classes to push data processing to HANA from the ABAP layer

AWS and AI

  • Hands-on experience with AWS services (Lambda, S3, Step Functions, DynamoDB, IAM, API Gateway, or similar) — deploying and operating production workloads
  • Proficiency in at least one modern language beyond ABAP — Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, or Java — with a demonstrated track record of shipping production code
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code (CDK, Terraform, or CloudFormation) — writing, deploying, and reviewing IaC in a team setting
  • Demonstrated heavy use of AI tools (Claude, Copilot, Bedrock, or similar) integrated into your daily engineering workflow — code generation, data analysis, automation, and problem-solving

Shared

  • Experience testing and debugging APIs using tools like Bruno or Postman — building request collections, handling authentication flows, and validating response contracts
  • Understanding of OAuth 2.0 authorization flows (authorization code, client credentials) and OpenID Connect (OIDC) for securing API integrations
  • Strong understanding of object-oriented design patterns (Factory, Strategy, Observer, Template Method) and SOLID principles
  • Finance domain knowledge — familiarity with FI/CO, FI/CA, AP, AR or GL

Bonus Points

  • Experience building AI-powered automations or agentic workflows in production — MCP servers, Bedrock agents, LangGraph, or similar
  • Experience building Fiori applications using the RESTful ABAP Programming Model (RAP) — including business object definition, behavior implementation (managed, unmanaged, or hybrid), and service binding/exposure

  • Medical, Dental, Vision & Disability Insurance
  • 401(k)

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
Job Purpose and Impact

The Senior Software Engineer designs, develops & maintains secure, scalable & reliable Salesforce solutions while applying strong software engineering practices throughout the development lifecycle. With minimal supervision, this job collaborates with cross-functional teams to translate business needs into well-designed technical solutions, writes clean & maintainable code, participates in peer code reviews, implements automated testing & CI/CD, troubleshoots complex issues & ensures appropriate security, quality & production readiness. This job makes sound technical decisions that effectively leverage Salesforce platform capabilities while balancing business value, performance, technical debt & long-term maintainability, and demonstrates end-to-end ownership from design through production support & continuous improvement.

Key Accountabilities

  • SOFTWARE ENGINEERING: Designs and develops high-quality software solutions by writing clean, maintainable and efficient codes, that delivers measurable business value.
  • AUTOMATION: Leads the application of internal software deployment platform, methodologies, CI/CD pipelines and tools to automate the deployment process, ensuring smooth and reliable releases.
  • COLLABORATION: Partners and leads cross functional team of product managers, designers and different engineers to gather complex requirements and deliver solutions that meet business needs.
  • TESTING, DEBUGGING and AUTOMATION: Writes and maintains unit tests and integration tests and performs debugging to maintain the quality and performance of the software. Develop, maintain, and execute automated test scripts to support regression, integration, and end-to-end testing.
  • DEFECT MANAGEMENT: Identify, document, and track defects, working with the team to ensure timely resolution and verification.
  • AGILE COLLABORATION: Work closely with Product Owners, Developers, and other QA team members in an Agile/Scrum team to ensure quality is embedded throughout the development lifecycle.
  • CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT: Suggests options for improving the software development and deployment processes and implements the approved standards to improve efficiency and reliability.
  • DOCUMENTATION: Builds and maintains comprehensive documentation for complex software applications, deployment processes and system configurations.
  • TECHNICAL SUPPORT: Provides technical support and troubleshooting for complex issues with deployed applications to ensure minimal downtime and fast resolution.

title: Senior Tax Analyst
description:
Summary

Topstep is seeking a hands-on Senior Tax Analyst to support its growing U.S. and international tax function. This individual contributor role will be a key member of the Finance team and will help build a scalable, well-controlled in-house tax compliance function. The role will initially focus on recurring indirect tax compliance across U.S. sales and use tax, Canada GST/HST, EU VAT/OSS, Australia GST, and New Zealand GST, with responsibility expanding as Topstep registers and becomes compliant in additional jurisdictions. The Senior Tax Analyst will work closely with the Tax Director, Accounting, Treasury, People/Payroll, Legal, Operations, Avalara, and external tax advisors to ensure accurate filings, timely payments, complete journal entries and reconciliations, and strong supporting documentation. A key near-term objective is to support the transition of recurring indirect tax compliance in-house beginning with the January 2027 compliance cycle.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own and support recurring indirect tax compliance across U.S. sales and use tax, Canada GST/HST, EU VAT/OSS, Australia GST, New Zealand GST, and additional jurisdictions as the compliance footprint expands.
  • Support the transition of recurring indirect tax compliance from external providers to the internal tax function beginning with the January 2027 compliance cycle.
  • Prepare monthly and quarterly tax returns and supporting workpapers; ensure filings and related tax payments are completed accurately and on time.
  • Extract, validate, and reconcile tax data from NetSuite, Avalara, payment processors, and other source systems, and investigate differences between tax collected, reported, paid, and general ledger balances.
  • Prepare indirect tax journal entries, accruals, true-ups, and balance sheet account reconciliations, and maintain complete filing and payment support.
  • Maintain the tax compliance calendar, registrations, filing frequencies, portal access, tax IDs, deadlines, and filing/payment confirmations.
  • Coordinate with Avalara and external advisors on filings, data requests, notices, registrations, taxability matters, and open compliance issues.
  • Assist with responses to state, federal, and international tax notices, audits, and information requests, including maintaining an organized record of correspondence and resolutions.
  • Coordinate data gathering and workpaper support for federal, state, and international direct tax compliance, including returns, extensions, estimated payments, and tax provision support performed with external advisors.
  • Provide support to People/Payroll on state tax registrations, payroll tax notices, withholding compliance, and related filings as needed.
  • Research taxability, nexus, filing requirements, and new jurisdiction obligations and support implementation of new registrations and compliance processes.
  • Identify opportunities to improve tax processes, documentation, controls, and automation, including effective use of Avalara, NetSuite, and other tax technology.
  • Partner with Finance, Accounting, Legal, Treasury, People/Payroll, and Operations on tax-related matters and support forecasting, exposure analyses, and other ad hoc tax projects.

Required Qualifications and Key Competencies

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Taxation, or a related field.
  • 4-7 years of progressive tax experience in a corporate, public accounting, or advisory environment.
  • Strong hands-on tax compliance, reconciliation, and Excel skills, with the ability to manage recurring monthly and quarterly deadlines across multiple jurisdictions.
  • Experience with U.S. sales and use tax and/or international VAT/GST compliance strongly preferred.
  • Experience with Avalara and NetSuite, including tax data extraction, reconciliation, or compliance workflows, strongly preferred.
  • Experience supporting corporate income tax compliance and coordinating with external tax advisors preferred.
  • CPA, EA, MST, or similar tax/accounting credential preferred but not required.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills with high attention to detail and accountability for personal deliverables.
  • Ability to operate as a hands-on individual contributor, prioritize competing deadlines, document processes, and collaborate effectively across Finance, Accounting, Legal, Treasury, People/Payroll, Operations, and external advisors.

Company Culture & Perks

  • Topstep is an engaging working environment which ranges from fully remote to hybrid. We foster a culture of collaboration with cameras on during meetings and a robust Slack environment for communication.
  • Holidays provided in accordance with applicable provincial minimum employment standards legislation. Paid time off is front-loaded.
  • Competitive RRSP matching, health, dental, and vision insurance is offered for full time employees.
  • Vacations are encouraged with a bonus for taking 5 consecutive days. Employee referrals are bonused. Topstep offers a food and groceries budget and contributes towards health and wellness.

title: Organ Recovery Coordinator I
description:
Career Opportunity: Organ Recovery Coordinator I in the Tri-State of Kentucky and Surrounding Regions

Are you looking for an opportunity to make a meaningful impact on organ donation by evaluating potential donors, coordinating clinical care, and helping maximize opportunities for successful donation? This role is ideal for an experienced healthcare professional who works well in fast-paced, sensitive, and highly collaborative environments.

As an Organ Recovery Coordinator I, you will evaluate the medical eligibility of potential organ donor referrals and organ imports, coordinate donation activities, and support the comprehensive clinical management of donors. You will collaborate with hospital teams, coordinate organ allocation, recovery, preservation, transportation, and documentation, and serve as a clinical resource for Hospital Services and Family Services. This position reports to the Manager of Recovery Services.

We are committed to supporting the professional growth and development of our team members, with opportunities to expand skills, take on additional responsibilities, and advance within the organization. In this role, you will be expected to consistently perform your work safely, ethically, and in accordance with organizational policies, professional standards, and applicable laws and regulations. Your commitment to safety, integrity, and compassionate care will be essential to supporting donors, their families, healthcare partners, and our mission.

Responsibilities:

  • Respond to donor referrals, complete follow-up evaluations, and determine organ and tissue suitability using LCO, CMS, OPTN/UNOS, AOPO, and CDC guidelines.
  • Apply legal and hospital requirements for death declaration and organ donation, identify the legal next-of-kin, and assess family dynamics and support needs.
  • Clinically manage donors under established protocols and collaborate with hospital teams to support optimal organ function.
  • Coordinate organ allocation, recovery, preservation, transportation, recovery teams, and related specimen collection and labeling.
  • Identify organ-, tissue-, and behavior-specific risk factors and serve as a clinical resource for Hospital Services and Family Services.
  • Maintain accurate, confidential donor records, complete post-recovery documentation and quality control, and support departmental quality-improvement projects.

Qualifications:

  • Associate degree in nursing, respiratory therapy, EMT, paramedic medicine, a related biological science, or certification as a paramedic required.
  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in nursing, respiratory therapy, or a related biological science preferred.
  • Organ recovery coordination or hospital emergency room, intensive care, or surgical experience preferred.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively while demonstrating sound judgment, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to respond sensitively to individual needs and values.
  • Strong computer and data-entry skills, including proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and internet-based systems.
  • Professionalism, discretion, and the ability to maintain a high degree of confidentiality.

The role operates across office and hospital clinical settings and requires lifting to 75 pounds and assisting with donor transfers. Reasonable accommodation may be available.

title: Clinical Scientist - Operations
description:
About Signant Health
At Signant Health, we help bring life-changing treatments to patients faster. We are a global evidence generation company that supports clinical trials with smart technology, scientific expertise, and hands-on operational support — so better data leads to better decisions in healthcare. We embrace AI and advanced technologies to enhance every aspect of what we do, from data analysis to operational efficiency.
Our teams work at the intersection of science, technology, and patient experience, delivering digital solutions powered by AI innovation that make clinical trials more efficient, more accurate, and more accessible around the world. Trusted by leading pharmaceutical companies and CROs, our platforms and services support studies across more than 90 countries and have contributed to hundreds of new drug approvals.
If you are motivated by meaningful work, global impact, and innovation in clinical research and digital health — including the opportunity to work with cutting-edge AI technologies — you will find purpose and opportunity at Signant Health.
About the Role
The Clinical Scientist is a member of the Digital Health Sciences team and serves as a scientific resource for internal and external stakeholders on the use of eCOA and other digital health technologies — including eConsent and sensors/wearables — in clinical trials. This role supports the full lifecycle of commercial and scientific activity: reviewing study protocols to identify requirements, advising on solution design, contributing to pre-sales and bid defense meetings, and providing input to product development and marketing initiatives. The Clinical Scientist also drives thought leadership through research, industry participation, and client-facing scientific consultation.
Key Accountabilities

-Support the commercial team by analyzing study protocols and relevant study documents, documenting requirements, and presenting scientific content in client meetings.
-Advise technical, operations, and client teams on the development of eCOA solutions to ensure solution design meets clinical trial objectives.
-Provide consultation services through special projects addressing client-specific scientific requests or external initiatives.
-Maintain comprehensive knowledge of current industry best practices and regulatory requirements for clinical outcome assessments (COA).
-Stay at the leading edge of eCOA and digital health technologies through participation in industry forums, working groups, and collaboration with clients and Key Opinion Leaders.
-Develop thought leadership materials and scientific content that demonstrate the company's expertise internally and externally.
-Represent Signant Health in the industry through active participation in forums, conferences, webinars, and publications.
-Manage time effectively across multiple concurrent projects.
-Develop training and marketing materials in support of organizational initiatives.

Knowledge, Skills & Attributes
Essential:

-Advanced degree (PhD preferred) in biological science or a healthcare-related field.
-1–3 years of experience in clinical trial technology or a related industry, preferably in a client-facing role.
-In-depth understanding of clinical research and the drug development cycle.
-Knowledge of clinical outcome assessments (COA) and related science, and/or eConsent, EDC, sensors, and wearables.
-Proven ability to multitask, manage time effectively, and deliver in a fast-paced environment.
-Business-driven mindset with an understanding of commercial growth.
-Familiarity with the intersection of technology and science in digital health for clinical trials.
-Proven ability to collaborate effectively across teams and in a matrix environment.
-Ability to develop expertise in new fields through independent research and networking.
-Excellent written and spoken English communication skills.

Desirable:

-Prior experience in commercial pre-award activities such as capabilities presentations, bid defense meetings, and/or solution design and requirements gathering.
-Experience in the development and use of ePRO or eCOA solutions for clinical trials.
-Ability to communicate effectively with clients and across all levels of the organization.

Why Signant Health?
At Signant Health, your work has real impact. Everything we build, support, and deliver helps advance clinical research and bring new treatments to patients faster — improving lives around the world. Our teams combine science, technology, and operational expertise to solve complex clinical trial challenges, and every role contributes to that mission.
We offer a collaborative, global environment where you can grow your career while working alongside experts across clinical, technology, data, and operations, with opportunities to learn, take ownership, and drive meaningful innovation — not just maintain the status quo.
If you are looking for purpose-driven work, smart colleagues, and the opportunity to help shape the future of clinical research and digital health, Signant Health is the place to do it.
At Signant Health, accepting difference isn't enough — we celebrate it, we support it, and we nurture it for the benefit of our team members, our clients, and our community. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and an affirmative action employer, committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or veteran status. Prior to their start date, all new hires are required to be verified through a thorough background check and identity verification to confirm eligibility for employment.
Unsolicited resumes submitted by agencies or third-party recruiters directly to hiring managers or any Signant Health employee will not be considered and will not obligate Signant Health to any fees or terms associated with the submission.

16 - 24 uur | minimaal € 2.337,- en maximaal € 3.212,- (FWG 25, CAO Gehandicaptenzorg) | contract onbepaalde tijd

Jouw werkplek: Nieuw Buitenzorg, waar ieder verhaal telt

In een fijne woonwijk van Leiderdorp vind je Nieuw Buitenzorg. Een moderne, ruime locatie met zes woningen en een eigen dagbesteding. In totaal wonen hier vijftig mensen met EMB. Zij krijgen ondersteuning op het gebied van zorg, beleving en welzijn. De woningen zijn voorzien van een beleeftuin, snoezelruimtes, aangepaste badkamers en slimme zorgtechnologie. Jij wordt onderdeel van een betrokken team dat samen de (basis)zorg draagt en waar ieders expertise telt. We werken belevingsgericht: wat de cliënt zelf kan, blijft hij of zij zelf doen, met ondersteuning van hulpmiddelen en mensgerichte technologie.

Meer weten over onze arbeidsvoorwaarden? Bekijk ze hier.

Wat je gaat doen: elke dag van betekenis

Als Assistent Begeleider ben jij de steun en toeverlaat in het dagelijks leven van onze bewoners. Je verricht huishoudelijke taken in de appartementen en de gezamenlijke ruimtes, bereidt de avondmaaltijd en zorgt samen met je collega’s voor een fijne, warme sfeer in huis. Je hebt contact met cliënten, beantwoordt hun vragen en stemt je werkzaamheden af met de begeleiders. Bij ziekte of vakantie vervang je elkaar, zodat het team altijd op elkaar kan rekenen.

  • Je bereidt de avondmaaltijd en zorgt voor gezelligheid aan tafel;
  • Je hebt oog voor de wensen en behoeften van de cliënten en draagt bij aan een huiselijke sfeer;
  • Je werkt samen met begeleiders en stemt taken goed af;
  • Je springt bij waar nodig en vervangt collega’s bij ziekte of vakantie;
  • Je denkt mee over activiteiten en projecten die het leven van de bewoners verrijken.

Wat deze rol bijzonder maakt

  • Je werkt in een huiselijke, moderne omgeving met veel licht en ruimte;
  • Je krijgt volop ruimte voor eigen inbreng en het ontwikkelen van jouw talenten;
  • Je maakt deel uit van een team waar samenwerking en vertrouwen centraal staan;
  • Je werkt belevingsgericht: de wensen en verhalen van de cliënt zijn het vertrekpunt;
  • Je draagt bij aan een warme, veilige plek waar bewoners zichzelf kunnen zijn.

Wat je krijgt

  • Een contract voor onbepaalde tijd, 16-24 uur per week;
  • Salaris volgens FWG 25 cao Gehandicaptenzorg: € 2.337,- en maximaal € 3.212,- bruto per maand (o.b.v. 36 uur);
  • Extra toeslagen voor onregelmatige diensten;
  • Volop ruimte voor eigen ontwikkeling, coaching en trainingen;
  • Faciliteiten om goed in je vel te zitten, van leefstijlchecks tot timemanagement;
  • Een team dat het beste uit elkaar haalt en waar je mag zijn wie je bent.

Bekijk hier alle arbeidsvoorwaarden.

Wat je meebrengt

  • Je hebt bij voorkeur een afgeronde mbo-opleiding niveau 2;
  • Je hebt affiniteit of ervaring met de doelgroep ouder wordende cliënten met een verstandelijke beperking;
  • Je bent een aanpakker en flexibel in je werkzaamheden;
  • Je bent positief, open en beschikt over een gezonde dosis humor;
  • Je werkt graag samen en hebt oog voor de mens achter de cliënt.

Waarom werken bij Nieuw Buitenzorg & Philadelphia?

Bij Philadelphia draait het om samen groeien, ontwikkelen en het beste uit elkaar halen. Nieuw Buitenzorg is een plek waar je samen met collega’s bouwt aan een warme, veilige thuisbasis voor mensen die dat het hardst nodig hebben. Hier krijg je de ruimte om jezelf te zijn, nieuwe ideeën in te brengen en écht verschil te maken. We zijn nieuwsgierig naar jouw kijk op het leven, want juist alle verschillende perspectieven, achtergronden en inzichten maken dat we onze cliënten optimaal kunnen ondersteunen.

Interesse?

Zie jij jezelf al werken als Assistent Begeleider bij Nieuw Buitenzorg? Vertel ons waarom jij bij ons past. Heb je vragen? Bel of stuur een WhatsApp naar Cem Canan (Corporate Recruiter bij Philadelphia) op 06 - 27 25 40 36.

We heten je van harte welkom bij Philadelphia om wie je bent. Het recruitmentteam van Philadelphia werkt zonder tussenkomst van bureaus.

title: SVP, Consultant Relations
description:
About Lantern

Lantern is the specialty care platform connecting people with the best care when they need it most. By curating a Network of Excellence comprised of the nation's top specialists for surgery, cancer care, infusions and more, Lantern delivers excellent care with significant cost savings to employers and their workforces. Lantern also pairs members with a dedicated care team, including Care Advocates and nurses, for the entirety of their care journey, helping them get back to good health, back to their families and back to work. With convenient access to specialists nationwide, Lantern means quality care is within driving distance for most. Lantern is trusted by the nation's largest employers to deliver care to more than 6 million members across the country. Learn more about us at lanterncare.com.

SVP, Consultant Relations

The SVP, Head of Consultant Relations will be responsible for executing Lantern's consultant relations strategy through named ownership of our major consulting and brokerage house relationships. This team both educates on the Lantern value proposition and differentiators for our surgery, cancer, and infusion care products, while simultaneously gathering insight and feedback to help Lantern continuously refine our messaging and support for our consultant partners. The team also partners closely with leaders from Sales and Client Success on relevant consultant-led client growth and expansion opportunities.

Consultant Relations creates value primarily by being embedded in live deals and by building deep, durable relationships at both the national and local level — not by generating outreach volume on its own. The Head of the Consultant Relations team will continue to build out the account ownership model, metrics, supporting processes, and roles and responsibilities for the function based on business needs, and will be accountable for the success of the function. They are responsible for ensuring we build and execute on named account plans and coverage across the major houses, that escalations are routed appropriately so the team's capacity is focused on proactive relationship management, and that we have a regular cadence to report out on results against the plan to the Commercial Leadership Team.

What We Learned From Our Recent Internal Review

We recently completed a structured interview series across CR staff, sales leadership, and senior executives on the state of the function. The de-identified findings below are the starting point for this role, not a fixed set of answers — we want this leader's own point of view on how to act on them.

  • Diffuse ownership is a live failure mode. Several interviewees independently described a “nobody owns [major house]” problem — large, high-influence consulting and brokerage houses with no single accountable relationship owner inside Lantern. Named-house ownership, with a cap of roughly 1–2 houses per person, is the model we're building toward.
  • Escalation drag crowds out proactive work. CR's time has been disproportionately consumed by reactive escalation handling. Routing escalations outside CR is a near-term priority so the team's capacity goes toward proactive house management.
  • Relationships build through deal involvement, not cold outreach. Trust with consultants compounds through being embedded in live deals — not through relationship-management touchpoints disconnected from the pipeline.
  • Activity-based KPIs are broadly rejected. Top-of-funnel and activity metrics (meetings held, touches logged) were almost universally dismissed as the wrong way to measure CR, in favor of outcome- and relationship-health-based measurement.
  • Coverage gaps are live, not hypothetical. Texas/Southeast and public sector/labor are both currently underserved segments and an active priority for this role to address.
  • Team-based compensation has been the load-bearing mechanism preventing turf conflict between CR and core sales in the current hybrid model — an important constraint to preserve or deliberately redesign.
  • CR-touched deals skew larger but win at a lower rate. We don't yet know whether that reflects a routing artifact (CR gets pulled into harder, larger, more contested deals) or an execution issue — an open analytical question this leader will be expected to help answer.

Location: Remote, USA (50% Travel)

Responsibilities:

The Consultant Relations function is instrumental to winning in the marketplace and to the quality of Lantern's deals, not just their volume. Through named ownership of major consulting and brokerage houses, and by staying embedded in active deals through the sales lifecycle, the team builds the trust that makes our consultant/brokerage channel a top referral source. Key responsibilities for the team include:

  • Owning named house relationships: building deep, accountable relationships at both the national and local market level — with clear, named ownership of each major house, generally capped at 1–2 houses per person — allowing us to influence and educate the intellectual capital point of view while driving business referrals locally.
  • Staying embedded in deals: relationship value is realized by being part of live deals alongside Sales and Solutions Consulting — tailoring deal strategy and leveraging consultant/broker relationships to gain insight and influence decision factors — rather than through standalone outreach.
  • Developing content: in partnership with the product marketing and sales enablement team, specific to consultants in general and further tailored to each firm when relevant.
  • Educating the marketplace: building awareness around the category (surgery COEs and cancer support) and how to evaluate solutions in this space.
  • Growing the business: improving Lantern's win rate with each consulting/brokerage firm and the quality of opportunities they bring to the table, not simply the number of proposals generated.
  • Closing active coverage gaps: building out dedicated coverage in currently underserved segments, including Texas/Southeast and public sector/labor.
  • Managing escalations deliberately: partnering with Sales and Client Success so that reactive, non-strategic escalations are routed outside CR — freeing the team's bandwidth for proactive house management.
  • Identifying opportunities for improvement: both within and outside of the consultant relations mandate, and where appropriate, how to address them.
  • Establishing strong cross-functional relationships: by working closely with sales, solutions consulting, client success, analytics, clinical, marketing, network, member services and other related functions to ensure a “one team” approach.

Goals and Metrics

Success for the function is measured primarily by the health and outcomes of named house relationships — not by top-of-funnel activity volume.

  • Relationship health and account coverage: success will be measured by the depth, breadth, and health of named relationships across our major consulting and brokerage houses.
  • Deal outcomes: win rate and deal quality on opportunities where CR is embedded, alongside overall net ACV growth across both net-new logos and existing business expansion.
  • Escalation load: a declining share of the team's time spent on reactive escalations, freeing capacity for proactive relationship-building.

Other metrics will include engagement and impact on qualified opportunities for new and existing clients, and the team's progress building out a durable, outcome-based measurement framework.

Ideal Candidate Qualities

The candidate is required to meet the below requirements:

  • 15+ years of professional experience working with employer health care benefits, either in health and benefits consulting and/or in a client- or consultant-facing role within a health care solution/vendor.
  • Strong management experience with the demonstrated ability to build, mentor and lead a high performing team, and to foster a culture of continuous improvement, professional development, and accountability.
  • Deep relationships and credibility across one or more of the top consulting/brokerage firms, ideally from having already done a CR-type, consultant-facing role (not solely a background in consulting itself) — our experience is that this profile builds a network and sales instinct that a straight consulting-to-CR conversion often lacks.
  • Experience designing or operating a named-account or portfolio-ownership model — with clear accountability per account or territory — in a relationship-management or sales function.
  • Ability to influence client and consultant points of view and decisions with a thoughtful, data-driven perspective, supported by real-life experience.
  • Experience in consultative sales or business development.
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to confidently convey complex information and messages to a broad and diverse audience, both internal and external.
  • Clear understanding of the mechanics of self-funded medical plans and the relationships between health plans/third party administrators, health care providers, and plan sponsors.
  • Effective interpersonal skills with the ability to work independently and within a team environment, both externally facing and behind the scenes.
  • Comfortable working in a high-growth, fast-changing environment; organized, adaptable, diligent, and self-motivated.
  • Passion for Lantern's mission and collaborating with others.
  • Bachelor's degree required.

Preferred qualifications include:

  • 5-10 years as a health and benefits consultant within one of the top consulting/brokerage firms.
  • Strong analytical skills, including experience working with medical claims data to project savings/program impact.
  • Knowledge of the broader ecosystem of point solutions and health care disruptors selling to self-funded employers.
  • Experience building outcome-based (rather than activity-based) performance metrics for a relationship-management or sales team.
  • Ability to adopt a continuous improvement mindset and actively contribute to the processes and procedures of the larger Commercial team.
  • Experience in an early / growth stage business.

Benefits

  • Medical Insurance
  • Dental Insurance
  • Vision Insurance
  • Short & Long Term Disability
  • Life Insurance
  • 401k with company match
  • Paid Time Off
  • Paid Parental Leave

Compensation: Base salary range: $225k–$275k, depending on relevant experience, location, and qualifications.

About You:

  • You use LOGIC in your decision making and understand that progress is critical to making change. You focus on the execution of your content while balancing a fast-paced environment and you take the time to celebrate both the small & big wins.
  • INCLUSION is a core tenant of your personal beliefs. A diverse and inclusive environment is incredibly important to you. You understand and desire to be a part of a diverse team with different experiences and perspectives & you cherish the differences in each individual that you interact with.
  • You have the GRIT, drive and ambition to tackle big problems. Big problems require big ideas and a team that supports new ideas.
  • You care deeply for your customers are driven to keep HUMANITY in all decisions. Your customers aren’t just the individuals using your product. They are the driving factor in your motivation to make a change.
  • Integrity guides you in life. Focusing on the TRUTH vs. giving people the answers they want to hear.
  • You thrive in a Team Environment. Collaboration is key in innovation and creating change.

These pillars of LIGHT are a reminder to our team that we are making a difference by providing guidance and support in navigating the often complex and confusing landscape of healthcare. We hope that through this LIGHT, individuals can find their way to the best care, resources, and support they need to get back to life.

If this sounds like you, we would love to connect to speak further about career opportunities at Lantern.

title: Area Supervisor (Behavioral)
description:
SUMMARY

Position Type: Full-time, exempt, salaried supervisor role.
Rate of Pay: $60,000/year
Scope of Role:

Responsible for managing the services delivered to a designated program or set of programs, and the operation of programs.

Key Responsibilities:

Oversee organization and implementation of direct supports, person-centered planning and implementation, health care, advocacy, stakeholder relations, regulatory compliance, staffing, training, financial management, and maintenance of the physical environment.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform each essential function listed below.

Staff Management:

Recruitment & Hiring: May participate in hiring events as needed and partner with Talent Acquisition to identify hiring needs for Direct Support Professionals and Program Supervisors in consultation with the Area Director.
Meetings & Training: Organizes and implements on-site orientation and training for assigned programs and monitors training compliance and documentation; conducts monthly staff meetings; attends monthly regional meetings and additional meetings as needed.
Employee Scheduling: Designs and monitors schedules to ensure that all shifts are covered; monitors and minimizes overtime.
Performance Evaluation: Conducts rotating performance snapshots and evaluations for direct reports in consultation with the PD’s manager; reviews and approves Direct Support Professional and other staff member’s performance evaluations.
Coaching, Discipline and Termination: Coaches employees, correcting or directing employee behavior where required; may remove employees at their sole discretion in the event of emergency; may recommend and participate in decisions regarding discipline and termination in consultation with the PD’s manager and Human Resources; manages the termination of Direct Support Professionals or other staff members, as necessary.
Employee Safety: Responsible for employee safety and workers’ compensation programs; monitors compliance; and assists in returning employees to work; implements, oversees, and trains employees about safety.

Program Management:

Program Planning: Acts as the QIDP (if required), writes and approves individual program plans; trains and assists appropriate staff members with implementation of plans across all shifts.
Records: Periodically audits individual records and other program documentation for accuracy and completion.
Program Team Meetings: Conducts progress meetings and (quarterly, annual, and/or other) reviews as appropriate or determined by the interdisciplinary team; provides and approves written and progress reviews.
Compliance: Oversees licensing compliance for program services and supports; ensures timely and accurate program documentation; implements the Sevita compliance plan and manages individual rights implementation while maintaining confidentiality and adhering to individual rights standards.
Management of Individuals’ Assets: Implements system and oversees management of individual’s funds and property, assuring safety and accuracy; audits, monitors, and reviews individual’s financial accounts.
Program Stakeholder Relations: Maintains productive and professional relations with individuals, families, case managers and other stakeholders; provides regular communication to stakeholders; and acts as point of contact for all stakeholders; implements satisfaction improvement plans.
Government Relations: Engages in government and community relations; participates in advocacy efforts and ensures preparedness for home visits (e.g., staff, families, legislators).
Incidents: Implements proactive strategies to reduce or eliminate serious incidents; takes immediate steps to correct potential safety concerns and limit the potential for continued concern or incident; reviews all incidents and directs appropriate response; ensures timely incident reporting; and signs and submits all incident reports as required.

Health Care:

Appointments: Oversees coordination of health care appointments and monitors individual attendance.
Medications: Oversees system for medication administration, documentation, and security; reviews documentation for accuracy and completeness; ensures all applicable employees are certified or trained in medication administration.
Medical Supplies and Equipment: Approves purchases of medical supplies and equipment; and ensures training in proper use to all employees.
Dietary planning: Monitors food service in accordance with dietary plans and to meet regulatory compliance; ensures consideration for special needs, occasions, and individual choice; ensures all applicable employees are certified or trained in meal preparation and/or dietary planning.

Financial Management:

Purchasing: Approves purchase of food, supplies and equipment; and reviews and monitors monthly invoices for accuracy and budgetary compliance; attests to company credit card statements and monthly invoices in accordance with company policy.
Billing and utilization: Oversees census, attendance information or other required documentation to assure accurate billing; ensures program documentation is accurate, complete, and compliant; monitors utilization between authorization and provision of services and supports.
Staffing: Monitors staffing hours for budgetary compliance.
Growth: Develops understanding of program growth strategy and supports implementation of growth initiatives within the program

Census Management:

Census Performance: Monitors census performance for their location(s) and escalates potential service disruptions that impact census to the Area Director and Regional Director.
Referrals: Reviews referrals to validate fit for specific locations and identifies and escalates potential barriers to serving individuals to the Area Director and Regional Director; coordinates and prepares for in-person site visits at locations during referral process.
Placements: Coordinates preparations required for expected placements including staffing, funding, home set-up, and safety requirements.

Maintenance:

Vehicles: Ensures vehicles are properly maintained, clean, and safe by consulting with maintenance personnel; implements training procedures for maintenance and safe operation of company-owned vehicles, including reviewing checklists on a regular basis; addresses known safety concerns with employee vehicles or other means of transportation, for the safe transport of individuals.
Housekeeping: Monitors and implements strategies to assure neat, clean, and safe program environments (internal and external); ensures age appropriate and esthetic decoration.
Maintenance and Repair: Oversees environmental safety program; establishes preventive maintenance schedule; maintains furnishings, equipment, and facilities in good repair and compliant with regulatory standards.

Other:

Performs other duties and activities as required, including backfilling roles under your supervision.
Must be available on-call to support staff, find coverage or cover shifts as needed.

Performs other related duties and activities as required.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

Manages the Direct Support Professionals, Program Supervisors and other direct or indirect staff members of the program. Completes performance evaluations, orientation, and training. Makes decisions on employee hires, transfers, promotions, salary changes, discipline, terminations, and similar actions. Resolves employee problems within position responsibilities.

Minimum Knowledge and Skills required for the Job
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or abilities required to perform the job.

Bachelor's degree

Two to three years of behavioral experience.

Other education and experience as required by applicable regulations.

Certificates, Licenses, and Registrations:

Documentation Compliance

The Program Director works at the program location(s) they oversee.

title: Behavior Intervention Specialist
description:

title: Production Washroom Operator
description:
Overview
Performs work as part of a team in an industrial laundry facility. Responsible for the safe, expeditious, and accurate handling of merchandise into and/or out of the laundry facility.
Responsibilities / Essential Functions

Checks all machine safety devices before operating equipment and records and signs the appropriate equipment safety form. If machine does not pass safety inspection, operator will not operate unit, and notifies supervisor.
When loading washer, retrieve sling from storage and maneuvers sling to the washer’s rails and in front of the washer. If loading a dryer, obtain an extracted sling from the overhead feed rail and verifies each batch ticket to avoid mixing lots and batches. Stages similar batches together for maximum product/wash utilization.
Positions washer/dryer in proper loading position (tilted up), removes batch ticket, loads the washer/dryer by untying the bottom cord of sling, forces the items into the washer/dryer cylinder, closes washer/dryer doors, lowers washer/dryer to the horizontal position, selects the appropriate washer/dryer formula, and starts the machine.
Takes the batch ticket and writes the ticket information on the washer/dryer form visually displayed by the machine.
For washer, enters the weight off of the batch ticket into SOFTROL. For dryer, re-ties the sling and transports to hoist staging area.
Unloads washer: opens washer door, tilts washer forward, moves lined cart with clean sling, and removes items from the washer into the cart, places batch tickets on top of items, moves cart to sling raise area, and tilts washer back into load position.
Unloads dryer: opens the front door, ensures items are at the proper moisture levels (if not, re-dry), raises the front-end of the dryer, moves to the rear of the machine, opens the rear door, places the appropriate tub at the dryer opening, removes items from dryer, places batch ticket on top of items, stores in appropriate area, closes rear door, and leaves dryer in tilted position to aid in loading process.
Verifies proper moisture retention of items, carts/tubs are not overload, load items are at proper temperature, all extracted slings are free of excessive water, and all items are properly cooled down.
Identifies any slings with rips or tears and removes them from the system.
Maintains safe and clean work environment, and observes best practices in all production activities.
Other duties as assigned.

Knowledge / Skills / Abilities

Ability to understand all required training, written, and verbal instructions.
Working knowledge of basic math skills.
Good verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Ability to meet attendance schedule.

Working Environment / Safety Requirements

Work is performed in a warehouse setting and regularly exposed to outside weather conditions, extreme heat and cold conditions as well as dust and noise.
Work is based on a shift schedule, and may include weekends.
Overtime required as needed.

Physical Requirements
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Requires the ability to move or maneuver slings or carriers weighing up to 220 lbs.
Requires the ability to move, lift, carry, push, or pull product weighing up to 50 lbs.
Requires bending, reaching, pulling, and pressing at shoulder level and below waist area.
Requires the use of hands for grasping and other manipulations.
Requires standing and walking for long periods of time.

Education
High school degree or equivalent preferred.

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
description:
About Care Access

Care Access is working to make the future of health better for all. With hundreds of research locations, mobile clinics, and clinicians across the globe, we bring world-class research and health services directly to communities that often face barriers to care. We are dedicated to ensuring that every person has the opportunity to understand their health, access the care they need, and contribute to the medical breakthroughs of tomorrow.

With programs like Future of Medicine, which makes advanced health screenings and research opportunities accessible to communities worldwide, and Difference Makers, which supports local leaders to expand their community health and wellbeing efforts, we put people at the heart of medical progress. Through partnerships, technology, and perseverance, we are reimagining how clinical research and health services reach the world. Together, we are building a future of health that is better and more accessible for all.

To learn more about Care Access, visit .

How This Role Makes a Difference

By joining our team as a Senior Machine Learning Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in building cutting-edge AI products that directly impact how new therapies reach patients. We’re looking for an experienced ML engineer who is passionate about turning advanced AI research into scalable, real-world solutions. You thrive on solving complex problems, pay close attention to detail, and consistently seek to automate and improve processes. You shine as a collaborator and excel as an individual contributor, with the courage to tackle challenging problems and the humility to learn and adapt. Your initiative and discipline allow you to thrive while working remotely, and your high degree of empathy and communication skills makes you the kind of colleague everyone wants on their team. As an integral member of our fast-growing organization, you will leverage AI to transform clinical research and improve patient care.

How You'll Make An Impact

  • Build and deploy AI-driven products that accelerate clinical trials and improve patient outcomes. Your work will deliver scalable machine learning solutions to complex, real-world problems in clinical research.
  • Develop advanced ML models and LLM-powered agents for critical use cases like patient recruitment, enrollment forecasting, and study feasibility. You’ll also help expand our AI knowledge base architecture to support these innovative solutions.
  • Leverage modern cloud tools and MLOps best practices to build robust data pipelines and deploy models at scale. You’ll use technologies like Python (and Clojure), AWS services (Athena, Bedrock, SageMaker, etc.), dbt, Prefect, and CI/CD automation with monitoring to ensure models are reliable and up-to-date.
  • Collaborate across teams of data scientists, product managers, designers, engineers, and domain experts to integrate AI capabilities into our platform (including Care Access products). Ensure these AI solutions seamlessly support and enhance clinical research workflows for end-users.
  • Continuously learn and innovate. Stay up-to-date with the latest developments in ML/AI (LLMs, NLP, probabilistic modeling, etc.) and proactively bring new ideas to the team. You’ll have the freedom to experiment with cutting-edge techniques and turn promising prototypes into production features that drive our mission forward.

The Expertise Required

  • Strong programming and data skills: Proficiency in Python and its ML ecosystem (pandas, scikit-learn, TensorFlow/PyTorch), with clean and efficient coding practices. Comfortable working with large datasets, writing complex SQL queries, and leveraging modern data processing frameworks. Experience with functional programming (e.g. Clojure) is a plus but not required.
  • Cloud and MLOps expertise: Experience with modern cloud infrastructure (AWS or similar) and containerization tools like Docker. Familiarity with MLOps best practices such as CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and monitoring model performance/data drift to ensure reliable, scalable deployments.
  • Deep ML/AI knowledge: Strong understanding of machine learning fundamentals (model selection, training, evaluation, feature engineering) and statistical modeling. Familiarity with NLP and large language models is important.

title: Sr. Data Analyst - Monetization (Remote)
description:
Who We Are (Mode.Inc)

Mode is a fast-growing technology company building businesses at the intersection of AI, data, mobile apps, and digital experiences. Our portfolio of mobile apps and digital products reaches 100M+ monthly active users across a global audience. We continue to accelerate growth through product innovation, strategic acquisitions, and emerging business opportunities.

Mode was recognized by Deloitte as the #1 fastest-growing software company in North America on the 2023 Technology Fast 500. Today, we are building our next phase of growth, including expanding Mode's AI and data business and developing direct relationships with companies that can benefit from the data and capabilities we have built.

Our Team and Culture Drive Our Success

Our team is the heart of our culture. We value innovation, collaboration, and curiosity, with a passion for getting things done. We strive to hire and cultivate the best team members and foster a culture of open communication and transparency. We are driven and hard-working but also committed to having fun along the way. We allow OKRs to guide us, assume positive intent, sometimes agree to disagree and commit, honor our commitments, seek to accomplish more with less, and encourage everyone to speak up as our team owns our company’s success.

You can read more about our team and how we work here.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Senior Data Analyst to be the analytical partner to our Monetization team. You’ll own how we measure and grow revenue across our portfolio of mobile apps and web properties, spanning subscriptions, in-app purchases, advertising, and partner offers, and turn that into clear recommendations on pricing, packaging, and revenue mix. The ideal candidate has exceptional SQL and Python skills, hands-on experience with consumer subscription apps, and the rigor to design pricing experiments that hold up.

What You’ll Do

  • Design, build, and maintain common datasets and data pipelines that strengthen self-service analytics and enable data-driven decision making across the organization
  • Improve data quality, accuracy, reliability, and documentation to strengthen self-service analytics
  • Own revenue and monetization metrics across the portfolio, including ARPU/ARPDAU, LTV, trial-to-paid conversion, renewal and churn rates, refunds, and revenue mix by source
  • Design and analyze pricing, packaging, and paywall experiments (price points, trial length, plan structure, paywall placement and copy), and read results with statistical rigor
  • Build subscription cohort and LTV models that inform pricing decisions and feed back into UA bidding and payback targets
  • Analyze ad monetization performance, including eCPM, fill rate, impressions per user, and mediation/bidding setup, and balance ad revenue against retention and user experience
  • Measure the economics of partner offers and rewards, including revenue earned vs. rewards paid out, to keep the rewards model profitable
  • Reconcile revenue data across app stores, subscription platforms, ad networks, and internal systems, and investigate discrepancies
  • Partner with Monetization, Product, and GMs on revenue forecasting, opportunity sizing, and roadmap prioritization
  • Communicate analytical findings through clear, compelling narratives to drive alignment, inform prioritization, and deliver measurable business impact

What You Bring to the Team

  • Analytical excellence to dissect complex, ambiguous problems and uncover actionable insights
  • Solid SQL and Python programming skills, and experience working with large-scale production data
  • Business acumen to translate data and analysis into business impact
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills to effectively collaborate in a highly cross-functional environment
  • 4+ years in analytics, preferred background in monetization, pricing, or revenue analytics for consumer subscription apps & games
  • Experience with LTV modeling and revenue forecasting on subscription and ad monetized apps/games
  • Track record of designing and interpreting pricing or paywall A/B tests, including pitfalls like novelty effects, long conversion windows, and LTV vs. short-term conversion tradeoffs
  • Familiarity with app store subscription mechanics (App Store/Google Play billing, trials, grace periods, renewals, refunds) and subscription platforms (e.g., RevenueCat, Superwall, Adapty)
  • Nice to have: experience with ad mediation experience (AppLovin MAX, ironSource/Unity LevelPlay, AdMob), web checkout or web-to-app payments, rewards or loyalty program economics, Big Data tools (Redshift/Spark/Airflow), dashboarding tools (Looker, Tableau), experiment design, predictive modeling, log analysis, AI, or experience in tech or startup environments

Alignment with Our Core Values:

  • ​​Accountable: You take ownership of your responsibilities, demonstrating trustworthiness and self-discipline. You are consistent in your work, transparent in your actions, and communicate effectively. You follow through on commitments and strive for continuous improvement.
  • Action-driven: Identify what is most important, agree on scope, execute in a timely manner, and drive the greatest impact. You take initiative, roll up your sleeves, and get things done.
  • Caring: You genuinely care about yourself and others, our business and craft, our mission and vision, and are passionate in heart and mind. You understand the importance of our team and strive to create a positive, supportive work environment.
  • Curious: You focus on the ‘why,’ learn and expand your knowledge, explore new ideas, and generally make things better. You're a lifelong learner with a thirst for knowledge and a constant desire to improve.
  • Thorough: Your work is thoughtful, impactful, timely, accurate, and complete. You pay attention to detail, are meticulous, and ensure quality work and compliance.

You’ll Thrive Here If You Are

  • Analytical
  • Pragmatic
  • Curious
  • Communicative
  • Action-Driven
  • Collaborative

Why Join Mode Mobile

  • High ownership and autonomy across business units
  • Direct impact on product, revenue, and user experiences
  • Strong partners across engineering, product, growth, and content
  • Opportunities to shape Mode’s analytics function and data culture
  • A fast-moving, supportive, global remote environment

We Believe in the Following Workplace Norms

  • Allow OKRs to Guide Us
  • Assume Positive Intent
  • Agree to Disagree & Commit
  • Set New Precedents
  • Accomplish More with Less
  • Hold Yourself & Others to High Standards
  • Speak Up
  • Be Resourceful
  • Follow the 80/20 Rule

What We Are Offering

  • We are a 100% remote-first, global company.
  • A competitive compensation package.
  • We offer generous perks & benefits to team members.
  • Participation in the Company's equity plan (for full-time team members).
  • We provide individual bonuses in accordance with our Company Bonus Program.

title: Senior Trim Technician
description:
The Role

In this role you will work to efficiently trim cannabis plants, while creating minimal waste, resulting in a high-quality product that is compliant and ready for sale or processing. This person will be responsible for maintaining and following standard operating procedures. In addition, as a Senior Trim Tech, you will be responsible for training new employees, using our computers systems for inventory and compliance tracking and ensuring quality requirements are met.

Responsibilities

Essential functions:

  • Trim flower from plants in a quick and efficient manner, while ensuring a quality product
  • Trim flower by hand and/or using trimming, sorting and packaging equipment.
  • Maintain a clean and organized work environment
  • Sit and stand for long periods of time while focusing on detail-oriented trimming, as well as post trim upkeep
  • Track the amount of unusable waste for each plant/batch, in addition to usable by-products
  • Demonstrate proficiency with weights, measurements, and math
  • Experience trimming several different strains of cannabis.
  • Maintain open communication with management team and co-workers
  • Train new hires/transfer on standard SOP’s and work instructions in area.
  • Work with inventory management software systems.
  • Other duties as assigned by Supervisor and/or Team Lead

Safety & Compliance:

  • Be aware of hazards in the workspace.
  • Retain and understand department specific training.
  • Report safety incidents/ concerns and comply with follow-up actions.
  • Be compliant with area safety requirements, state regulations and PPE requirements.
  • Follow GMP, biosecurity, sanitation or other quality and compliance requirements.
  • Perform record keeping accurately and completely as directed by a lead or supervisor.
  • Maintain and calibrate tools, equipment and machinery as directed by a lead or supervisor.
  • Report and escalate safety & quality concerns.

Qualifications

  • Effective time-management skills and ability to multi-task
  • Ability to work well with others while also completing individually assigned tasks
  • Prior cannabis experience not required

Working Conditions

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to perform reaching, grasping, bending, stooping, talking, hearing, seeing and repetitive motions.
  • Must be able to sit and/or stand for extended periods of time while maintaining focus.
  • Must be able to lift, carry, and balance up to 50 pounds (and up to 100 pounds with assistance) AND must be able to do so with extreme care and caution when working with product.

title: Senior Data Warehouse and Integration Engineer
description:
About Goods & Services

Goods & Services is a product design and engineering company.

We solve mission-critical challenges for some of the world’s largest enterprises, with deep expertise in highly regulated industries—including life sciences and financial services. Our design-led approach allows us to apply cutting-edge capabilities in AI, Data and Hardware Engineering to companies of any size.

Headquartered in the United States, we operate regional development centers in Mexico and the United Kingdom. This global footprint—anchored by our nearshore model—enables us to deliver at scale with the speed, efficiency, and cultural alignment our clients expect.

At Goods and Services, we value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and welcome qualified applicants from all backgrounds.

About the job

Goods & Services is looking for a Senior Data Warehouse and Integration Engineer responsible for database engineering, data warehouse architecture and support, data integration, reporting support, production troubleshooting, and technical delivery. This role requires someone who can independently own complex DB/data work from investigation and design through production completion and ongoing support. The biggest need is database/data integration ownership and production troubleshooting, followed by data warehouse architecture and reporting. The role needs someone to be comfortable with the existing on-prem/Microsoft environment while also helping us move toward more modern Azure-based solutions.

What you’ll do:

  • Design, develop, maintain, and troubleshoot SQL Server databases, stored procedures, views, jobs, and related database objects.
  • Design and support enterprise data warehouse architecture, data models, schemas, and data flows.
  • Evaluate and improve data warehouse structure, scalability, performance, and maintainability.
  • Support data warehouse production operations, including failures, performance issues, data quality issues, and downstream dependencies.
  • Support and troubleshoot SSIS, ETL processes, integrations, APIs, files, feeds, and scheduled data processes.
  • Design reliable data movement between source systems, staging layers, data warehouse environments, and reporting platforms.
  • Investigate production database, data warehouse, integration, and reporting issues and drive them to root cause and resolution.
  • Reconcile report and data discrepancies against source systems.
  • Review database, warehouse, and integration changes for dependencies and downstream impact.
  • Support query performance, data integrity, reliability, and production stability.
  • Define and execute technical testing for database, warehouse, and integration changes.
  • Support DEV, TEST/UAT, and PROD deployments, including rollback planning where needed.
  • Build monitoring, failure detection, retry, and recovery processes for automated integrations and warehouse processes.
  • Maintain documentation for critical databases, warehouse architecture, integrations, jobs, reports, data flows, and support procedures.
  • Work directly with Development, BA, PM, Applications, Infrastructure, and Support teams.
  • Maintain clear status, target dates, blockers, risks, and next steps for assigned work.
  • Escalate risks and dependencies early instead of allowing work to remain indefinitely in investigation.
  • Ensure completed technical work is tested, validated, documented, deployed, and supportable.

What you’ll need:

  • Strong Microsoft SQL Server experience
  • Advanced T-SQL
  • Data warehouse design and architecture
  • Dimensional modeling and enterprise data modeling
  • Data warehouse support and production troubleshooting
  • Stored procedures, views, functions, and SQL Agent jobs
  • SSIS / SSISDB or equivalent ETL experience
  • ETL architecture and data pipeline design
  • Data integration and troubleshooting
  • Data reconciliation and reporting support
  • Query performance and optimization
  • Production database support
  • Root cause analysis
  • Data lineage and dependency analysis
  • APIs, files, feeds, and system integrations
  • Production deployment and change management
  • Azure data services where applicable

Nice to have:

  • Enterprise data warehouse environments
  • Complex operational, financial, or regulatory reporting
  • Multi-system integrations
  • Large production SQL environments
  • Data warehouse modernization or redesign initiatives

title: Associate Media Director
description:
At SixSpeed, we believe great media is about more than reaching the right audience. It's about understanding people, connecting the dots, and making smarter decisions that move our clients' businesses forward.

As our Associate Media Director, you're a strategic leader who knows how to bring the big picture together. You understand how audiences, channels, creative, data, and business objectives work together to create meaningful results. You're equally comfortable developing a media strategy, digging into campaign performance, challenging a recommendation, or sitting across the table from a client.

You'll lead media strategy across a portfolio of clients, helping our teams deliver smart, integrated work that drives business outcomes. You're a trusted partner to clients, a resource for your team, and someone who is always looking for ways to make the work better.

You're also a people leader. You'll coach and develop our media team, raise the bar for strategic thinking and execution, and work closely with our VP of Media to continue building SixSpeed's media capabilities. You know when to step in, when to challenge, and when to give your team the room to run.

This is a hybrid role based at our Minneapolis office, and candidates must be local to the Twin Cities area, in office at least three days per week.

THE TASK AT HAND

  • Lead the strategy. Develop and oversee integrated media strategies across a portfolio of clients, connecting audience insights, business objectives, creative thinking, channel selection, and measurement to drive meaningful results.
  • Be a true client partner. Build trusted relationships, bring proactive recommendations to the table, challenge conventional thinking, and help clients see opportunities they might not have considered.
  • Own the quality of the work. Oversee media planning, buying, activation, optimization, and measurement to ensure our strategies are sound, our execution is strong, and our investments are working as hard as possible.
  • Turn data into decisions. Connect performance data, audience insights, and market trends to understand what's working, what's not, and what we should do next. Push beyond reporting results to finding ways to improve them.
  • Build a stronger team. Lead, coach, and develop media team members, helping them grow their strategic thinking, technical expertise, confidence, and leadership skills.
  • Make the department better. Partner with the VP of Media to strengthen our processes, tools, partnerships, and capabilities. Identify opportunities to work smarter, improve consistency, and continue evolving what Media brings to SixSpeed.
  • Help grow the business. Identify opportunities to expand existing client relationships and play an active role in new business strategy, pitch development, and presentations.
  • Stay ahead of what's next. Explore emerging platforms, technologies, data, and measurement solutions, and help determine which opportunities are worth testing and investing in.
  • Connect the agency. Work closely with Strategy, Creative, Account, Analytics, and other teams to make sure media is part of the conversation early and contributes to stronger, more integrated ideas.

WHO YOU ARE

  • You bring 7–10+ years of experience in media strategy, planning, buying, optimization, and measurement across digital and traditional channels.
  • You've spent at least 3 years leading and developing media professionals and know how to coach, challenge, and empower a team to do their best work.
  • You know the media landscape inside and out, from Paid Search, Paid Social, and Programmatic to traditional media, emerging platforms, and measurement solutions. You also have hands-on, in-platform experience and aren't afraid to dig in, troubleshoot, or help your team solve a problem.
  • You're a strategic thinker who understands how to connect media decisions to broader business objectives. You don't just recommend channels. You understand the role each one plays and why it deserves investment.
  • You're analytical and financially minded. You know your way around a media budget, understand forecasting and pacing, and can turn complicated performance data into a clear story about what's happening, why it matters, and what we should do next.
  • You're confident in front of clients. You can build credibility with senior stakeholders, communicate a strong point of view, navigate difficult conversations, and push for better outcomes.
  • You know how to lead without needing to control every detail. You set clear expectations, ask smart questions, hold people accountable, and trust your team to deliver.
  • You're naturally collaborative. You understand that the best work doesn't happen in silos and know how to bring different disciplines together to solve a problem.
  • You see opportunities beyond the immediate ask. Whether it's improving performance, testing a new approach, growing a client relationship, or contributing to a new business pitch, you're always thinking about what's next.
  • You're curious about the future of media, but you don't chase shiny objects. You understand the difference between something that's interesting and something that can actually make a difference for our clients.
  • You're organized, proactive, and a strong communicator. You can balance big-picture thinking with the day-to-day realities of agency life, keep multiple priorities moving, and help your team deliver great work.
  • You have a bachelor's degree, preferably in Advertising, Marketing, Business, Communications, or a related field.

WHO WE ARE

To be what others can’t, you have to do what they won't. We are SixSpeed, a full-service advertising agency that is employee-owned, audience-first, and built to deliver big ideas at speed. We're here to make the world's most adventurous brands impossible to imitate.

This role offers a salary range of $90,000 to $110,000* per year.

*Don’t let this range drive your decision to apply. Actual compensation packages are based on the level of skill and experience each candidate brings to their role. Similarly, there may be a more senior or junior position available that would be a better fit with your expertise. The final offer will be determined based on the candidate's experience, skills, and qualifications as they relate to the requirements of the position.

Inspect track conditions and switch points to identify any issues affecting safe operation.

Communicate with train crews and yard personnel to ensure coordinated rail movements.

Follow all safety procedures, including proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE).

Maintain awareness of surroundings and potential hazards in a high-traffic rail environment.

2-3 years of rail experience desired
Switching or conductor experience preferred
Valid driver’s license
Ability to always follow safety requirements and practices
Reliable, punctual and a strong work ethic
Ability to work outdoors in all weather conditions
Ability to lift up to 75lbs
Ability to climb ladders and stairs both off and on railcars
Must pass a pre-employment background verification, physical and drug screening.

The Federal Rail Administration sets and enforces safety regulations and standards for railroad operations. Use of cannabis is strictly prohibited. If applicable for the position you are applying to, and if you are offered the position, you will have to take and pass a drug screen.

Open availability

Previous experience in rail yard or switching operations.

title: (Coördinerend) Begeleider EMB/OUD Vierhouten
description:

Op de locatie Bospad 🌳werk je in een kleinschalige woonomgeving in het bos. Een plek waar bewoners zich veilig mogen voelen en waar jij als begeleider/ coördinerend begeleider het verschil maakt in de kleine momenten.

Werken op Bospad 🌿.

Bospad is in het najaar van 2024 geopend en bestaat uit 6 kleinschalige woningen 🏘️ en een eigen dagcentrum. Je werkt met bewoners met een ernstig meervoudige beperking en/of ouder wordende bewoners (16 tot 80 jaar). Iedere bewoner heeft een eigen ritme, manier van communiceren en zorgvraag. Jij sluit daarop aan met aandacht, rust en duidelijke begeleiding. We werken op Bospad integraal samen met de dagbesteding. Dat betekent: samen kijken wat iemand nodig heeft, zowel thuis als overdag.

Wat ga je doen? 🌟

Je organiseert alles wat er voor de bewoners op medisch en administratief vlak geregeld moet worden. In de omgang met collega's heb je een coachende en faciliterende rol. Je weet je een goede werksfeer te creëren waarbij positiviteit en openheid voorop staan.

In jouw werk: 🧩
