title: Energy Marshal
description:
About Overwatch Mission Critical
Overwatch is a service-disabled Veteran-owned small business (SDVOB) certified through the National Veterans Business Development Council (NVBDC), offering construction professional services, talent acquisition, and general contractor services for the mission-critical infrastructure industry.
Our mission is the construction and management of state-of-the-art data centers with the precision and reliability this industry demands. From high-end engineers to seasoned professionals, we deploy the people you need to get your data center off the ground. At Overwatch, it's more than a job. It's a purpose.

Overview
We're looking for an Energy Marshal to lead hazardous energy control and Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) operations on a major data center construction project. Data centers are among the most energy dense construction environments. This role is the central authority for safe isolation, verification, and energization of electrical and mechanical systems as the facility moves through construction, startup, and commissioning.

What You'll Do
  • Manage the project's LOTO program, ensuring all isolations are planned, documented, and properly executed.
  • Maintain the master energy log and communicate real-time energy status to all trades.
  • Review MOPs, SOPs, commissioning scripts, and work plans to identify energy hazards and required controls.
  • Coordinate safe energization sequencing with electrical, commissioning, and operations teams.
  • Conduct field audits, verify PPE and arc-flash boundaries, and enforce NFPA 70E compliance.
  • Serve as stop-work authority for any unsafe energy-related activity.
  • Provide training and guidance to subcontractors on hazardous-energy procedures.
  • Oversee and enforce safe energization and LOTO procedures on site.
  • Coordinate with commissioning teams, contractors, and client representatives.
  • Review and approve switching procedures and method statements.
  • Maintain strict compliance with site safety standards and energization protocols.
  • Monitor energization activities and ensure risk mitigation at all stages.
  • Lead daily briefings related to energy control and safety.

What You Bring
  • 5–10+ years of electrical experience in mission-critical, industrial, or data center environments.
  • Strong understanding of NFPA 70E, OSHA 1910/1926, and hazardous-energy control programs.
  • Experience with MV/LV systems, UPS, generators, switchgear, ATS, and mechanical equipment.
  • Ability to read one-lines, interpret commissioning documentation, and coordinate across multiple teams.
  • Confident communicator who can lead safety discussions and enforce standards in high-risk environments.
  • Proven experience as an Energy Marshal (or similar role) on data center or mission-critical projects.
  • Experience working on hyperscale or large-scale construction/commissioning sites.
  • Relevant safety certifications (e.g., OSHA, NFPA 70E preferred).
  • Excellent communication and coordination skills.

Required Skills & Experience
  • 5+ years of Data Center or Mission Critical Construction experience (ability to interpret blueprints, electrical one-lines, construction drawings, etc.).
  • Energy isolations.
  • Energy tracking.
  • MEP systems (power distribution, lighting, grounding, fire alarms, security, life safety, and control systems).
  • Experience with paralleling switchgear, redundant UPS systems, DC battery strings, multi-source electrical utility switchgear, standby diesel generators, etc.
  • Building management systems and automation, electrical controls & frameworks.
  • Substation, transmission, and distribution.
  • Experience in the control of hazardous energy in complex mission-critical infrastructure.
  • NFPA 70E, NEN 3840, NEN 3140, National Electrical Code (NEC), and/or OSHA requirements as they relate to data center best practices.

Sub Specialty Area
  • Lead the LOTO Program

Required Training and Certifications
  • NFPA 70E
  • NEN 3840
  • NEN 3140
  • National Electrical Code (NEC)
  • And/or OSHA requirements as they relate to data center best practices.

Required Experience
  • 5–10+ years of electrical experience in mission-critical, industrial, or data center environments.

Driver’s License Requirement
For roles that require on-site presence or travel between work locations as an essential function of the position, candidates must possess and maintain a valid driver’s license appropriate for the role and be eligible to operate a motor vehicle in accordance with applicable laws.

Communication Skills
Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively in a professional work environment, including preparing written reports and documentation, conveying information clearly to team members, clients, and stakeholders, and responding appropriately to verbal and written communications related to job duties.

Physical Requirements and Work Environment
This position operates primarily in an active data center construction environment, encompassing both indoor and outdoor work settings. The role requires the physical ability to perform essential job functions safely and effectively in a dynamic environment that includes ongoing construction activity and evolving site conditions.
The work environment includes areas and temporary structures owned, leased, or controlled by third parties over which Overwatch may have limited or no control. Because the project remains under construction, certain areas of the site — including access routes, staging zones, and temporary structures — may not yet be fully ADA-compliant until construction is complete or those third-party areas are finalized.

Physical Requirements
  • Must be able to walk, stand, stoop, twist, bend, and climb stairs or ladders for extended periods while navigating uneven, unpaved, or obstructed terrain.
  • Must be able to lift, carry, push, or pull up to 50 pounds on an occasional basis.
  • Must be able to drive between job sites and access all areas of an active construction zone, including raised platforms, scaffolding, and confined spaces.
  • Must be able to tolerate exposure to outdoor weather conditions, dust, and construction-related noise, vibrations, and odors.
  • Must be able to communicate effectively with contractors, engineers, and site personnel, and maintain situational awareness in high-activity environments.
  • Personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hats, safety vests, hearing protection, and steel-toe boots, is required.
  • Must have sufficient visual acuity to read drawings, specifications, and safety signage, and to observe site activity.

Work Environment:
Work is performed primarily in and around active construction areas, which may include unfinished buildings, temporary field offices, staging areas, and partially completed infrastructure. These locations may contain uneven surfaces, limited accessibility, and other conditions typical of construction projects prior to final completion. Overwatch does not control and cannot modify accessibility conditions within areas, facilities, or temporary structures owned or managed by third parties.

Reasonable Accommodation
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position, provided such accommodations do not create safety hazards, impede essential mobility within active work zones, or require modification of facilities not owned or controlled by Overwatch.

Benefits
We offer a competitive salary and benefits package, including health insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, 401(k) plan, and paid time off. Relocation assistance is available to support candidates transitioning to the location.

OVERWATCH is committed to creating a diverse work environment and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. OVERWATCH considers candidates regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status.

title: Senior Business Consultant
description:
The Senior Business Consultant is the strategic lead for the knowledge management workstream. This person owns the Requirements Matrix, sets the direction of the discovery effort, and is accountable for the decision-grade output the client will use to determine whether Genesys Cloud can carry their knowledge management requirements or whether a gap justifies a broader tool evaluation.

This is a senior, client-facing advisory role. The successful candidate will spend their time with business owners, contact centre operations leaders, and vendor technical teams, and will be the person in the room when the client asks "can the platform actually do this, and what will it cost us to run it?"

Responsibilities:

  • Own the Requirements Matrix. Drive the matrix to completion through structured discovery with business lines, operations, and the contact centre. Establish a clear, traceable, prioritised set of knowledge management requirements that can survive scrutiny from both the client and the vendor.
  • Set and guide the overall discovery strategy. Define the discovery approach, sequence the workshops and interviews, identify the right stakeholders across each business line, and keep the workstream aligned to the client's three target outcomes — operational improvement, expanded self-service, and agent enablement.
  • Map requirements line-by-line against Genesys Cloud AI capability. Take the Phase 1 Requirements Matrix and assess each requirement against the native Genesys Cloud knowledge management and AI feature set — knowledge surfacing, semantic search, agent assistance, summarisation and virtual agents. Document what the platform supports natively, what it supports with configuration or workaround, and what it cannot support. Identify which gaps are acceptable trade-offs and which are material enough to justify looking beyond the approved-vendor scope.
  • Gather and model total cost of ownership, including AI token consumption. Collect the licensing, token allocation, configuration, integration, content migration, and ongoing administration cost inputs. Model what each AI capability costs to run at full agent population scale against the client's allocated-token fair-usage terms, and flag the usage threshold at which a licence change becomes financially necessary. This is one of the most commercially consequential pieces of analysis in the engagement.
  • Compile the evaluation criteria and author the Tool Evaluation Report. Define weighted, defensible evaluation criteria with the client. Produce the Tool Evaluation Report as the primary decision artefact — findings, capability assessment, TCO, risks, and a clear recommendation.
  • Write the Governance Playbook. Document how knowledge will be created, reviewed, approved, published, versioned, retired, and audited. Define roles, review cycles, quality standards, escalation paths, and the metrics by which knowledge health will be measured on an ongoing basis.
  • Design templates and best practices. Produce the article templates, writing standards, style guidance, and authoring best practices that content owners will use day to day — written for a government environment with plain-language, accessibility, and official-languages obligations in mind.
  • Observe and assess proofs of concept. Participate in PoC sessions, test requirements against what is demonstrated rather than what is claimed, and feed findings back into the evaluation. Apply the client's established pilot pattern — demonstrate the capability, assess the process and operating changes it requires, then execute those changes — rather than treating feature enablement as the end point.
  • Act as the client-facing lead for the workstream. Provide regular status, risk, and decision reporting to the client's transformation lead and to Miratech and Bell programme leadership.
  • 10+ years in management consulting, business consulting, or enterprise transformation, with a substantial portion of that time focused on knowledge management, content operations, or contact centre operations.
  • Demonstrated experience leading a requirements gathering and vendor or tool evaluation effort end to end, through to a written recommendation that an executive used to make a decision.
  • Hands-on working knowledge of enterprise knowledge management platforms and KM administration — configuration, content architecture, permissions, publishing workflow, and reporting. Experience with more than one platform is strongly preferred.
  • Working understanding of contact centre AI capability and its dependency on knowledge quality — knowledge surfacing, semantic search, interaction summarisation, agent assistance and virtual agents. The successful candidate must be able to explain to a business audience why content structure determines AI accuracy.
  • Familiarity with consumption-based AI licensing and the ability to model cost at scale.
  • Proven ability to build a TCO model from incomplete inputs and defend the assumptions behind it.
  • Exceptional written output. This role produces the Tool Evaluation Report and the Governance Playbook; writing quality is a primary selection criterion, and candidates should expect to provide a redacted writing sample.
  • Experience operating in a large, regulated, process-heavy organisation — government, financial services, healthcare, or utilities.
  • Eligible to obtain and hold a Government of Canada security clearance.

Nice to have:

  • Direct hands-on experience with Genesys Cloud CX and Genesys Cloud AI — knowledge base administration, knowledge authoring and optimisation tooling, agent assistance, or bot flows. This is the strongest single differentiator between candidates.
  • Experience evaluating an incumbent platform against requirements where the commercial outcome was constrained — the ability to produce a credible assessment when “choose a different tool” is not initially on the table.
  • Bilingual English/French.
  • Certification in a recognised KM or service management framework (KCS, KMI, ITIL, Lean Six Sigma).

We offer:

  • Culture of Relentless Performance: join an unstoppable technology development team with a 99% project success rate and more than 30% year-over-year revenue growth.
  • Competitive Pay and Benefits: enjoy a comprehensive compensation and benefits package, including health insurance, language courses, and a relocation program.
  • Growth Mindset: reap the benefits of a range of professional development opportunities, including certification programs, mentorship and talent investment programs, internal mobility and internship opportunities.
  • Global Impact: collaborate on impactful projects for top global clients and shape the future of industries.
  • Welcoming Multicultural Environment: be a part of a dynamic, global team and thrive in an inclusive and supportive work environment with open communication and regular team-building company social events.
  • Social Sustainability Values: join our sustainable business practices focused on five pillars, including IT education, community empowerment, fair operating practices, environmental sustainability, and gender equality.

* Miratech is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other protected status under applicable law.

title: Summer Law Clerkship - 2027
description:
You: A motivated and liberty-minded law student dedicated to individual freedom. You came to law school with a vision—to fight for your principles and make a difference. You want to learn about the world of public-interest law from the best.

Them: Bureaucrats, city councils, mayors, governors, and federal agencies are stripping Americans of their rights every day. There's a lot of government overreach out there, and it's backed by seemingly endless resources. But fortunately, like all lumbering giants, abusive government is most vulnerable when countered by individuals who act strategically and nimbly, take calculated risks, have each other's backs, and are confident in, and passionate for, the cause—the very sort of swashbucklers we employ in spades here at PLF.

Us: We fight back. Pacific Legal Foundation is the nation's first and most successful public interest law firm dedicated to vindicating individual liberty. PLF has an unmatched record in the United States Supreme Court, with 18 victories out of 21 cases litigated at the Court. We also have more than 200 active cases across the nation.

We’re a next-generation public interest law firm that challenges convention, adapts to a changing landscape, and strives to set the standard for what’s possible in legal advocacy.

About PLF's Summer Clerk Program

PLF's Summer Clerk Program introduces you to public-interest law, immerses you in active litigation, and offers you a unique chance to study the constitutional and philosophical framework of liberty. You will benefit from hands-on training as you perform legal research and writing projects in PLF's four litigation areas: property rights, equality and opportunity, separation of powers, and environment and natural resources. This is a full-time, paid summer position of $22/hour, including transportation benefits and wellness leave.

What makes this program different:

  • Assignments: Our confidence in individualism extends to how we set assignments, and this is often cited as one of the best aspects of the program. You will not only have the opportunity to work across all four practice areas, but you will also get to choose most of your assignments. Your designated supervisor will ensure you receive feedback, guide you in managing your work, and offer advice and expertise. We create the environment and opportunity for you to craft your experience, and clerks who get the most out of the program are the ones who embrace this mentality.
  • Weekly Programming: Every week, you will participate in educational and social activities to supplement your connection to PLF, the world of public interest law, and your fellow clerks. This includes field trips around the DC area, moot courts, department introductions, and deep-dive conversations with PLF attorneys on cases and litigation strategy.
  • Networking and Mentorship: One of the most important things at this stage of your career is to build relationships, so we strongly encourage all clerks to set aside time to connect with other PLFers. Many clerks naturally build mentorship relationships beyond their supervisor through working with other attorneys, and we offer a mentorship program if there is a specific area of PLF's work you are most interested in.

Your specific job duties will likely include:

  • Drafting legal memoranda on research questions for active trial and appellate litigation.
  • Assisting in drafting motions and briefs before federal and state courts.
  • Contributing to the discovery process across all four of our practice areas.

This role is ideal for someone with:

  • One to two years of law school completed by the spring or summer of 2026.
  • Excellent writing and legal research skills.
  • A demonstrated interest in the philosophical and constitutional principles of individual liberty.

Program Dates & Location:

  • The clerkship will run from June 2nd to August 20th. If this end date conflicts with other commitments, you have the option of ending your clerkship on August 13th instead.
  • On June 2nd and 3rd, we will host an Opening Summit in our DC Office. All clerks are expected to attend. Accommodation may be made for those participating in complimentary fellowships if advance notice is given.
  • Participants are expected to work at least three days a week from our DC Office in Arlington, Virginia, for the duration of the program.

To Apply:

We will be accepting applications from October 9th to January 3rd. PLF will begin providing updates and reaching out to candidates for an interview the week of December 21st. If you think you might be a good fit, please submit the following application materials:

  • Your resume, including your relevant educational and professional experience
  • A cover letter explaining why PLF is the place for you, why you want to fight for liberty, and what distinguishes you from typical applicants
  • A legal writing sample that demonstrates your ability to research and analyze the law. Work completed for a law school course is welcome.

title: Organ Preservationist
description:
Career Opportunity: Organ Preservationist in the Tri- State of Kentucky and Surrounding Regions

Are you looking for an opportunity to make a meaningful impact on organ donation by bringing your surgical expertise to a role where precision, purpose, and teamwork come together? As an Organ Preservationist, you will evaluate potential donors, coordinate clinical care, and help maximize opportunities for successful donation through the recovery, preservation, and perfusion of organs and tissues for transplantation or research. This role is ideal for an experienced healthcare professional who thrives in fast-paced, sensitive, and highly collaborative environments.

As an Organ Preservationist, you will perform aseptic organ preservation and kidney perfusion, support operating room preparation, maintain preservation supplies and equipment, and build strong relationships with hospital OR teams through education and collaboration. You will help ensure every recovery is handled safely, accurately, and in accordance with applicable policies, regulatory standards, and manufacturer guidelines. This position reports to the Manager of Surgical Services.

We are committed to supporting the professional growth and development of our team members, with opportunities to expand skills, take on additional responsibilities, and advance within the organization. In this role, you will be expected to consistently perform your work safely, ethically, and in accordance with organizational policies, professional standards, and applicable laws and regulations. Your commitment to safety, integrity, and compassionate care will be essential to supporting donors, their families, healthcare partners, and our mission.

Responsibilities:

  • Perform aseptic organ preservation, including flushing abdominal organs with the appropriate solution and packaging and labeling organs, vessels, and tissue-typing materials in accordance with OPTN policy.
  • Assist hospital staff with operating room preparation for organ recovery procedures.
  • Perform aseptic kidney pumping and pulsatile perfusion following kidney separation by a surgeon.
  • Support aseptic surgical recovery of organs and tissues for research.
  • Obtain biopsy specimens, prepare frozen slides, and submit materials for pathologist review.
  • Maintain preservation supplies, solutions, laboratory readiness, and mechanical preservation equipment in accordance with organizational policy, regulatory standards, and manufacturer guidelines.
  • Develop productive relationships with operating room staff and provide donation-related education through in-services, presentations, and meetings.

Qualifications:

  • Completion of a Surgical Technologist Program required; Certified Surgical Technologist credential preferred.
  • Two or more years of operating room experience with demonstrated knowledge of sterile technique.
  • Experience in organ or tissue recovery is strongly desired.
  • Organ perfusion and previous on-call experience preferred.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively while demonstrating sound judgment, problem-solving, and decision-making.
  • Excellent arm-hand steadiness, manual dexterity, and finger dexterity for precise clinical work.
  • Strong computer and data-entry skills, including Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and internet-based systems.
  • Professionalism, discretion, and a high degree of confidentiality.
  • Certified Transplant Preservationist credential required within 24 months of hire.

Schedule & Work Environment:

This role includes significant on-call responsibility, including the ability to work 24-hour on-call shifts, respond promptly to dispatches, and travel throughout the designated service area. Work is performed in hospital clinical areas. The position requires the ability to lift up to 75 pounds and assist with donor transfers. Reasonable accommodations may be available to support qualified individuals in performing the essential functions of the role.

What We Offer:

  • Paid time off (PTO) and paid holidays.
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance options.
  • Retirement savings benefits.
  • Employer-supported professional development and training opportunities.
  • Additional employee wellness and support resources.

If you are passionate about helping others and ready to bring your surgical expertise to a mission-driven, inclusive team, apply online today and become part of our future.

EEO/M/F/D/V. No third-party applications please.

title: Verzorgende IG Ouderenzorg | Gehandicaptenzorg | Monster (Westland)
description:
Wil jij werken op een plek waar je bewoners écht leert kennen? Waar je niet alleen zorgt, maar ook begeleidt? En waar je jouw kennis als Verzorgende IG inzet voor mensen die jou vertrouwen en waarderen? Dan voel jij je waarschijnlijk thuis op De Kruithoff in Monster.

Voor onze locatie De Kruithoff zoeken wij een Verzorgende IG voor 24 tot 28 uur per week.

Jouw rol

Als Verzorgende IG op De Kruithoff werk je met ouder wordende mensen met een verstandelijke beperking. Je combineert verzorging, begeleiding en verpleegtechnische handelingen in één afwisselende functie.

Je ondersteunt bewoners bij hun dagelijkse verzorging, maar kijkt vooral naar wat iemand nog zelf kan. Je hebt oog voor de persoon achter de zorgvraag en begrijpt dat goede zorg begint met aandacht, vertrouwen en persoonlijk contact. Veel bewoners wonen al jarenlang op De Kruithoff. Daardoor bouw je een band op met bewoners én hun familie. Je leert mensen kennen zoals ze zijn en merkt vaak als eerste wanneer er iets verandert in gezondheid, gedrag of welzijn.

Wat ga je doen?

  • Je begeleidt en verzorgt ouder wordende cliënten met een verstandelijke beperking;
  • Je ondersteunt bij ADL-zorg zoals wassen, aankleden, toiletgang en medicatie;
  • Je verricht verpleegtechnische handelingen binnen jouw bevoegdheden;
  • Je ondersteunt bewoners met onder andere dementie, diabetes, epilepsie en andere ouderdomsgerelateerde aandoeningen;
  • Je signaleert veranderingen in gezondheid en welzijn en schakelt waar nodig met collega's of andere disciplines;
  • Je werkt samen met familieleden, artsen, behandelaren en collega's;
  • Je draagt bij aan een veilige, warme en huiselijke leefomgeving;
  • Je werkt ochtend-, avond- en weekenddiensten.

Over de locatie

De Kruithoff ligt op loopafstand van het centrum van Monster in het Westland. Hier wonen 24 ouder wordende cliënten met een verstandelijke beperking. De bewoners zijn tussen de 55 en 90 jaar oud. Door het ouder worden krijgen veel bewoners te maken met lichamelijke achteruitgang, dementie en complexere zorgvragen. Je komt onder andere in aanraking met diabeteszorg, epilepsie, stomazorg, mobiliteitsproblemen, medicatiebeheer en intensieve ADL-ondersteuning.

Binnen het team is veel kennis aanwezig op het gebied van ouderenzorg, dementie en gehandicaptenzorg. Samen zorgen jullie ervoor dat bewoners zo zelfstandig mogelijk kunnen blijven leven in een vertrouwde omgeving. Wanneer externe dagbesteding tijdelijk niet mogelijk is, bieden we activiteiten op de locatie zelf aan. Daarnaast maken bewoners graag gebruik van de tuin, het terras en de voorzieningen in het dorp.

Wat maakt De Kruithoff bijzonder?

Werken op De Kruithoff betekent werken op een plek waar je de tijd krijgt om goede zorg te leveren.

Je bent niet alleen bezig met zorgtaken, maar ook met het welzijn van bewoners. Een gesprek tijdens de koffie, samen een wandeling maken of aansluiten bij iemands belevingswereld kan soms net zo belangrijk zijn als een verpleegtechnische handeling. Juist die combinatie van zorg, begeleiding en langdurige relaties maakt het werk bijzonder.

Wat bieden wij jou?

Een leuke baan waar je met plezier naar toe gaat. Wij investeren in onze medewerkers en daarom krijg je de ruimte om te groeien, zoals jij dat wilt: met jouw talent en ambitie, maar ook met ons Leerhuis en de vele opleidingsmogelijkheden. Verder vinden we belangrijk dat er rust in een rooster zit zodat je weet waar je aan toe bent. Wij werken met een basisrooster wat voor een jaar wordt uitgerold ( vastgesteld rooster).Daarnaast krijg je:

  • Een brutosalaris volgens de CAO Gehandicaptenzorg van min. € 2.649,- en max. € 3.708,- (FWG 35) bij een fulltime dienstverband van 36 uur. Bij onregelmatige diensten krijg je een toeslag van 122 tot 160%
  • Direct een contract voor onbepaalde tijd; tenzij er redenen zijn om hiervan af te wijken;
  • Mogelijkheid om jouw vakantietoeslag en/of eindejaarsuitkering elke maand laat uitbetalen.
  • Volop ruimte voor eigen inbreng en het ontwikkelen van jouw talenten, je werkt mee aan projecten en activiteiten;
  • Korting op uitjes, je sportschool en een interessante laptop- en fietsregeling en voordelen als extra vrije dagen tot aan coaching. Kies wat jij wilt;
  • Volop ruimte voor eigen inbreng; Wij zijn altijd op zoek naar mogelijkheden om onze begeleiding te verbeteren. Werken mee aan projecten en activiteiten!

Bekijk al onze arbeidsvoorwaarden.

Wie ben jij?

Jij bent een Verzorgende IG die verder kijkt dan de zorgvraag alleen. Je hebt oog voor de mens achter de beperking en vindt het belangrijk om bewoners een fijne, veilige en betekenisvolle dag te bieden.

Daarnaast beschik je over:

  • Een diploma Verzorgende IG niveau 3;
  • Affiniteit met ouderenzorg en mensen met een verstandelijke beperking;
  • Interesse in onderwerpen zoals dementie, epilepsie, diabetes en medicatieveiligheid;
  • Een rustige, positieve en stabiele houding;
  • Het vermogen om zelfstandig én in teamverband te werken.

Solliciteren?

Wil jij werken op een plek waar ouderenzorg, gehandicaptenzorg en persoonlijk contact samenkomen? Solliciteer dan eenvoudig met je cv. Een motivatiebrief is welkom. We bekijken sollicitaties doorlopend, dus je kunt direct reageren.

Heb je vragen of wil je eerst eens kennismaken? Neem gerust contact op met Recruitment via: Recruitment@Philadelphia.nl .Wil je deel uitmaken van deze warme en betrokken omgeving? Dan kijken wij uit naar jouw reactie.

title: Staff Product Manager, Growth & E-commerce Experimentation
description:
About Us

At Prenuvo, we are on a mission to flip the paradigm from reactive “sick-care” to proactive health care. Our award-winning whole body scan is fast (under 1 hour), safe (MRI has no ionizing radiation), and non-invasive (no contrast). Our unique integrated stack of optimized hardware, software, and increasingly AI, coupled with the patient-centric experience across our domestic and global clinics, have allowed us to lead the change against “we caught it too late again".

We are looking for a Staff Product Manager, Growth & E-commerce Experimentation to accelerate how Prenuvo learns and improves across our digital commerce experience.

This is a hands-on growth product role. You will own a high-velocity experimentation roadmap across the customer consideration and purchase journey, from landing pages and product discovery through selection, booking, checkout, and immediate post-purchase experiences. You will turn customer behavior, qualitative insight, and business data into clear hypotheses and measurable tests.

You will partner closely with Design, Engineering, Analytics, Marketing, E-commerce, Clinical, Legal, Privacy, and Operations to move quickly without compromising patient trust or the integrity of the healthcare experience.

An immediate area of focus will be improving conversion and learning velocity across Prenuvo’s booking experience: understanding where customers experience friction, testing how we position and package our offerings, and building the instrumentation required to know what is working and why.

You will help Prenuvo evolve from running individual tests to operating a durable experimentation engine that continuously improves the customer experience and informs broader product strategy.

This role does not provide visa sponsorship. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and must not require employer sponsorship for a work visa (current or future).

Help reshape the world through proactive healthcare while working with cutting-edge technology and high performing teams with deep expertise - join us to make a difference in people’s lives!

What You'll Do

  • Own a prioritized e-commerce experimentation roadmap tied to clear customer and business outcomes, including conversion, product selection, booking completion, average order value, and repeat purchase.
  • Use funnel analysis, behavioral data, customer research, and qualitative feedback to identify the highest-value friction points and growth opportunities across the digital journey.
  • Turn opportunities into clear hypotheses with defined target populations, success metrics, guardrails, and decision criteria before tests launch.
  • Partner with Design and Engineering to prototype, build, and launch A/B tests and other experiments rapidly while maintaining a high-quality patient experience.
  • Build the measurement and instrumentation needed to understand customer behavior across landing, selection, scheduling, checkout, and post-purchase flows.
  • Analyze experiment results with Analytics, distinguish signal from noise, and translate findings into clear product decisions, follow-up tests, or scaled experiences.
  • Partner with Marketing and E-commerce on offer, merchandising, messaging, pricing, packaging, and channel-to-site experiments while maintaining clear product ownership of the end-to-end experience.
  • Establish lightweight experimentation standards, documentation, and learning loops so insights are reusable rather than lost after an individual test ends.
  • Ensure experiments account for healthcare-specific guardrails, including clinical accuracy, privacy, legal requirements, accessibility, operational readiness, and customer trust.

What You’ll Bring

  • 8+ years of product management experience, with meaningful experience in consumer growth, e-commerce, conversion optimization, or experimentation.
  • A track record of improving digital funnels through structured experimentation and measurable product changes.
  • Hands-on experience designing and evaluating A/B tests, including hypotheses, success metrics, guardrails, segmentation, and experiment interpretation.
  • Strong analytical fluency and comfort working with funnel data, behavioral analytics, experiment results, and dashboards to make product decisions.
  • Excellent product judgment with the ability to balance conversion opportunities with customer comprehension, trust, and long-term value.
  • Experience partnering closely with product design and engineering to move from insight to shipped experiment quickly.
  • Experience working across Marketing, E-commerce, Analytics, and other commercial teams where ownership can span multiple functions.
  • Ability to separate a customer problem from a proposed solution and design tests that generate useful learning, not just activity.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain experiment design, results, uncertainty, and recommendations to executives and cross-functional teams.
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity, prioritizing among many possible tests, and making practical trade-offs between rigor and speed.
  • Experience in healthcare, health technology, regulated consumer products, or another high-trust environment is preferred.
  • Experience in a high-growth or scale-up environment is strongly preferred.

How You Work

  • You are naturally curious about customer behavior. When you see a drop-off, unexpected pattern, or strong opinion, your instinct is to ask what we can learn and how we can test it.
  • You are analytical without becoming academic. You care about experimental rigor, but you also know how to make pragmatic decisions when perfect data is not available.
  • You move quickly and collaborate well across functions. You can challenge assumptions, narrow an oversized idea into a testable hypothesis, and keep teams focused on the learning that matters.

Most importantly, you understand that growth in healthcare depends on trust. You optimize the commercial experience without compromising clarity, clinical integrity, or the patient experience.

Our Values

First: we are Pioneers

  • Transforming healthcare requires divergent thinking, bias for action, disciplined experimentation, and consistent grit and determination to maintain momentum. This journey is as challenging as it is rewarding.

Second: we are Platform-Builders

  • We’re always building foundations that allow us to achieve tomorrow more than we did today. We never lose sight of what’s ahead – in a mindset of ownership and duty to our mission.

Above all: we are Patients

  • We could all be the next person who walks through our very doors, seeking clarity or peace of mind. We are proud of our impact on our patients’ lives, and we won’t stop till everyone can benefit from our work.

What We Offer

  • An avenue to make a positive impact on people's lives and their health
  • We believe in preventative healthcare for everyone, including our team - Prenuvo provides free, whole-body scans to each team member
  • Growth opportunities are at the heart of our people journey, we’re doing big things with bright minds - there is no single path to success, it can be shaped along the way
  • Building strong relationships is at the core of everything we do - our team gets together each week to connect, share, and socialize
  • Recognizing time away to restore is vital to our wellbeing - we have a flexible vacation policy and we will encourage you to use it
  • Prenuvo offers a 401(k) retirement savings plan to eligible employees, allowing team members to make pre-tax contributions toward their retirement. While Prenuvo facilitates access to the plan, the company does not currently offer matching contributions.
  • We offer a comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, vision, including Mental Health coverage, to support you and your family
  • The base salary for this role ranges from $161,500-$190,000 in local currency, depending upon experience and geographic location

We are an equal-opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

As part of the hiring process, successful candidates will undergo a background check in compliance to applicable federal, provincial, and state rules.

Please be advised that official communication from our recruitment team will only come from our authorized domain []. If you are contacted by a recruiter, please ensure their email address ends with @prenuvo.com. We do not use third-party recruitment services or any other email domains for hiring purposes. If you receive communication that you believe to be fraudulent, please report it immediately to jobs@prenuvo.com.

title: Journeyman Rigger
description:
Job Title: Journeyman Rigger
Company: Loenbro, LLC
Business Unit/Department: Loenbro West
Location: Lead, SD
Reports to: Superintendent / Project Manager
Employment Type: Full-time
FLSA Classification: Non-Exempt

About Loenbro

Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries, and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.

At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.

Job Summary
Loenbro is seeking an experienced Lead Rigger to support the LBNF/DUNE-US South Dakota Rigging Services at the Sanford Underground Research Facility (SURF) in Lead, SD. This multi-shift underground role supports cryostat and infrastructure installation in the North and South Caverns. The Lead Rigger provides daily on-site supervision while working as a productive member of the crew, communicates daily with the FFDG representative, maintains schedule adherence, upholds employee conduct and competence standards, and administers disciplinary action when required.

The successful candidate will have a solid background in rigging, erecting, and modifying structural steel in an industrial construction setting. Your leadership skills and your experience have earned you the ability to direct the work of others and make quick decisions. You must be well-organized and favor safety above everything else.

Essential Job Responsibilities

  • Coordinates and supervises daily activities of crew while working as a productive member of that crew.
  • Communicate daily with the FFDG representative regarding schedule status, operational concerns, and crew performance.
  • Visually inspect and test rigging materials to ensure safety and reliability.
  • Select appropriate gear such as cables, pulleys, vices, winches, etc. according to load weights and sizes, work area, and job specifications.
  • Ensure all lifts comply with DOE-STD-1090-2020, ASME B30 series, and project-specific lift plans.
  • Maintain satisfactory standards of employee conduct, integrity, and competence.
  • leading or participating in daily JHAs / toolbox talks and exercising stop-work authority.
  • Initiate and administer disciplinary action regarding deficiencies; support removal of personnel when requested in writing by FFDG.
  • Be aware of obstacles, surrounding structures, barriers or objects and the location of other people.
  • Signal or verbally communicate with workers and others engaged in hoisting, suspending, and moving loads to ensure the safety of workers and materials.
  • Dismantle, inspect, clean, organize and store rigging equipment after use.
  • Supervise and train workers.
  • Guarantee all safety precautions and quality standards are followed.
  • Ensure crew PPE compliance (Type II hard hat with chin strap, Level IV cut-resistant gloves, reflective clothing, steel-toe boots, self-rescuer, and 4-gas monitor when acting as Guide).
  • Support two-shift (day/night) and six-day work schedules as required by the installation sequence.

Minimum Qualifications

Required:

  • NCCER Advanced Rigger / Rigger Level II certification (or NCCCO Rigger Level II equivalent) – mandatory.
  • 5+ years’ experience industrial or heavy-lift rigging experience.
  • Successfully complete all required FFDG training, including LBNF/DUNE Guide Training for Crew Leads, Site Orientations, and Practical Factors.
  • Able to manage team members and multiple projects.
  • Knowledge of reading and interpreting sketches, blueprints, and detailed drawings
  • Coordinate tasks according to priorities and plans.
  • Ensure labor and resources are adequate.
  • Must pass a background check and do a drug screening.

Preferred:

  • Capable of performing physically demanding tasks during long shifts.
  • Skilled in math which includes adding and subtracting fractions.
  • Prior experience at DOE sites, underground mines, or similar high-hazard environments.
  • Fall Protection Competent Person, MEWP, First Aid/CPR certifications.
  • Previous Lead or Foreman experience on multi-shift industrial projects.
  • Must have a valid driver's license.

Physical Demands and Work Environment

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Work is performed primarily underground at the Sanford Underground Research Facility (SURF) in Lead, SD, within the North and South Caverns (approximately 4,850' below surface). Two-shift (day and night) and six-day schedules are anticipated. Company identifiable attire with logo is always required on SURF property. Compliance with all FFDG, DOE, and Loenbro ES&H requirements is mandatory.

Work Environment:

  • Potential exposure to extreme cold and hot temperatures.
  • Working in underground conditions,
  • Fit and move in confined spaces including tanks and vessels.
  • Limited working surfaces.
  • Exposure to noise above 85 decibels and intense odors.
  • Exposure to areas with limited visibility.

This role requires compliance with all applicable safety regulations, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and Loenbro's Environmental Health and Safety (EH&S) policies.

Benefits

Loenbro offers a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and rewards to those who join our team:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company match
  • Paid time off (PTO) and holiday pay.
  • Life and disability insurance
  • Professional development and training opportunities
  • Employee assistance program (EAP)

Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification and hours worked.

Guided by Core Values (LEAD), grounded in grit and a commitment to excellence, Loenbro betters our families, customers, and local communities. If you are ready to be part of a company that LEADS by:

  • Living with Integrity
  • Exceeding Expectations
  • Acting with Urgency
  • Delivering Excellence

…we want to hear from you.

Loenbro is an Equal Opportunity Employer

title: Principal Software Engineer (Embedded)
description:
Forj Medical designs and develops custom electromechanical devices driven by safety-critical embedded software. We work in 4 major Technology Segments: Fluid & Gas Management, Optical Systems, Surgical Energy and Stimulation/Active Wearables. Our projects typically involve ‘greenfield’, bespoke designs - giving our engineers both depth and breadth in design challenges – opportunities to learn & grow abound.
What you’ll do
As a Principal Software Engineer at Forj, you’ll be one of our most trusted technical leaders—helping teams turn our clients’ most difficult medical-device challenges into safe, secure, and maintainable embedded software. You’ll combine deep hands-on engineering with broad influence: shaping product and platform architectures, guiding critical technical decisions, and raising the quality of software work across projects. You’ll work with significant autonomy, but not alone—partnering closely with clients, program leaders, and engineers across systems, electrical, mechanical, test & quality.
Core responsibilities include:

Applying expert knowledge of the Forj Quality Management System, FDA regulations, IEC 62304, and cybersecurity standards to software system development.
Proactively identifying the highest technical and program risks early; evaluating alternatives, making thoughtful tradeoffs, and communicating recommendations clearly to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
Leading requirements definition, architectural design, and technical decision-making across software-intensive medical device systems.
Providing detailed estimates in support of project milestones and software deliverables; delivering medium to highly complex software projects within scope, schedule, and budget constraints.
Applying a unique feature-focused method of breaking down software system functionality; you'll iteratively lead your software team through architecture, design, implementation, testing and integration of software features in an agile workflow.
Leading and mentoring a team of software engineers through work planning, task delegation, and coordination of execution.
Design, implement and test project source code, especially in critical areas, including debugging difficult system issues, navigating integration challenges, and demonstrating effective engineering practices.
Owning the technical quality of all software artifacts – ensuring architectural integrity, code quality and design robustness.
Driving software process improvements, reusable platforms, and engineering initiatives that benefit multiple projects.
Serving as a trusted advisor to clients, engineering leadership, and cross-functional teams on high-impact technical decisions.

You’ll have a chance to make a meaningful impact on the lives of patients – our recent products help clinicians treat cancer, sustain life and alleviate pain.
To top it off, we think you’ll enjoy working with other smart, curious and talented engineers as you bring medical devices to life.
What you bring

BS, MS, or equivalent degree in Computer/Software Engineering, Computer Science or similar field.
10+ years’ experience in embedded software development in medical device or other regulated industry, including in a lead role with a track record of successful software delivery using an inspirational and effective leadership style.
A record of technical leadership on complex products or platforms, with influence extending beyond a single feature or project team.
The ability to create clear technical narratives and diagrams, explain difficult concepts to varied audiences, and build trust with clients, peers, and leaders.
Significant experience with embedded Linux development on SoMs – particularly with Yocto Project/BSP and driver configuration.
Deep expertise in embedded software architecture, design, implementation, integration, and test using C and/or C++; experience with C#, Python, or other supporting languages is helpful.
Demonstrated proficiency in solving high-complexity software problems – including a methodical, reasoned approach to reproducing and fixing bugs.
Strong experience with microcontrollers, RTOS-based systems (e.g. ThreadX), device drivers, interprocess or interprocessor communications, and hardware/software integration.
Experience with one or more of the following: communication protocols; Qt/QML, LVGL or other GUI frameworks; automated builds and CI/CD; static analysis; Python or other scripting languages; medical-device cybersecurity.
Experience creating reusable software components, influencing engineering practices across teams, evaluating shared technologies, or contributing to proposals and technical strategy is especially valuable.

How we work
Project teams are led by a Program Manager / Systems Engineer; technical leads from Software, Electrical, Mechanical, Test and Quality collaborate on projects for clients ranging from established companies to small startups.
We foster a strong engineering culture and operate under mature software & product development processes.
We invest in tools, automation and continuous improvement.
We work at an efficient, sustainable pace – taking time for fun along the way!
Working Conditions: Must be authorized for permanent work in the United States.
EEO Statement
Forj, Inc. provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.
This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

Overview of the role
The Business Analyst, Experience is responsible for supporting the planning, design, and delivery of complex transformation initiatives. The role works closely with Program Managers, business leaders, operational teams, technology partners, and external vendors to understand business challenges, define future-state solutions, and ensure successful implementation.
This role requires strong analytical capabilities, business process expertise, and an ability to bridge business and technology teams. Key Responsibilities

Business Analysis & Solution Design

Support experience transformation initiatives from discovery through implementation.
Work with Program Managers, sponsors, and stakeholders to understand project objectives, scope, and desired outcomes.
Gather, analyze, document, and validate business, operational, and technology requirements.
Assess current-state processes, systems, and experiences while identifying opportunities for improvement.
Develop future-state processes, workflows, business requirements, and operational designs.
Create process maps, journey maps, business cases, requirements documentation, and solution recommendations.
Translate business needs, assumptions, risks, and requirements into clear functional and technical specifications.
Evaluate impacts across guest experience, operations, technology platforms, people, policies, and processes.

Stakeholder Management & Facilitation

Facilitate workshops, working sessions, and discovery activities with stakeholders across the organization.
Lead meetings with business, technology, operational, and external partner teams to advance project outcomes.
Build alignment across stakeholders with diverse priorities and perspectives.
Work collaboratively to identify and resolve issues, bottlenecks, and dependencies.
Support governance activities through preparation of project documentation, reports, recommendations, and executive presentations.

Technology & Delivery Support

Partner closely with technology teams, vendors, architects, and delivery teams throughout implementation.
Support agile and waterfall project delivery methodologies as required.
Work with development teams to ensure requirements are clearly understood and solutions meet business needs.
Support system testing, user acceptance testing, operational readiness, and implementation activities.
Assist with issue resolution, change requests, risk identification, and ongoing delivery activities.
Support benefits tracking and measurement of business outcomes following implementation.

Operational Transformation

Assess impacts of proposed changes on frontline teams, guest touchpoints, and operational processes.
Support process redesign activities across commercial, operational, and guest-facing functions.
Help ensure solutions balance guest experience improvements with operational feasibility and business objectives.
Contribute to change management and organizational readiness activities that support successful adoption.

Experience & Qualifications

Required

3-7 years of experience in a Business Analyst, Process Analyst, Product Analyst, Consultant, or similar role.
Demonstrated experience supporting technology-enabled transformation projects.
Strong requirements gathering, process mapping, and business documentation skills.
Experience facilitating workshops and requirements sessions with business stakeholders.
Proven ability to work across multiple stakeholder groups and manage competing priorities.
Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking capabilities.
Strong verbal, written, and presentation communication skills.
Experience creating process documentation using tools such as Visio, Miro, Lucidchart, or similar platforms.
Working knowledge of both Agile and Waterfall delivery methodologies.
Bachelor's degree in business, or Technology related fields

Preferred

Experience working within airline, travel, hospitality, retail, or other service-based industries.
Experience supporting digital product, customer experience, loyalty, e-commerce, retailing, or operational transformation initiatives.
Familiarity with customer-facing technology platforms, mobile applications, CRM/CDP systems, loyalty programs, or enterprise technology solutions.
Experience working alongside agile development teams and technology delivery organizations.
IIBA, CBAP, CCBA, PMI-PBA, CAPM, Agile, Scrum, Lean, or related certifications.
Experience working within large-scale enterprise transformation programs.

Who You Are
You are a naturally curious problem solver who enjoys understanding how businesses operate and identifying opportunities to improve them.
You can move seamlessly between strategy discussions, operational process reviews, and detailed solution requirements. You ask thoughtful questions, challenge assumptions respectfully, and help teams connect business objectives with practical solutions.
Most importantly, you are passionate about improving experiences for guests and employees while helping deliver meaningful business outcomes.

  • Improve the foundations. Refactor, modernise, and pay down technical debt in a mature codebase that's earned its complexity honestly.

  • Shape the platform. Contribute to architectural decisions and help guide where our frontend goes next.

  • Collaborate with the best. Join a team of skilled engineers where you'll brainstorm, refine ideas, and learn from people who care about their craft.

Backend

title: Staff Platform Product Manager, UX Platform
description:
We are looking for a Staff Product Manager to own product strategy and execution for the Web Development Platform within our UX Platform organization. You’ll drive the roadmap, define success metrics, and prioritize investments across the full web development lifecycle — local development, build tooling, component systems, performance observability, and CI/CD — serving two audiences: the thousands of engineers and builders across Intuit business units, and increasingly, Intuit’s own customers building custom apps and agentic capabilities within our products.


This isn’t an abstract platform role. You’ve shipped code, felt the pain of slow build pipelines, and know what it takes to move fast without breaking things. That credibility is what lets you earn trust with engineering, ask sharp questions, and make prioritization calls that hold up.
A core part of the mandate: extending the platform with agentic and AI-assisted capabilities — shaping how coding agents and AI-driven tooling change the way builders work, whether internal or customer-facing, and partnering closely with engineering and design to bring those capabilities to market at scale. Required

title: APRN: Mobile OTP- 7333
description:
Recognized as a Top Workplace for 13 consecutive years! Your career can mean different things in different workplaces. Apply with CHR now to see what it's like to work somewhere your voice is heard, your wellness is a priority, and your success matters.

JOB TITLE: APRN

EMPLOYMENT TYPE: Part-time, 25 hours/wk

SCHEDULED HOURS: 4 hours a day, 5 days a week, 7am-11am.

PROGRAM/LOCATION: Mobile OTP, Putnam, CT

PC#: 2935

ABOUT THE POSITION: CHR's Mobile OTP

The Mobile OTP is a SAMHSA-certified extension of our brick-and-mortar Opioid Treatment Program, bringing Medication for Opioid Use Disorder (MOUD), specifically Methadone services, directly to underserved communities. Clinicians are primarily based at the Putnam OTP but may also provide care in the community aboard the mobile treatment unit. Please note, clinicians meet the RV at its designated location in the community but do not operate or drive it.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Provides administration of medications as indicated in agency policies and procedures under the direction and supervision of the agency MD.

Direct Treatment Services

  • Provides treatment services consistent with those authorized by payors and agency clinical standards and guidelines.
  • Provide direct clinical services to clients, which may include; psychiatric evaluations, diagnostic assessments, ongoing treatment as well as crisis planning and response.
  • Maintain positive working relationships with community health organizations and outside medical services to ensure coordination of client care.
  • Provide training and consultation to staff as indicated.
  • Develop programs and psycho-educational interventions for clients across the agency on issues such as wellness, side effects, health, etc.
  • Participates in case conferences/consultations, as required, and in team meetings and training as needed.
  • Makes comprehensive bio-psycho-social assessments of client and develops focus of treatment.
  • Provides comprehensive and clear case formulation.
  • Makes clinically appropriate, focused, goal-oriented treatment plans and reviews as required by agency guidelines.
  • Provides individual, group and/or family therapy as appropriate.
  • Assesses level of care needs/changes and follows up with and/or makes referrals to appropriate type of treatment and length of treatment.
  • Provides brief treatment for clients who do not have a major mental illness.
  • For the client who has a serious and pervasive mental illness, provides acute treatment services when indicated and ongoing supportive, less intensive treatment to facilitate continuous stability.
  • Makes risk assessments and follows through as clinically indicated in client crisis.
  • Demonstrates competency in age-related or specialty issues and developmental needs for each population served.

Indirect/Administrative Services/Tasks

  • Makes collateral contacts with clients’ natural support network; with other team members in-house; with other professionals/providers/agencies and in-patient treatment settings.
  • Collaborates with the team to arrange for admission to other levels of care or referrals to other services.
  • Completes all client record keeping conforming with agency policy and procedures (form, content, timeliness).
  • Completes all necessary information to support transactions with insurance and managed care companies (written and telephone) comprehensively and in a timely manner.
  • Completes any other required administrative record keeping or tasks relevant to the functioning of the agency/department/staff role per policy and procedures, or as assigned by supervisor or Program Director.
  • As plan manager co-ordinates client’s treatment with other providers in and outside the agency and completes all referrals as needed.

Additional Duties and Responsibilities

  • Provides clinical leadership role.
  • Provides staff supervision when assigned.
  • Provide clinical supervision and consultation to case management teams as assigned.
  • Participation in agency/departmental committees as required.
  • Takes responsibility for own professional growth and development within and outside of the agency. Participates in individual/group supervision, case conferences and any other training provided internally that is relevant to one’s role and work focus.
  • Attends administrative, clinical and programmatic staff meetings.
  • May perform other assignments and duties, as area needs required.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Education: APRN

Experience: 5 years' experience in adult or child mental health. Community mental health experience preferred.

Licensure/Certification/Registration: CT APRN license.

Why Join CHR?

Be part of an exciting, supportive, and dynamic workplace where your growth and well-being are our top priorities!

  • Comprehensive benefits packages include health insurance, ample paid time off (including your birthday!), employer contributions to your 403b Retirement Plan, and competitive insurance premiums with added discounts on pet, home and auto!
  • Tuition reimbursement and professional development programs, including exclusive tuition discounts for CHR employees at several local colleges/universities
  • Career development opportunities! FREE robust training curriculum, featuring our Clinical Training Series for interactive learning, practical skill enhancement, and professional growth! Clinical supervision and/or mentoring offered at several programs
  • Wellness program: Annual wellness stipend, FREE premium subscription to the Calm app, 6 FREE confidential counseling sessions through our Employee Assistance Program
  • Employee appreciation and involvement, including contests, lunch & learns (meet with our CEO!), employee appreciation events, employee-led resource groups open to all, and more!

And so much more! (Many benefits are available to all staff, regardless of the hours worked, with some subject to eligibility)

title: Shipper II - 1st shift - M-F - 7am-2:30pm
description:
The Shipping Clerk II works under close supervision of the Shipping Supervisor to prepare packages for shipment by packaging boxes and staging pallets according to the daily shipping schedule and delivery specifications and assisting with loading and unloading trucks as needed.

Sort and stage pallets in the shipping dock by operating a Pallet Jack or by hand based on daily shipping schedule, truck weight limits and requirements.

Prepare packages for shipping by taping or stapling boxes shut and affixing completed address label.

Generate air pillows at the shipping line by entering quantity and size needed in the Air Pillow Machine and placing them in boxes.

Investigate packages that are flagged as not meeting the specified weight requirements on the shipping conveyor line and make necessary adjustments or escalate issues to the Shipping Supervisor.

Wrap ready-to-ship pallets by operating the shrink wrap machine to ensure the product on the pallet does not shift during transport before it is loaded on the truck for shipment.

Scan products for delivery by operating RF Scanner to scan bar code of packages and enter delivery information.

Assemble specialized boxes for custom orders using a Staple Gun.

Note any order discrepancies and damages to inform Shipping Supervisor.

May load product on trucks by operating a Forklift or Pallet Jack.

Perform daily safety inspections of material handling equipment.

Observe all safety guidelines and report safety concerns to management.

Follow Six Sigma lean manufacturing standards to keep work area clean and safe from hazards.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

One year of relevant work experience required. High School Diploma/GED and experience working in a distribution or manufacturing environment preferred.
Must be able to read, write, speak and understand basic English.
Must possess knowledge in updating data and navigating through warehouse management systems.
Experience with IMI Series (AS400) and Boss is preferred.
Must be able to operate a Class II Order Picker and Class II Stand-Up Forklift, Pallet Jack, Label Printing System, RF Scanner, and Staple Gun.
Ability to demonstrate basic math skills (addition, subtraction, multiplication and division).
Ability to work in a fast-paced team environment.
Ability to work independently and with others.
Ability to meet established deadlines.
Ability to demonstrate strong attention to detail.

Physical Demand Requirements
Regularly required to stand, walk, bend, and lift; use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools or controls; reach with hands and arms; The employee is occasionally required to sit, reach above shoulders, climb stairs; balance; stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl; talk or hear; taste or smell. The employee must lift and/or move objects up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

title: Vastaava työterveyslääkäri, Helsinki
description:
Me Terveystalossa teemme työksemme tärkeintä, terveyttä. Työllämme on suuri merkitys, ei vain asiakkaillemme, vaan koko yhteiskunnalle. Meitä tärkeimmän tekijöitä on Terveystalossa jo yli 14 000 lähes 400 toimipaikassa eri puolilla Suomea. Siellä, missä ihmiset elävät arkeaan ja missä kotimaista työtämme tarvitaan.

Etsimme nyt osaavaan ja motivoituneeseen joukkoomme vastaavaa työterveyslääkäriä Helsinkiin toimipaikkoina Redi, Itäkeskus ja Herttoniemi.

Tutustu tehtävään ja hae!

Mitä työ vastaavana työterveyslääkärinä pitää sisällään?

Terveystalossa pääset tekemään monipuolisia vastaavan työterveyslääkärin tehtäviä sekä hyödyntämään ja kasvattamaan osaamistasi esihenkilötyön, työkykyjohtamisen ja muiden työterveyshuollon ydintoimintojen sekä lääketieteellisen laadun ja asiakaskokemuksen parissa. Saat upean paikan nähdä terveydenhuollon innovaatioiden käyttöönottoa ja jatkuvaa laadun kehittämistä sekä myös osallistua toiminnan kehittämiseen.

Vastaavan työterveyslääkärin tehtävät koostuvat 60% työterveyslääkäreiden ammatillisesta johtamisesta yksiköissä sekä lääketieteellisen osaamisen, laadun ja työterveyden prosessien varmistamisesta ja kehittämisestä muiden alueella toimivien vastaavien työterveyslääkäreiden ja vastuuhenkilöiden kanssa. Toimit esihenkilönä sinulle nimetyissä yksiköissä työskenteleville työsuhteisille työterveyslääkäreille ja substanssin asiantuntijan roolissa osallistut tarvittaessa myös lääkäreiden rekrytointiin.

Vastaavan työterveyslääkärin tehtävien lisäksi toimit 40% työterveyslääkärinä asiakas- ja asiakkuustyötä tehden. Työterveyslääkärinä pääset työskentelemään osana yritysterveyden moniammatillista tiimiä, johon kuuluu lisäksesi työterveyshoitajia, työfysioterapeutti, ravitsemusterapeutti ja työterveyspsykologi. Moniammatillisuus merkitsee meille paljon: oman osaamisen tunnistamista, yhteistä vastuuta asiakkaasta, yhteisen tiedon luomista, asiakaslähtöistä organisaatiota ja tiimioppimista. Osaajayhteisö takanasi Terveystalossa on vahva, saat tukea ja sparrailuapua työhösi aina. Yksiköidemme laaja ja monipuolinen asiakaskanta sekä erinomaiset palvelut tarjoavat mielenkiintoisen työskentely-ympäristön, jossa oppii joka päivä jotain uutta.

Työsuhde on toistaiseksi voimassa oleva ja työtä voi tehdä osittain myös etätyönä. Lähimpänä tukenasi ja esihenkilönäsi on koko Helsingin alueen vastaava työterveyslääkäri Johanna Larkio.

Miksi meille töihin?

Meillä arki rakentuu sujuvuudesta ja toisista välittämisestä, jatkuvasta halusta kehittyä ja ennen kaikkea inhimillisistä kohtaamisista. Vaikka maailmaa muuttuu, meidän tapamme tehdä työtä säilyy: Terveystalossa sinä voit keskittyä tekemään sitä, mikä on tärkeintä – terveyttä.

  • Arkemme on sujuvaa. Panostamme lähijohtamiseen ja esihenkilötyöhön, jotta jokainen ammattilaisemme saa työssään tarvittavan tuen. Ammattirajat ylittävä tiimityö, joustavuus ja edistykselliset hoitopolkumme tukevat arjen työtä.
  • Välitämme toisistamme. Meillä jokainen on oma arvostettu itsensä, oman alansa huippuosaaja ja tärkeä osa työyhteisöä. Osaajatutkimuksemme mukaan ammattilaisemme arvostavat muun muassa lämmintä työyhteisöämme, hyvää esihenkilötyötä ja lähijohtamista sekä mahdollisuutta onnistua omassa työssä.
  • Teemme vaikuttavaa työtä. Terveystalossa on ainutkertaista osaamista aina ennaltaehkäisystä perusterveydenhuoltoon, suunterveyteen ja erikoissairaanhoitoon. Käytössämme ovat ainutlaatuiset oman työn laatumittarit ja digitaaliset hoitopolut kaikkiin yleisimpiin sairauksiin. Panostamme myös ammattilaistemme laadukkaaseen kouluttautumiseen, kehittymiseen ja ammatilliseen kasvuun.
  • Kotimainen ja vastuullinen. Vastuullisuus on meille sydämen asia. ISS ESG:n arvioinnissa kuulumme globaalisti oman alamme kärkeen, ja Suomalainen työ ry on myöntänyt meille Avainlippu-tunnuksen osoituksena Suomessa tuotetusta ja työllistävästä palvelusta. Teemme työtä suomalaisten terveyden ja koko yhteiskunnan hyvinvoinnin eteen tinkimättömällä ammattitaidolla. Suomen suurimpana yksityisenä terveydenhuoltoalan toimijana vaalimme kotimaisia juuria ja olemme ylpeitä suomalaisista omistajistamme.
  • Monimuotoinen ja yhdenvertainen. Terveystalossa olemme kaikki samanarvoisia riippumatta sukupuolesta, iästä, etnisestä tai kansallisesta taustasta, kansalaisuudesta, kielestä, uskonnosta, vakaumuksesta, mielipiteestä, vammasta, terveydentilasta, seksuaalisesta suuntautumisesta tai muusta ominaisuudesta. Pohjoismaisten pörssiyritysten ylimmän johdon monimuotoisuutta tarkastelevan Nordic Business Diversity Index 2025 -tutkimusraportin mukaan Terveystalo on Suomen kolmanneksi monimuotoisin organisaatio keskisuurten yritysten sarjassa.
  • Kilpailukykyinen palkitseminen ja monipuoliset edut. Ammatinharjoittajille tarjoamme vaihtuvat kumppanietumme ja muun muassa mahdollisuuden sopimushintaiseen työterveyshuoltoon.
  • Oma lääkäri- ja asiantuntijavastaava. Meillä lääketieteellisen tuen lisäksi työtäsi helpottaa ja tukee oma nimetty lääkäri- ja asiantuntijavastaavasi, joka tukee sinua arkesi suunnittelussa, huolehtii perehdytyksestäsi Terveystaloon, järjestelmiimme ja toimipisteeseen. Hän varmistaa, että arkesi on sujuvaa ja voit keskittyä ydinosaamiseesi.

Tarjoamme osaajillemme omat laadukkaat koulutuksemme, Terveystalon Lääkäripäivät, viikoittaiset Tiedosta taidoksi -koulutukset, työterveyden moniammatilliset sparrit, eri erikoisalojen omat koulutukset sekä Terveystalo Academyn monipuolisen kurssivalikoiman. Odotamme sinulta vankkaa kokemusta ja substanssiosaamista työterveyshuollosta sekä hyviä vuorovaikutustaitoja. Aiempi esihenkilökokemus katsotaan eduksi, mutta ei ole välttämätöntä.

Jätä yhteystietosi hakulomakkeen kautta viimeistään 16.10.2026. Huomioithan, että emme käsittele sähköpostitse lähetettyjä hakemuksia. Aloitamme hakemusten käsittelyn jo hakuajan aikana ja valinta tehdään sopivan hakijan löydyttyä.

title: Electrical Install Apprentice
description:
About Bell Bros:

At Bell Brothers Plumbing, Heating & Air, we are your gateway to a rewarding career in HVAC and plumbing services! We are proud to be a leading provider of heating, ventilation, air conditioning, windows, and plumbing solutions, and we believe that our success is rooted in the dedicated and passionate team members who make it all possible. We offer a culture of excellence, professional growth and development, cutting-edge technology and tools, a strong team environment, and competitive compensation and benefits.

Build Your Career in Residential Electrical Work

Bell Brothers is hiring an Electrical Installation Apprentice who is mechanically inclined, dependable, and ready to build a long-term career in the electrical trade.

Working under an Electrical Lead Installer, you'll contribute to residential installation projects while developing your technical knowledge, workmanship, and field experience. This is a hands-on development role, not simply a general labor or helper position. As you demonstrate competency, you'll take on more complex work and build toward becoming an independently capable residential electrician and, ultimately, a Lead Installer.

How We Work

At Bell Brothers, professional installation work means working safely, respecting the homeowner's property, and being accountable to your crew. You'll help keep jobsites organized, protect work areas, and communicate professionally while working in occupied homes.

Learning is part of the job. You'll receive coaching from Lead Installers, Field Supervisors, and Electrical leadership, and you'll be expected to ask questions, apply feedback, and show progress. When a task, installation method, or electrical condition is unclear, we expect you to seek direction rather than guess.

What You'll Do

  • Assist with residential projects such as main panel replacements, service upgrades, subpanels, rewires, device replacements, dedicated circuits, and electrical work supporting other trades.
  • Install wiring, devices, electrical boxes, raceways, breakers, lighting, equipment, and grounding and bonding components as assigned.
  • Perform tasks within your demonstrated skill level and under the direction of the Electrical Lead Installer.
  • Help with demolition, preparation, layout, material staging, equipment installation, testing, and project closeout.
  • Follow the approved job scope, applicable electrical codes, manufacturer requirements, and company installation standards.
  • Keep tools and materials organized, help identify material needs, and maintain clean, safe work areas.
  • Protect the homeowner's property through floor protection, work-area preparation, cleanup, and restoration coordination.
  • Use hand tools, power tools, ladders, testing equipment, and personal protective equipment safely.
  • Assist with testing, labeling, documentation, photographs, and assigned mobile-technology tasks.
  • Participate in field coaching and technical development, taking on greater responsibility as your skills progress.
  • Maintain assigned tools, company-issued equipment, and installation vehicles when applicable.

What You'll Bring

You may be an Electrical Trainee, a trade-school graduate, an apprenticeship participant or graduate building field experience, or someone with residential installation experience who has not yet obtained California Residential Electrician Certification.

Required qualifications:

  • Current California Electrical Trainee registration or other qualifying apprenticeship status when required under California requirements.
  • Willingness to learn residential installation methods, electrical codes, and company standards.
  • Dependability, punctuality, attention to detail, and willingness to accept coaching.
  • Ability to follow instructions and contribute to a two-person or multi-person installation crew.
  • Professional conduct and customer-service awareness when working in occupied homes.
  • Ability to use ServiceTitan or other mobile technology for assigned responsibilities.
  • Ability to perform physical installation work, including lifting up to 50 pounds and tasks requiring manual dexterity.

Helpful, but not required:

  • Electrical trade-school education, apprenticeship participation, or residential electrical field experience.
  • Basic understanding of electrical tools, materials, wiring methods, and residential systems.
  • Previous construction experience.

Training and Benefits

You'll receive on-the-job training and field coaching to help you develop your skills, with advancement opportunities as your capabilities grow.

  • 401(k) with company match
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Life insurance
  • Paid vacation and holidays
