title: Sr. Facility Security Officer
description:
The Facility Security Officer (FSO) has the ultimate responsibility for interpreting, implementing, and leading the security program for SkyWater, Austin, Texas. This role will be crucial in SkyWater’s ability to procure and maintain relationships with customers within various industries including the U.S Government.
Responsibilities:

  • Process, obtain, and maintain Facility Clearance (FCL) for SkyWater Texas.
  • Oversight of integrity of personnel and procedures required to protect classified and sensitive information and material per the National Industrial Security Program (NISP).
  • Interface with DCSA (Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency).
  • ITAR (International Trade and Arms Regulations) program management and implementation.
  • Research and Implement compliance of security programs.
  • Oversight of implementation and maintenance of contractual security documentation.
  • Prepare government compliance forms (Form DD254) issued to subcontractors, vendors, and suppliers.
  • Conduct security briefings and policy/procedures manuals.
  • Create and maintain specialized security areas (Closed Areas, etc.) in response to client and program requirements.
  • Advises and defines security procedures to protect program information and material.
  • Administer personnel security clearances in government systems (DISS) and work with candidates to obtain/maintain clearance.
  • Administer required filings with various government agencies.
  • Analyzes and responds to potential security breaches or spillages, reporting, and implementing corrective actions.
  • Develop systems to improve security and meet new requirements.
  • Interpret and implement relevant government flow down requirements.
  • Interface with customer security offices.
  • Define, interpret and implement security requirements and procedures for handling of Controlled Unclassified information (CUI) & CDI
  • Administer insider threat program and serve as Insider Threat Program Senior Official (ITPSO)

Required Qualifications
Experience and/or Training:

  • Active Secret clearance.
  • Minimum of five years working as a Facility Security Officer (FSO/AFSO) or equivalent role.
  • Completion of DCSA CDSE FSO Program Management for Possessing Facilities, ITPSO, and other applicable FSO training programs.
  • Strong working knowledge of the 32CFR, ICDs, and DoD Directives required.
  • Submitting, processing and obtaining Facility Clearance (FCL)
  • Demonstrated experience with entire lifecycle of classified contracts, insider threat program, counterintelligence, personnel clearances, secure area builds, creation of standard operation procedures, and visitor management.
  • Experience in Industrial Security and/or Government Contracts.
  • Demonstrated experience as liaison with law enforcement, USG, and DoD.
  • Familiar with government security program management, including: Electronic Questionnaires for Investigations Processing (e-Qip), Defense Information Security System (DISS), Secure Web Fingerprint Transmission (SWFT), Defense Information System, National Industrial Security System (NISS).
  • Physical and guard service supervision.
  • Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally and gain consensus from stakeholders on solutions to security problems.
  • This position is 100% on-site. Responsibilities sometime require working evenings and weekends and in some cases with little to no advance notice.

Required Skills:

  • Prior experience working in a role as self-starter requiring minimal supervision. Ability to plan, schedule and arrange activities to accomplish objectives.
  • Ability to analyze situations accurately and adopt an effective course of action.
  • Possesses good organizational skills and the ability to communicate clearly, concisely, and effectively verbally and in writing.
  • Ability to communicate with respect, openly, directly and effectively.
  • Demonstrated experience with public speaking, public relations, and education.
  • Thinks ahead, minimizing potential problems. Proactive in identifying areas to improve.
  • Technology/Equipment: Proficient with MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).

US Citizenship Required: This position requires that the applicant selected be a U.S. citizen. Must have a current Secret Clearance with the ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret/SCI clearance. Current active Top Secret/SCI clearance with polygraph is desired.

title: Begeleider Kind & Jeugd Gehandicaptenzorg | Middelburg | 18-20 uur
description:
Kort verblijf, blijvende impact

De ene middag help je een kind na school om tot rust te komen. In het weekend staat er weer een heel andere groep klaar voor een gezellige logeerpartij. Samen koken, spelen, eropuit of juist zorgen voor rust en duidelijkheid wanneer iemand dat nodig heeft.

Dat is werken bij Phila Agaat in Middelburg.

Voor onze locatie voor kort verblijf zoeken we een Begeleider Kind & Jeugd voor 18 tot 20 uur per week. Je werkt met kinderen, jongeren en jongvolwassenen met heel verschillende ondersteuningsvragen. Juist die afwisseling maakt deze plek bijzonder.

Werken bij Phila Agaat

Phila Agaat in Middelburg biedt logeeropvang, weekendopvang en naschoolse opvang. We zijn er voor zo'n 60 kinderen, jongeren en jongvolwassenen – natuurlijk nooit allemaal tegelijk. Zij komen bij ons om een fijne tijd te hebben én zodat ouders en verzorgers thuis even worden ontlast.

De verschillen tussen onze gasten zijn groot. Je begeleidt onder andere kinderen en jongeren met een lichte verstandelijke beperking (LVB), ernstig meervoudige beperking (EMB), lichamelijke beperking of gedragsproblematiek.

Dat betekent dat jij makkelijk kunt schakelen. Met de één onderneem je lekker een activiteit, een ander heeft behoefte aan duidelijke grenzen en structuur en weer een ander heeft ondersteuning nodig bij de lichamelijke verzorging.

Maar wat iemand ook nodig heeft: aandacht en plezier staan voorop. We willen dat kinderen en jongeren zich bij Phila Agaat veilig voelen, zichzelf kunnen zijn en vooral een fijne tijd hebben.

Je komt terecht in een hecht team op een locatie die volop in ontwikkeling is. Samen kijken jullie steeds opnieuw: wat heeft deze groep vandaag nodig om er iets moois van te maken?

Wat ga je doen?

Als Begeleider Kind & Jeugd combineer je begeleiden, verzorgen en vooral veel persoonlijke aandacht.

  • Je begeleidt kinderen en jongeren tijdens hun verblijf bij Phila Agaat;
  • Je zorgt voor een veilige, gezellige en vertrouwde omgeving;
  • Je organiseert activiteiten die passen bij leeftijd, interesses en mogelijkheden;
  • Je biedt structuur en stelt duidelijke grenzen wanneer dat nodig is;
  • Je ondersteunt cliënten bij lichamelijke verzorging en ADL;
  • Je signaleert veranderingen in gedrag, gezondheid en welzijn;
  • Je hebt aandacht voor ouders, verzorgers en het netwerk rondom het kind;
  • Je werkt dag-, avond- en weekenddiensten en draait ook slaapdiensten.

Wie ben jij?

Je vindt het leuk dat je nooit precies dezelfde groep voor je hebt. Je kunt het ene moment enthousiast meedoen met een activiteit en het volgende moment rust brengen wanneer een jongere spanning ervaart.

Je bent duidelijk zonder de verbinding te verliezen en hebt een gezonde dosis humor en relativeringsvermogen.

Daarnaast:

  • Heb je minimaal een afgeronde mbo niveau 4 of hbo-opleiding binnen Zorg & Welzijn, bijvoorbeeld Social Work of Pedagogiek;
  • Heb je affiniteit met kinderen en jongeren met een verstandelijke beperking;
  • Sta je stevig in je schoenen en kun je goed omgaan met verschillende begeleidingsvragen;
  • Ben je positief, creatief, leergierig en flexibel;
  • Ben je bereid onregelmatige diensten, weekenden en slaapdiensten te werken;
  • Is ervaring met gedrags- of psychische problematiek mooi meegenomen.

Wat krijg je van ons?

Bij Philadelphia krijg je de ruimte om jezelf te ontwikkelen én vooral te doen waar je goed in bent.

  • Salaris conform CAO Gehandicaptenzorg FWG 40: €2.951,- tot €3.980,- bruto per maand bij 36 uur;
  • Toeslagen voor onregelmatige diensten;
  • Direct een contract voor onbepaalde tijd;
  • Een dienstverband van 18 tot 20 uur per week;
  • Trainingen, cursussen en e-learnings om jezelf verder te ontwikkelen;
  • Faciliteiten om goed in je vel te blijven zitten, van coaching tot ondersteuning bij timemanagement;
  • Veel ruimte voor eigen ideeën en om samen met het team het werk te organiseren;
  • De mogelijkheid om je vakantietoeslag en/of eindejaarsuitkering maandelijks te laten uitbetalen.

Solliciteren

Zoek jij een baan als Begeleider Kind & Jeugd in Middelburg waarin begeleiding, plezier en verzorging samenkomen? En word je enthousiast van een plek waar iedere groep weer anders is?

Dan maken we graag kennis met je. Kom ontdekken waarom kort verblijf bij Phila Agaat misschien wel heel goed bij jou past.

title: MRI Quality Control Technologist
description:
About Us

At Prenuvo, we are on a mission to flip the paradigm from reactive “sick-care” to proactive health care. Our award-winning whole body scan is fast (under 1 hour), safe (MRI has no ionizing radiation), and non-invasive (no contrast). Our unique integrated stack of optimized hardware, software, and increasingly AI, coupled with the patient-centric experience of our clinics across North America, have allowed us to lead the charge against “we caught it too late again.”

The MRI Quality Control (QC) Technologist is responsible for performing quality control checks on MRI-based body composition analyses. This role ensures accuracy, consistency, and adherence to established imaging protocols and QC standards across the clinic network. The QC Technologist works closely with clinic MRI technologists across our network of Prenuvo clinics and the MRI QC Manager to maintain high standards for clinical accuracy and patient experience.

This role does not provide visa sponsorship. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and must not require employer sponsorship for a work visa (current or future).

Help reshape the world through proactive healthcare while working with cutting-edge technology and high performing teams with deep expertise - join us to make a difference in people’s lives!

What You'll Do

Quality Control Execution

  • Perform QC checks on MRI body composition imaging (fat, muscle, organ segmentation).
  • Verify that imaging outputs meet established thresholds and acceptance criteria.
  • Document and escalate deviations to the MRI QC Manager.
  • Support audits by maintaining accurate QC records and documentation.

Protocol Adherence & Process Support

  • Apply standardized imaging and QC protocols across all assigned cases.
  • Identify areas of inconsistency or error in imaging outputs.
  • Assist in updating QC processes and reference materials under manager guidance.

Collaboration & Communication

  • Communicate imaging QC findings to technologists, analysts, and clinical staff as appropriate
  • Provide feedback to MRI technologists on QC results when needed.

What You'll Bring

Education & Certification

  • Bachelor’s degree in Medical Imaging, Radiologic Sciences, or related field preferred.
  • ARRT (MR) or CAMRT certification required

Experience

  • 2+ years of experience as an MRI Technologist or in MRI image post-processing.
  • Prior QC or imaging analysis experience preferred.
  • Familiarity with MRI body composition or quantitative imaging platforms a plus.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong technical understanding of MRI imaging protocols.
  • Detail-oriented with ability to identify subtle errors or inconsistencies.
  • Proficient in QC documentation and workflow tracking tools.
  • Excellent communication and teamwork skills.

Our Values

First: we are Pioneers

  • Transforming healthcare requires divergent thinking, bias for action, disciplined experimentation, and consistent grit and determination to maintain momentum. This journey is as challenging as it is rewarding.

Second: we are Platform-Builders

  • We’re always building foundations that allow us to achieve tomorrow more than we did today. We never lose sight of what’s ahead – in a mindset of ownership and duty to our mission.

Above all: we are Patients

  • We could all be the next person who walks through our very doors, seeking clarity or peace of mind. We are proud of our impact on our patients’ lives, and we won’t stop till everyone can benefit from our work.

What We Offer

  • An avenue to make a positive impact on people's lives and their health
  • We believe in preventative healthcare for everyone, including our team - Prenuvo provides free, whole-body scans to each team member
  • Growth opportunities are at the heart of our people journey, we’re doing big things with bright minds - there is no single path to success, it can be shaped along the way
  • Building strong relationships is at the core of everything we do - our team gets together each week to connect, share, and socialize
  • Recognizing time away to restore is vital to our wellbeing - we have a flexible vacation policy and we will encourage you to use it
  • Prenuvo offers a 401(k) retirement savings plan to eligible employees, allowing team members to make pre-tax contributions toward their retirement. While Prenuvo facilitates access to the plan, the company does not currently offer matching contributions.
  • We offer a comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, vision, including Mental Health coverage, to support you and your family
  • The hourly rate for this role ranges from $42.79-$52.88 in local currency, depending upon experience and geographic location

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

As part of the hiring process, successful candidates will undergo a background check in compliance to applicable federal and state rules.

Please be advised that official communication from our recruitment team will only come from our authorized domain []. If you are contacted by a recruiter, please ensure their email address ends with @prenuvo.com. We do not use third-party recruitment services or any other email domains for hiring purposes. If you receive communication that you believe to be fraudulent, please report it immediately to jobs@prenuvo.com.

title: Electrical Lead Installer
description:
About Bell Bros:

At Bell Brothers Plumbing, Heating & Air, we are your gateway to a rewarding career in HVAC and plumbing services! We are proud to be a leading provider of heating, ventilation, air conditioning, windows, and plumbing solutions, and we believe that our success is rooted in the dedicated and passionate team members who make it all possible. We offer a culture of excellence, professional growth and development, cutting-edge technology and tools, a strong team environment, and competitive compensation and benefits.

Lead the Crew. Own the Installation.

Bell Brothers is hiring an Electrical Lead Installer who combines residential electrical expertise with strong crew leadership and pride in workmanship.

You'll lead sold residential electrical installation projects from arrival through completion, taking responsibility for safe execution, code-compliant work, crew productivity, homeowner communication, and job closeout. This is a hands-on leadership role for an experienced electrician who can organize a project, solve field challenges, and develop the people working alongside them.

How We Work

At Bell Brothers, quality installation work means completing the approved scope correctly, respecting the homeowner's property, and keeping the crew safe and productive. You'll set the standard for workmanship, jobsite organization, and professional conduct.

We expect Lead Installers to coach less-experienced electricians and apprentices through clear instruction, thoughtful delegation, and field support. You'll assign work that matches each person's capabilities while remaining accountable for the finished installation.

You'll also know when to escalate. When site conditions, material needs, or technical concerns affect the approved plan, you'll work with Electrical leadership to resolve them rather than make unauthorized changes to scope, pricing, design, or customer commitments.

What You'll Do

  • Lead residential projects including main panel replacements, service upgrades, subpanels, rewires, device replacements, dedicated circuits, system upgrades, and electrical work supporting other trades.
  • Review the approved scope, material package, photos, notes, and installation requirements before starting work.
  • Coordinate scope questions, technical concerns, material issues, and additional work requirements with the Electrical Field Supervisor or appropriate leader.
  • Plan daily installation activities and assign tasks based on crew members' skills, project requirements, and safe work practices.
  • Perform and oversee installations that meet applicable electrical codes, manufacturer requirements, company standards, and the approved scope.
  • Coach apprentices and installers while maintaining responsibility for crew performance, conduct, and overall job execution.
  • Keep homeowners informed about work progress, expected interruptions, project status, and completion.
  • Monitor productivity and communicate potential delays or material shortages early, following department processes to keep work moving.
  • Complete testing and quality checks before placing installed systems or equipment into service.
  • Complete required ServiceTitan documentation, photos, invoice summaries, signatures, payment collection, financing paperwork, and work-completed acknowledgments.
  • Identify and communicate return work, corrections, restoration, inspection items, and follow-up needs before closing the job.
  • Maintain your assigned installation vehicle, tools, equipment, and company-issued property.

What You'll Bring

  • Current California Residential Electrician Certification or higher electrical certification.
  • Residential electrical installation experience sufficient to independently lead complex projects and direct a small crew.
  • Strong knowledge of service upgrades, main panels, subpanels, rewires, device replacements, branch circuits, grounding and bonding, wiring methods, and residential electrical equipment.
  • A strong understanding of applicable electrical codes and safe installation practices.
  • Ability to lead, delegate to, and develop apprentices and other installation crew members.
  • Professional communication with homeowners, crew members, and Electrical leadership.
  • Ability to use ServiceTitan or similar field-service software and mobile technology.

Experienced residential installers, lead electricians, journeyman-level electricians, and residential service electricians with substantial installation and crew-leadership experience are encouraged to apply.

Working Conditions

This is a hands-on field role in residential properties, including occupied homes. You'll perform installation work while directing the crew, maintaining safe working conditions, and protecting the homeowner's property. Safe use of tools, equipment, and appropriate personal protective equipment is required.

#BELLP

Pay Range
$39—$49 USD

We are an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic outlined by federal, state, or local laws. Additionally, we will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the California Fair Chance Act.

Face to Face (not video or telephone) Interpretation

WHO WE ARE: Access 2 Interpreters, LLC, is the largest local interpretation & translation business in Columbus providing interpreters and translators locally and nation-wide. Our main office is located in Downtown Columbus.

As a face-to-face interpreter, you'll use your language skills to assist others during medical, social service and other types of appointments. Interpreting with Access is a great way to earn money. The more assignments you take, the more you can earn. It's perfect for those looking for a flexible schedule with good pay. Using your unique bilingual skills to help those in need who speak the language or dialect you speak is very rewarding.

What you need to know:

  • Your bilingual skills are in high demand!
  • As a contractor, you decide your own schedule!
  • Assignments are available 24/7/365! (Most assignments are requested during business hours.)
  • Take as many or as few of our available assignments as you can!

Requirements

All applicants must:

  • Be located in the Central Ohio area.
  • Have a High School Diploma or equivalent.
  • Be eligible to work in the United States.
  • Pass a Federal Criminal Background Check based on fingerprints and a 10-panel drug screening (at no cost to you).
  • Provide proof of program completion from an accredited interpreter training of at least 40 hours (e.g. Bridging the Gap, Access 2 Interpreters' "Access Academy", Court Interpretation, Certificate or Degree in interpretation from an accredited college or university).

title: Head of Social - Square
location: Bay Area, CA, United States of America
description:
As Head of Social for Square, you’ll sit within Brand Strategy & Marketing and own social as a channel: its strategy, audience, content calendar, community, and performance. This is an individual contributor role with no internal team; you’ll be the primary point of contact for social, partnering with the Brand Lead and your creative counterpart to connect Square’s positioning to the work that gets published. Your primary focus will be organic and owned content, with responsibility for advancing brand perception goals and partnering with paid teams so organic and paid reinforce each other.

You Will

  • Set the social strategy for Square. Define what social is for, what it does that other channels cannot, and what it is deliberately not for. Connect that strategy to Square’s positioning in partnership with the Brand Lead.
  • Define the audience and measures of success. Identify who Square is talking to on social, what they care about, and where they spend time. Make that understanding the foundation of the strategy, and establish the channel’s key success metric and the rationale behind it.
  • Build and own the social content calendar. Plan for major brand campaigns and moments alongside a consistent, always-on content program, showing how both support Square’s brand perception goals.
  • Bring cross-team activity into social with intent. Work with partnerships, the Brand Lead, and other teams to identify what belongs on social and how it should show up. Be the primary point of contact for requests and make decisions about channel fit.
  • Partner with paid social and media teams. Ensure organic and paid activity reinforce each other as part of a connected approach.
  • Shape the role of creators and influencers. Identify where they can credibly support Square’s social strategy, audience, and campaign goals. Partner with Partnerships, Brand, Demand Generation, Legal, and agencies on recommendations, vetting, briefing, disclosure guidance, and performance readouts.
  • Take content from idea to publication. Work with your creative counterpart to develop and publish content, balancing strategic intent, quality, and the pace social demands.
  • Own community management. Define how Square shows up in replies, comments, and direct messages, and maintain a consistent brand voice in partnership with creative.
  • Turn social listening into action. Monitor conversations about the brand, campaigns, product launches, category, competitors, and emerging issues. Translate those signals into clear readouts, recommendations, and escalation notes for partner teams.
  • Apply judgment to trends and timely opportunities. Know what is moving on social, assess its relevance to Square’s positioning, and move quickly on opportunities that fit while passing on those that do not.
  • Support Communications-led crisis and issues management. Monitor inbound activity and sentiment shifts, recommend channel responses, route urgent issues, and help protect owned channels through Sprinklr workflows or moderation guidance.
  • Be accountable for channel performance. Track progress against the agreed success metric and Square’s brand perception goals, alongside content consistency and quality, campaign integration, community health, and the effectiveness of cross-team partnerships.

You Have

  • 8 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 6 years and a Master’s degree; or a PhD with 3 years experience; or equivalent experience.
  • Exceptional communication skills: you make strategy clear and concise, and write confidently in a brand’s voice.
  • Deep understanding of your audience, including the references, formats, and conversations that matter to them.
  • Strong judgment about trends and their relevance to brand positioning, with the ability to distinguish a meaningful opportunity from something the brand should pass on.
  • The ability to move quickly, make sound decisions, and publish work without unnecessary process.
  • Strength in both strategy and execution: you can develop the channel strategy and publish the post.
  • Strong partnership skills and experience working with brand leads, creative partners, partnerships, and paid teams without direct reporting authority.
  • A track record of building and running organic, owned social channels, with clear examples of what you grew and why it worked.

Job Description

Job Title: Senior Maintenance and Utilities Technician
Location: Lexington, Massachusetts


About the role:

As a Senior Maintenance and Utilities Technician, you will work within the Site Engineering organization to ensure the safe, compliant, and reliable operation of critical process equipment, manufacturing systems, and utility infrastructure supporting Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) manufacturing operations. You will perform advanced maintenance, troubleshooting, operational monitoring, alarm response, and non-routine event triage to maintain plant readiness, maximize equipment reliability, and minimize risks to product supply, quality, safety, and regulatory compliance. Working closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Validation, and external service providers, you will take ownership of equipment performance, support operational continuity, and drive continuous improvement while maintaining high standards of safety, documentation, and compliance.


How you will contribute:

  • Respond to alarms, abnormal conditions, and non-routine equipment or utility events by assessing priorities, communicating operational impacts, and ensuring timely escalation, coordination, and documentation.
  • Serve as the primary operational contact during assigned shifts by triaging issues, screening calls, prioritizing responses, determining resource requirements, and coordinating support to minimize disruptions to manufacturing operations.
  • Monitor, maintain, and take ownership of process equipment and utility systems to ensure continuous plant readiness, proactively identifying and addressing performance deviations.
  • Execute maintenance and reliability activities in accordance with site safety requirements, current GMP (cGMP) standards, and regulatory expectations, including hazard assessments, proper personal protective equipment (PPE) use, and adherence to approved procedures.
  • Maintain accurate, complete, and timely documentation, including work orders, logbooks, maintenance and calibration records, alarm and event reports, and other GMP records required to support compliant, audit-ready operations.
  • Partner with Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Validation, contractors, vendors, and equipment manufacturers to troubleshoot issues, improve equipment reliability, and ensure work is completed safely, compliantly, and right-first-time.
  • Provide technical leadership, guidance, and knowledge transfer to peers and contractors, promoting accountability, collaboration, and high standards of workmanship.
  • Identify and support reliability and continuous improvement initiatives by analyzing equipment performance data and operational trends to strengthen maintenance strategies, improve equipment reliability, and reduce operational risk.
  • Support the maintenance, operation, and troubleshooting of process equipment and critical utility systems, including water for injection (WFI), reverse osmosis (RO), autoclaves, clean utilities, chromatography systems, ultrafiltration skids, and other GMP manufacturing support systems, as applicable.
  • Support inspection and audit readiness by maintaining compliant maintenance practices and documentation, using computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS), and following site procedures for safety, confined space entry, and other assigned activities.

What you bring to Takeda:

  • High school diploma or equivalent with 4–8 years of relevant experience, or technical certification, associate degree, military technical training, or equivalent technical education in a related field with at least 3 years of relevant experience.
  • Demonstrated competency in maintaining, operating, and troubleshooting process equipment and critical utility systems, including WFI, RO, autoclaves, clean utilities, chromatography systems, ultrafiltration skids, and other GMP manufacturing support systems, as applicable.
  • Advanced troubleshooting and diagnostic skills for process and utility systems, with the ability to interpret technical documentation, including piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), equipment drawings, and technical manuals.
  • Strong understanding of cGMP requirements, maintenance documentation, regulatory compliance, and audit readiness, with demonstrated ownership of equipment performance, operational readiness, and work quality.
  • Proficiency in preventive and corrective maintenance execution and computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS), along with the ability to use digital tools and electronic business systems supporting procurement, safety, maintenance, and quality management.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision, manage competing priorities in a dynamic environment, and collaborate effectively with Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, contractors, and other stakeholders.
  • Strong commitment to safety, compliance, and continuous improvement, with the ability to guide peers and contractors. Ability to obtain and maintain an Industrial 1I or higher Massachusetts Wastewater Operator license as required by site needs, and to perform or support confined space entry activities when applicable and authorized. Ability to meet physical requirements, including wearing required PPE, gowning for pharmaceutical manufacturing areas, lifting, pushing, or pulling up to 50 pounds, standing for extended periods, climbing ladders and working from platforms, bending or stooping to troubleshoot equipment, handling approved site chemicals, and traveling or working across Massachusetts Bio Ops facilities as required.

Important Considerations

At Takeda, our patients rely on us to deliver quality products. As a result, we must follow strict rules in our manufacturing facilities to ensure we are not endangering the quality of the product. In this role, you may:

  • Work in a controlled environment requiring special gowning and wear protective clothing over the head, face, hands, feet and body. This may include additional hearing protection for loud areas.
  • Need to remove all make-up, jewelry, contact lenses, nail polish and/or artificial fingernails while in the manufacturing environment.
  • Work in a cold, wet environment.
  • Work multiple shifts, including weekends, or be asked to work supplemental hours, as necessary.
  • Work around chemicals such as alcohol, acids, buffers and Celite that may require respiratory protection.

This is an on-site role in Lexington, Massachusetts, required to support GMP manufacturing operations, plant readiness, and shift coverage needs.


More about us:

At Takeda, we are transforming patient care through the development of novel specialty pharmaceuticals and best in class patient support programs. Takeda is a patient-focused company that will inspire and empower you to grow through life-changing work.

Certified as a Global Top Employer, Takeda offers stimulating careers, encourages innovation, and strives for excellence in everything we do. We foster an inclusive, collaborative workplace, in which our teams are united by an unwavering commitment to deliver Better Health and a Brighter Future to people around the world.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Senior Endpoint Administrator serves as a critical technical leader responsible for the security, scalability, performance, and lifecycle management of enterprise endpoint environments across Windows and Apple platforms. This role owns endpoint governance, compliance, automation, deployment, patching, and modern workplace technologies that directly impact workforce productivity, operational resilience, and regulatory readiness. Leveraging AI as a force multiplier, the position accelerates decision-making, improves service quality, enhances operational scale, and increases automation effectiveness. Operating within Empower’s hyper-growth, highly regulated 503A/503B environment, the role partners across Infrastructure, Security, Cloud, and Service Operations to deliver secure, compliant, and efficient endpoint services. Success requires talent characterized by strategic thinking, execution rigor, technical depth, accountability, continuous learning agility, and a relentless commitment to operational excellence.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Endpoint Administration

  • Platform Management: Administer and optimize enterprise endpoint platforms across Windows and macOS environments, including Microsoft Intune, Jamf Pro, Apple Business Manager, and Autopilot. Execute endpoint configuration, policy management, deployment, compliance monitoring, and lifecycle activities that support secure, scalable operations. Leverage AI-enabled insights and automation capabilities to improve service quality, accelerate issue resolution, enhance decision-making, and increase operational efficiency while maintaining alignment with organizational standards and regulatory requirements.
  • Device Lifecycle: Execute end-to-end device lifecycle processes including provisioning, imaging, deployment, onboarding, refresh planning, retirement, and asset governance activities. Ensure devices are deployed securely, efficiently, and consistently while maintaining compliance with established standards. Utilize automation, workflow optimization, and AI-assisted operational tools to reduce manual effort, improve deployment speed, increase accuracy, and support workforce productivity across a rapidly growing enterprise environment.
  • Application Delivery: Manage application packaging, deployment, maintenance, updates, and retirement activities across supported endpoint platforms. Ensure software availability, compatibility, performance, and compliance while minimizing business disruption and operational risk. Apply automation, analytics, and AI-enabled operational capabilities to improve deployment success rates, identify issues proactively, streamline software delivery processes, and enhance the overall end-user technology experience at scale.

Security and Operational Excellence

  • Security Compliance: Maintain endpoint security controls, compliance standards, vulnerability remediation activities, and endpoint protection capabilities across the enterprise environment. Execute security policies, monitor compliance status, support audit readiness, and partner with cybersecurity teams to address identified risks. Utilize AI-driven analytics and automation tools to improve threat visibility, accelerate remediation efforts, strengthen security posture, and support ongoing regulatory compliance requirements.
  • Patch Management: Administer enterprise patch management processes for operating systems, applications, and endpoint technologies. Coordinate testing, deployment, validation, and remediation activities to ensure timely patch implementation while minimizing operational impact. Leverage automation platforms, predictive insights, and AI-assisted prioritization to improve deployment effectiveness, reduce vulnerabilities, strengthen endpoint reliability, and maintain a secure and compliant technology environment.
  • Process Improvement: Develop, document, and enhance operational procedures, technical standards, runbooks, and support documentation that improve consistency, scalability, and service maturity. Identify opportunities to streamline workflows, eliminate inefficiencies, and strengthen operational controls. Apply data-driven analysis, automation capabilities, and AI-enabled recommendations to improve productivity, reduce recurring issues, and support continuous improvement across endpoint management operations.

Technical Support and Collaboration

  • Advanced Support: Provide advanced Tier 2 and Tier 3 endpoint support for complex technical issues impacting end users, devices, and endpoint services. Perform root cause analysis, implement sustainable solutions, and restore service with urgency and precision. Utilize AIenabled troubleshooting tools and operational insights to accelerate diagnosis, improve resolution quality, reduce downtime, and enhance the overall support experience.
  • Infrastructure Integration: Support endpoint integration with infrastructure, cloud, virtualization, networking, identity, and collaboration platforms. Partner with cross-functional technology teams to ensure endpoint services remain secure, connected, reliable, and scalable. Contribute technical expertise to modernization initiatives while leveraging automation and AI-assisted analysis to improve interoperability, performance, and operational effectiveness across enterprise technology environments.
  • Knowledge Sharing: Serve as a trusted endpoint subject matter expert by providing technical guidance, mentoring support personnel, and promoting knowledge transfer across IT Operations teams. Maintain comprehensive documentation, support resources, and operational knowledge repositories that improve organizational effectiveness. Leverage AI-enabled knowledge management capabilities to enhance information accessibility, accelerate issue resolution, and support continuous learning and technical excellence.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Advanced expertise administering Microsoft Intune, Jamf Pro, Apple Business Manager, Windows 10/11, macOS, Autopilot, endpoint deployment technologies, and enterprise device lifecycle management platforms.
  • Strong understanding of endpoint security, compliance management, vulnerability remediation, patch management, Active Directory, Entra ID, Group Policy, and enterprise governance practices.
  • Advanced automation and scripting capabilities utilizing PowerShell and related technologies to improve operational efficiency, scalability, service quality, and endpoint administration effectiveness.
  • Ability to leverage AI-enabled tools, analytics, and automation platforms to improve decision-making, accelerate problem resolution, enhance productivity, and drive operational excellence.
  • Strong collaboration, communication, stakeholder management, and organization skills.

EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5–8+ years of endpoint administration, desktop engineering, or systems administration experience.

title: VP, Financial Planning & Analysis
description:
OnPoint is the largest community owned credit union in Oregon – and we’re growing! Our growth provides great opportunities for you to reach your personal and professional goals. We value enthusiasm, commitment to outstanding performance, and providing opportunities to truly make a difference. If you are looking to join a team of dedicated, collaborative, and passionate individuals, OnPoint is looking for our next VP, Financial Planning & Analysis. We invite you to explore and grow your career with us!

JOB SUMMARY:
The VP, Financial Planning & Analysis leads the credit union’s enterprise-wide financial planning, forecasting, performance management, and strategic decision-support capabilities. Reporting to the Vice President of Strategic Finance, this role translates enterprise direction into actionable financial plans, analysis, and performance insights. The VP serves as the organization’s primary FP&A partner, helping leaders understand financial implications, evaluate opportunities and tradeoffs, and connect resource decisions to OnPoint’s strategy and commitment to members’ financial well-being. The VP is accountable for the quality, integrity, and effectiveness of the FP&A function, including its people, processes, systems, analytics, and governance.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

Lead enterprise-wide annual budgeting, recurring forecasting, reforecasting, and long-range planning that translates OnPoint’s strategy and member commitments into clear financial priorities, coordinated timelines, stakeholder input, quality reviews, and deliverables across a highly collaborative organization.
Lead integrated financial forecasting by defining, documenting, validating, and aligning assumptions, business drivers, performance targets, and planning scenarios across revenue, expenses, loan and deposit growth, and other key financial and operational drivers. Partner with Treasury to incorporate approved balance-sheet, capital, liquidity, funding, and interest-rate assumptions into consistent and accurate organization-wide forecasts.
Lead, develop, and retain a high-performing FP&A team by setting clear expectations, strengthening technical and business partnership capabilities, investing in each employee’s growth, and building succession depth within the function. Foster an inclusive, collaborative culture grounded in service, curiosity, continuous improvement, and high-quality execution.
Lead improvements to FP&A forecasting methods, planning tools, data quality, reporting automation, self-service analytics, governance controls, and business processes. Partner with Data, Technology, Accounting, Treasury, Risk, Strategy, and other functions to standardize inputs, strengthen variance analysis and back testing, and improve the accuracy, efficiency, and usefulness of planning and performance insights.
Advise leadership by providing objective analysis, financial modeling, and recommendations for major business, operating, capital, investment, and incentive-plan decisions, including assessment of profitability, return on investment, risks, tradeoffs, and potential financial outcomes. Evaluate profitability, return on investment, risks, tradeoffs, potential financial outcomes, and expected value for OnPoint’s members and communities, and elevate enterprise-level recommendations to the Vice President of Strategic Finance and executive leadership.
Establish and maintain performance measurement frameworks, executive dashboards, scorecards, key performance indicators, variance and profitability analysis, and reporting tools that provide meaningful visibility into organizational performance and future outlooks.
Collaborate with Finance and business and functional leaders to support budgeting, financial projections, business cases, initiative valuation, expense management, leadership reporting, and enterprise forecast alignment; lead cross-functional planning discussions that surface tradeoffs, encourage healthy debate, and align priorities, resources, assumptions, and actions.
Translate complex financial information into clear, compelling stories and recommendations that help leaders make informed decisions. Prepare executive and Board reporting in partnership with the Vice President of Strategic Finance, and present FP&A insights as requested, connecting financial outcomes to strategy, risk, member impact, and organizational priorities.
Monitor relevant economic, regulatory, competitive, and financial-services trends and incorporate their implications into plans, forecasts, and recommendations.
Perform additional projects, responsibilities, or duties as assigned.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & COMPETENCIES:

Enterprise-level financial and business acumen, with the ability to connect enterprise priorities, operations, risk, and financial performance.
Executive presence and the ability to communicate complex financial matters clearly, credibly, and persuasively to senior leaders and governing bodies.
Strategic judgment and analytical rigor, including the ability to challenge assumptions, evaluate alternatives, and influence decisions through data and insight.
Advanced expertise in financial modeling, forecasting, scenario analysis, performance management, and management reporting.
Ability to build trusted cross-functional partnerships, lead through influence, and drive organizational accountability.
Proven people leadership, change leadership, integrity, sound judgment, and discretion.

MIN QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, economics, business administration, or a related field is required or additional relevant experience in lieu of a degree;
10 years of progressively responsible experience in financial planning and analysis, corporate finance, accounting, or related financial leadership roles within financial services.
5 years of people leadership experience, including responsibility for building teams, developing talent, and leading enterprise-level planning or performance-management processes.
Demonstrated experience advising senior executives and presenting complex financial analysis and recommendations to executive or governing audiences.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Master of Business Administration or advanced degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related discipline.
CPA, CFA, CTP, or other relevant professional certification.
Leadership experience within a credit union, bank, or other financial services organization.

We take care of our Members, and OnPoint takes care of us by offering employees a generous vacation package, incentives, competitive hourly pay, 100% - paid employee medical, dental and vision premiums, Tri-Met / parking passes, 401k matching, tuition reimbursement and more!

title: Counselor Resident / Social Work Fellow
description:
Counselor Resident / Social Work Fellow

Backpack Healthcare | Residency Program | Fully Remote

About Backpack Healthcare

At Backpack Healthcare, we believe every child and family deserves access to high-quality, compassionate mental health care. We are a clinician-led, minority-owned behavioral health organization providing accessible, whole-family mental health services to children, adolescents, and young adults through telehealth.

We understand that every individual carries an invisible backpack filled with experiences, emotions, and challenges. Our mission is to help lighten that load by connecting families with the support they need to thrive.

We're looking for passionate, motivated early-career clinicians to join our Residency Program as a Counselor Resident or Social Work Fellow. This is an opportunity to strengthen your clinical skills, gain supervised experience, and work toward independent licensure while making a meaningful difference in the lives of children and families.

About the Role

Counselor Residents and Social Work Fellows provide telehealth-based therapy to children, adolescents, and families while completing the supervised clinical hours required for independent licensure. You'll receive clinical supervision, participate in structured training and professional development, and collaborate with an interdisciplinary team committed to delivering high-quality, trauma-informed care.

The title of your position will align with your licensure track, but both roles share the same core responsibilities and program expectations.

Available Tracks:

  • Counselor Resident: For clinicians pursuing independent counseling licensure.

  • Social Work Fellow: For clinicians pursuing independent clinical social work licensure.

Part-Time and Full-Time Opportunities Available

  • Part-Time: Minimum of 15 client contact hours per week.

  • Full-Time: Minimum of 25 client contact hours per week.

What You'll Do

  • Provide Clinical Care: Deliver individual, family, and group therapy via telehealth to children, adolescents, and families.

  • Conduct Assessments: Complete intake assessments, risk assessments, treatment plans, and safety plans under the guidance of your assigned Clinical Supervisor.

  • Maintain Timely Documentation: Complete accurate, thorough clinical documentation within 24 hours of each session, following all organizational and regulatory requirements.

  • Participate in Supervision: Attend scheduled individual and group supervision sessions, actively engage in case consultations, and consistently track clinical and supervision hours.

  • Engage in Professional Development: Complete the Backpack Residency Program curriculum, including didactic training, case consultations, and licensure exam preparation.

  • Collaborate Across Teams: Partner with clinical leadership, care coordination, and administrative teams to promote continuity of care and support positive client outcomes.

  • Prioritize Compliance and Safety: Follow HIPAA requirements, applicable state licensing regulations, ethical standards, and Backpack's clinical policies and procedures.

  • Build Your Clinical Expertise: Apply feedback, participate in required training, and demonstrate consistent progress toward independent licensure.

What We're Looking For

  • A master's degree in Social Work, Counseling, or a related mental health field, either completed or in the final term of your program.

  • An active provisional, associate-level, or equivalent license that aligns with your residency track:

    • Social Work Fellow: LMSW or state-equivalent provisional/associate social work license.

    • Counselor Resident: LGPC or state-equivalent provisional/associate counseling license.

  • Current residence and licensure in a state where Backpack Healthcare operates.

  • Commitment to completing all supervised clinical hours and licensure milestones required for independent practice.

  • A strong interest in working with children, adolescents, and families.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • A willingness to receive feedback, engage in supervision, and continuously develop your clinical skills.

  • Strong clinical judgment, professionalism, cultural humility, and a commitment to ethical, identity-affirming care.

What Success Looks Like

Successful residents and fellows demonstrate consistent growth in clinical competence, professional judgment, and confidence in delivering effective care. You'll be expected to:

  • Meet your designated weekly client contact hour requirements.

  • Complete all clinical documentation within 24 hours of each session.

  • Attend all scheduled individual and group supervision sessions and log hours weekly.

  • Make steady progress toward licensure milestones in partnership with your Clinical Supervisor.

  • Participate actively in training, case consultations, and exam preparation.

  • Meet quarterly performance expectations for clinical development, documentation quality, and professional conduct.

Work Environment

This is a fully remote, telehealth-based position. Team members must have a private, HIPAA-compliant workspace, reliable high-speed internet, and the ability to conduct scheduled video sessions in a professional environment.

Why Join Backpack Healthcare?

  • Grow With Support: Receive structured supervision, clinical guidance, and professional development as you work toward independent licensure.

  • Make a Meaningful Impact: Support children, adolescents, and families as they navigate mental health challenges and build healthier futures.

  • Learn Through Collaboration: Work alongside a multidisciplinary team that values clinical excellence, teamwork, and compassionate care.

  • Build Your Career: Strengthen your clinical foundation through hands-on experience, case consultation, and licensure exam preparation.

  • Be Part of a Mission-Driven Team: Join an organization working to make quality mental health care more accessible to the families who need it most.

Backpack Healthcare is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity in age, background, identity, experience, ability, and perspective — and we're committed to creating a team that reflects the communities we serve.

title: Analyst, Financial Planning & Analysis
description:
Who We Are & What We Do
At Helix, our mission is simple: to help everyone improve their lives through their DNA.

Ready to make a real-world impact with your skills? At Helix, we're transforming healthcare by making genomics a standard of care. We partner with health systems and life science companies to accelerate the integration of genomic data into clinical practice. Join us in building a future where healthcare is personalized, proactive, and powered by genomics.

What is special about this role?
As a Senior FP&A Analyst at Helix, you'll own operating expense planning, reporting, and forecasting for the Finance team.
Your work will shape strategic decisions and optimize how we spend across the company.
Beyond traditional FP&A, you'll design and support the systems behind our numbers, including NetSuite, our procurement platform, and our CRM.

AI is now core to how our Finance team works, not an add-on. We're looking for someone who already treats it as a real part of their toolkit and wants to grow further against Helix's Finance AI Fluency framework.

You'll thrive in our fast-paced startup environment, where autonomy and ambition directly shape our mission.

As a Senior FP&A Analyst, you will:
  • Financial Modeling & Forecasting:
    • Own the operating expense planning, reporting, and forecasting process, working closely with budget owners across the organization.
    • Own comprehensive budget and forecast models, collaborating closely with internal stakeholders to set and achieve financial targets.
    • Support the monthly closing process, including actual-to-budget bridge analysis and specific deep dives of other key accounts.
    • Use AI to produce first-draft variance commentary and bridge analysis, grounded in our specific GL data and accounting policies.
    • Communicate financial results and actionable insights to budget owners and leadership, driving informed decision-making.
    • Ensure compliance with our finance and accounting policies, and understand legal and GAAP business requirements.
  • System Architecture & Data Management:
    • Design and support our core business systems, including NetSuite (ERP), our procurement system (Ramp), and our CRM system (Hubspot), ensuring seamless operation and data flow.
    • Partner with key stakeholders throughout the organization to maintain and improve data integrity across all systems, ensuring accuracy of actuals and forecasts for both financial and operational reporting.
    • Develop scalable processes and procedures within these systems to support Helix's fast-growing business lines.
  • Reporting & Insights:
    • Create, maintain, and enhance reporting decks and dashboards, including those for Board-level and investor presentations.
    • Transform complex data into clear, concise, and actionable insights, effectively telling the story behind the numbers.
    • Build and maintain reusable AI workflows and skills for recurring reporting tasks, so good practices scale across the team.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration:
    • Partner with stakeholders across several departments to inform strategic decision-making and drive company growth.
    • Work effectively as part of cross-geographic, cross-organizational, and cross-cultural teams.

About you:
  • Experience: Typically 5+ years of relevant financial planning and analysis experience.
  • Systems Expertise: Demonstrated experience managing, designing, and troubleshooting key financial and operational systems like NetSuite (ERP), procurement platforms (Ramp), and CRM systems (Hubspot), ideally with prior admin-level access and responsibility.

title: Everyday AI Agent Tester
description:
Role Title: Everyday AI Agent Tester

Role Type: Contractor

Location: U.S based


Opportunity Snapshot


Pay: $25-45/hour

Time per task: ~1.5 hours per run (evidence and scoring included)

Project kickoff: Monday, October 12

Onboarding: Today (Fri), Saturday, or Sunday, so you’re ready to start Monday

You’ll need: An active personal popular AI account (Free, Go, or Plus; not Pro), an active personal and a smartphone that can screen record

Your tasks: Run everyday errands with two AI agents, approve key steps, screen record, and score the results


About the role


AI agents are starting to handle real-life errands: paying bills, booking trips, doing the groceries. We want to know how well they actually do it, from the point of view of a real user. That’s you.

You’ll test two AI agents side by side, using your own accounts on your phone, and tell us what worked, what didn’t, and how it felt.


What you’ll do

  1. Run real-life scenarios: bills, returns, email follow-ups, bookings, shopping, groceries, travel, family logistics, outings, and forms
  2. Approve or stop the agent at key steps
  3. Screen record every attempt
  4. Score each run on completion, quality, control issues, satisfaction, and time
  5. Share clear written feedback on the agent experience

Who we’re looking for

  1. US-based, with a Bachelor’s degree
  2. Someone who already uses AI in daily life
  3. 2-3 years of experience, preferably in engineering, business management, or office/operations
  4. Detail-oriented, great at following instructions and documenting each step
  5. Clear written communication
  6. Generalists welcome, domain experts preferred
  7. No coding or AI background needed


Why you’ll like it

  1. Get paid to use the AI tools you already use
  2. Work entirely from your phone, on your schedule
  3. Have a direct say in how next-generation AI agents get built and improved


How the selection process works

  1. Apply
  2. Complete the screening questions
  3. Interview: 15-30 minutes max
  4. Profile review: if everything looks good, we present you to the client
  5. Onboarding: our Talent Ops team will contact you to get you started

title: Creative Strategy Lead - Copy (Hybrid)
description:
We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas or take over sponsorship at this time.

About the Role

This is a high-ownership role at the center of how Enova Studios uses data to shape creative work. We're rapidly evolving how we deliver content across the business, and we need a creative strategy lead who can build the bridge between performance insight and creative execution. You'll report to and partner closely with the Associate Creative Director, bringing a data-driven lens that complements the ACD's storytelling and craft leadership. Together you'll set creative strategy, surface risks and drive the strategic roadmap for the copy team. You'll be the connective tissue between Enova Studios and our marketing and business teams, bringing back what's working and translating it into stronger creative across OnDeck, CashNetUSA and NetCredit.

About Enova Studios

Enova Studios is the in-house creative agency for Enova's small business and consumer lending brands: OnDeck, NetCredit, CashNetUSA, Simplic and more. We bring Creative, Content, Code and UX capabilities together under one roof. Leveraging deep brand knowledge, cross-functional relationships and strategic context, we turn customer insights into work that drives real results.

About You

You've built a career in copy and creative, but these days you're more interested in why the work performs than how it reads. You know what makes people click, apply or scroll past, and you can back it up with data. You understand how creative teams work and where good strategy gets diluted in production, which is why you're the one who brings the numbers into the room and turns them into ideas a copy team can run with.If you're energized by connecting performance data to creative decisions and raising the bar for a copy team, this role could be a great fit.

What You'll Do

You'll own the creative strategy behind Enova's portfolio of brands and the loop that connects performance data to the work. Storytelling sits inside that loop: you'll define the story from the data, then manage and coach a small team of copywriters to tell it well.

  • Insight in: Pull performance data and business insights from marketing and channel partners.
  • Strategy set: Turn insight into the narrative and messaging direction.
  • Coach execution: Guide writers to bring that story to life, editing for both craft and strategic fit.
  • Measures back: Absorb results, learn what worked and feed it into the next brief.
  • Insight to Creative: Partner with marketing and business teams to gather performance results, customer insights and channel learnings, then translate them into creative strategy, briefs and recommendations. Give creative leadership a clear view of what's working, what isn't and what to prioritize next.
  • Testing Strategy: Work with channel owners and marketers to develop testing strategies and learning agendas. Shape concepts built to be tested, iterated and scaled, and feed results into the next round of work.
  • Creative & Brand Strategy: Ground campaigns in clear strategic pillars and messaging frameworks across channels, keeping each brand distinctive and on-voice.
  • Paid Social Evolution: Drive how we build paid social campaigns partnering with design, marketing and business teams to concept ideas from the ground up and optimize them based on performance.
  • Team Leadership: Manage and mentor a small team of copywriters, using data and AI tools to sharpen and accelerate their work. Own team processes and resources and evolve how the team operates as needs change.
  • Hands-On Contribution: Step in on high-priority work when needed, whether that's shaping a concept or pressure-testing a headline against what the data says.
  • Stakeholder Communication: Present strategic recommendations clearly and persuasively, using data to make the case and keep creative and business priorities aligned.

Requirements

  • 8+ years of experience in creative strategy, content strategy, or copywriting leadership
  • Experience using performance marketing data to shape creative strategy and testing
  • Experience working in a highly regulated industry, preferably banking or financial services
  • Proven experience operating across both strategy and creative execution
  • Strong copywriting and editing skills, with a portfolio that shows conceptual thinking and results
  • Direct experience managing, mentoring, and developing copywriters or creative team members
  • Comfort with tools such as Asana, Figma, Adobe Analytics, Meta Ads Manager and Snowflake

Competencies

  • Analytical Storytelling: Frame a problem, uncover the insight, and translate data into a narrative that moves people to act.
  • Test-and-Learn Mindset: Treat creative as a hypothesis, design tests with channel partners and let results shape what comes next.
  • Strategic Range: Operate from campaign pillar down to headline and know which altitude a given problem needs.
  • Collaborative Leadership: Develop writers and build frameworks that keep a team's output consistent without flattening it.
  • AI Fluency: Use AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT to accelerate ideation and execution, sharpen concepts, and streamline how a team works, including ownership of existing messaging and copy bots.
  • Cultural Fluency A genuine, current pulse on trends, platforms, and shifting audience behavior, applied to real creative decisions.

Compensation

  • The budgeted annual salary range for this position is $90,000 - $115,000. Actual annual salary will be determined based on qualifications, skills, experience, and level assessed during the hiring process and may fall outside of the range shown. Additional compensation for this role may include a bonus. All full-time employees are eligible to participate in Company benefits, described in more detail here.

title: PER DIEM - School-Based Therapist
description:
PER DIEM School-Based Therapist - Oakland, CA Area

Transforming student mental health in schools.

About Effective School Solutions

Effective School Solutions (ESS) is a leading provider of school-based mental health services, serving 6,000+ K–12 students across 12 states.

We deliver the level of clinical care typically found in private practice, out-of-district placements, or higher levels of care directly within public schools- providing a full continuum of clinical programming, professional development, and district consultation.

Position Type: Per Diem

Hourly Rate: $55.00-$62.00/hour

This is a per diem position and is not eligible for benefits. Per diem therapist support ESS on an as-needed basis, including coverage for leave assignments (e.g., medical or maternity leave).

Therapist in this role have flexibility in their level of commitment. They may choose to pick up occasional shifts, work a few days per week on an ongoing basis, or take on a temporary full-time schedule when covering a longer-term leave assignment. Per diem clinicians can accept or decline assignments based on their availability.

This role does not follow a consistent full-time schedule; however, full-time hours may be required on a temporary basis when covering extended leave assignments.

Why This Role Matters

You’ll provide critical mental health support to students who may not otherwise have access to care—helping them succeed academically, build resilience, and thrive.

At ESS, clinicians are trusted partners in shaping supportive school environments.

Responsibilities

Direct Clinical Care & Family Support

  • Provide comprehensive, school-based mental health services, including individual, group, and family therapy, as well as intake, diagnostic, and clinical assessments
  • Partner with families and facilitate parent support programming
  • Conduct risk assessments and crisis intervention, ensuring student safety and coordinating referrals to appropriate levels of care when needed
  • Develop and implement individualized, evidence-based treatment plans that support students’ emotional, behavioral, and academic success

Supervision, Training & Collaboration

  • Oversee the day-to-day clinical operations of the assigned school-based program
  • Serve as the primary clinical point of contact for school partners, providing expert guidance, ensuring alignment on student support strategies, and fostering strong, collaborative relationships.
  • Facilitate weekly consultation sessions to ensure alignment on student goals and documentation standards
  • Collaborate with families, school staff, and interdisciplinary teams to deliver coordinated care, and provide consultation, coaching, and training on mental health and trauma-informed practices
  • Participate in team meetings, supervision, and ongoing professional development

Documentation, Compliance & Professional Expectations

  • Maintain timely, accurate clinical documentation in accordance with regulatory, ethical, and organizational standards
  • Uphold professional standards by maintaining active licensure, ethical practice, reliability, and a strong professional presence
  • Monitor program performance and ensure alignment with ESS clinical and operational standards
  • Support clinician performance through feedback, coaching, and evaluations

Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in Social Work, Counseling, or a related field
  • Active associate number or clinical license (e.g., AMFT, APCC, ACSW or LMFT, LPCC, LCSW) in the state of California
  • 2+ years of experience working with children and/or adolescents with behavioral and emotional needs
  • Experience providing training and coaching to educational professionals and parents/caregivers on student mental health issues.
  • Experience working with schools, families, and community-based services (school-based experience preferred)
  • Demonstrated ability to build and maintain trusting relationships with students, families, and school staff
  • Commitment to delivering high-quality, evidence-based care and advocating for best practices
  • Proven ability to positively influence, motivate, and elevate team members and stakeholders
  • Ability to make confident, sound decisions in ambiguous or evolving situations
  • Proficient in clinical documentation and use of electronic systems (e.g., EMR, Microsoft Office), with the ability to maintain accurate and timely records

Why Clinicians Choose ESS

✔ School-day schedule — No weekends; occasional evening hours as needed to support family engagement
✔ Light summers
✔ Small caseloads
✔ Ongoing clinical support, and free CEUs
✔ Competitive Pay
✔ Clinical leadership at the heart of our company

Make a meaningful impact on student mental health.
Join Effective School Solutions

dit breng je mee


Je houdt van mensen en wilt klanten echt helpen. Je bent nieuwsgierig, durft initiatief te nemen en krijgt energie van samenwerken. Je hebt gevoel voor service én voor verkopen. Ook als het druk is, blijf je vriendelijk en betrokken. Je ziet kansen en pakt ze, durft te leren van feedback en draagt actief bij aan een goede werksfeer. Kortom: je kijkt verder dan je takenlijstje en bent graag van waarde – voor de klant én je team.

jij maakt HEMA echt


Bij HEMA werken we met ruim 17.000 collega’s aan een beter alledaags leven in een mooiere wereld. Met producten die praktischer, mooier, beter zijn en ook nog eens langer meegaan. Én met kleurrijke winkels in dorpen, steden en online. We zijn trots op hoe ver we zijn gekomen, maar we zijn nog niet tevreden. HEMA is weer écht HEMA en klaar voor de volgende stap. Onze ambitie? Koploper worden in een uitdagende markt. Dat doen we samen, als één team, met trotse collega’s, ondernemers en partners. Door te spelen om te winnen. Dat betekent dat je nieuwsgierig bent, kansen grijpt, met plezier samenwerkt en altijd gaat voor het beste resultaat. Je durft jezelf uit te spreken en anderen uit te dagen om samen beter te worden. Jij kunt met jouw unieke bijdrage meebouwen aan het HEMA van morgen. Jij maakt HEMA echt. Doe je mee?

title: Clinical Specialist
description:
Clinical Specialist Looking for rewarding work in an organization dedicated to making a positive impact in the lives of others? Bring your clinical and interpersonal skills to a team-based workplace that puts people first. As the Clinical Specialist, you will provide services in residential, vocational, or in-home settings, providing invaluable support to the individuals you serve.

Ensure that support plans and services adhere to Individual Plans, quality standards, and regulatory requirements.
Complete structured assessment interviews with parents/care providers.
Conduct observation of the individual in appropriate settings such as home, school, or community.
Review social history information, complete functional assessments, and target appropriate behavior baseline information for each referred individual.
Write and submit a summary of assessment and recommended behavior support plan components to interdisciplinary team (IDT) or operations leader, as applicable.
Advocate for the human and civil rights of individuals receiving services from the agency by attending and presenting behavior support plan information to review committees.
Document progress and activity; review records and logs to stay abreast of changes in service plans; maintain confidentiality; complete billing documentation as applicable; organize and record all documentation in an accurate and timely manner.
Maintain healthy and professional relationships with individuals, friends, families, guardians, and case managers; implement the company’s Customer Service Standards.
Report any instance of alleged abuse or neglect according to internal and external standards; report medical, behavioral, and other incidents following company policy and external requirements.
Maintain confidentiality and respect the rights of individuals according to applicable bill of rights; practice universal precautions; assist individuals in exercising their rights.
Support and train staff in implementing Individual Support Plans (i.e.: behavior intervention plans) and conduct classes and orientations as assigned. Attend staff meetings and interdisciplinary team meetings as needed.
Assist with socialization and behavioral development, personal care, housekeeping, recreational activities, transportation, community orientation, shopping, financial management, citizenship, and other activities of daily living as needed.
May accompany individuals to medical appointments; relay instructions and information to and from medical providers as required.
If assigned, accurately administer and document delivery of medications and treatments; promptly report administration errors; maintain appropriate security of controlled medications and other medications and supplies.
If assigned, monitor individual’s health, documenting concerns and communicating with nurse or supervisor as appropriate; follow individual health care directives.
May transport individuals into the community; drive safely and according to local laws; assure proper use of safety equipment including seat belts, lifts, and wheelchair ties; report accidents and safety concerns to appropriate authorities, supervisor, or maintenance personnel immediately.
Check water temperature as required when assisting with bathing; participate in safety drills and protect persons being served in the event of emergency.
Comply with all established safety policies, procedures, and rules; report unsafe hazards to supervisor and participate in safety-related training or activities.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s Degree in a human services field.
Two years of related experience.
Training in behavior modification techniques and/or experience providing behavior management treatment as required by state or program funder.
Knowledge of specialized populations such as individuals with a developmental disability, brain injury, or mental health; expertise in special disciplines such as behavioral support, early intervention, or crisis intervention.
Reliable, responsible, and caring nature with ability to work well with others.
Commitment to the company’s mission and values.
Current driver’s license, car registration and auto insurance if providing transportation for individuals receiving services.
All state-required training and certification completed in mandated timeframes.

Why Join Us?

Full compensation/benefits package for full-time employees.
Salary range: $46,000-$48,000
401(k) with company match.
Paid time off and holiday pay.
Rewarding, hands-on work with plenty of variety – no two days are ever the same!
Make a lasting impact in the lives of individuals!
Enjoy job security with nationwide career development and advancement opportunities.
Employee Referral Program bonus opportunities for eligible roles

We have meaningful work for you – come join our team – Apply Today!
